entries.assertion: Where a Costa Blanca home has built area on the ground that does not appear in the Registro de la Propiedad or the Catastro, what effect does that have on a mortgage valuation, on the buyer's finance and on the notarial deed — and what routes exist to regularise it before a sale?
entries.source_required: Consolidated BOE texts governing appraisal (Orden ECO/805/2003), notarial/registral treatment of obra nueva (art. 28 TRLSRU) and the Valencian planning-legality clock (TRLOTUP).
entries.source_opened: Orden ECO/805/2003 texto consolidado https://www.boe.es/buscar/pdf/2003/BOE-A-2003-7253-consolidado.pdf ; RDLeg 7/2015 TRLSRU texto consolidado https://www.boe.es/buscar/pdf/2015/BOE-A-2015-11723-consolidado.pdf ; Decreto Legislativo 1/2021 TRLOTUP texto consolidado https://www.boe.es/buscar/pdf/2021/DOGV-r-2021-90283-consolidado.pdf
entries.locator: ECO/805/2003 art. 5.1.c) and arts. 10–11 (condicionantes/advertencias); TRLSRU art. 28.1 and 28.4; TRLOTUP art. 255 (plazo de caducidad de 15 años) and art. 255.5 (exceptions).
entries.as_of: ECO/805/2003 última modificación 12-06-2025; TRLSRU última modificación 25-05-2023; TRLOTUP última modificación 02-07-2026
entries.final_wording: Where a Costa Blanca home has built area on the ground that does not appear in the Registro de la Propiedad or the Catastro, what effect does that have on a mortgage valuation, on the buyer's finance and on the notarial deed — and what routes exist to regularise it before a sale?
entries.note: The premise holds and every limb is answerable from primary sources. Short answer the engine should be steered toward: the valuer must use the surface it verifies on site, but adopting a surface more than 5% above the registral/cadastral one (10% for a flat), or valuing a building with no inscribed obra nueva, requires verifying planning compliance first (ECO/805/2003 art. 5.1.c); otherwise it becomes a condicionante or advertencia, which is what kills the buyer's mortgage. Regularisation is by declaración de obra nueva (TRLSRU art. 28.1) or por antigüedad once the 15-year Valencian restoration clock has run (art. 28.4 TRLSRU + art. 255 TRLOTUP).

entries.assertion: Establish what a declaración de obra nueva terminada requires under the current consolidated planning text, and separately what the obra nueva por antigüedad route requires and under what conditions a registrar may refuse it.
entries.source_required: The consolidated BOE text that actually imposes these requirements, identified by name and article.
entries.source_opened: RDLeg 7/2015, Texto Refundido de la Ley de Suelo y Rehabilitación Urbana, texto consolidado https://www.boe.es/buscar/pdf/2015/BOE-A-2015-11723-consolidado.pdf ; Decreto Legislativo 1/2021 (TRLOTUP) texto consolidado https://www.boe.es/buscar/pdf/2021/DOGV-r-2021-90283-consolidado.pdf
entries.locator: TRLSRU art. 28.1 (obra nueva en construcción y terminada), art. 28.2 (deberes del Registrador), art. 28.4.a) (por antigüedad: certificación del Ayuntamiento o técnico competente, acta notarial descriptiva o certificación catastral descriptiva y gráfica, terminación en fecha determinada, descripción coincidente con el título; el Registrador comprueba la inexistencia de anotación preventiva por incoación de expediente de disciplina urbanística y que el suelo no tiene carácter demanial ni está afectado por servidumbres de uso público general); TRLOTUP art. 255.1 (15 años) y 255.5 (excepciones).
entries.as_of: TRLSRU última modificación 25-05-2023; TRLOTUP última modificación 02-07-2026
entries.final_wording: Establish what a declaración de obra nueva terminada requires under art. 28.1 of the consolidated Texto Refundido de la Ley de Suelo y Rehabilitación Urbana (RDLeg 7/2015) — certificación de técnico competente acreditativa de la finalización conforme al proyecto, proof of the requisitos de la legislación de la edificación for handover, and the administrative authorisations (or the acreditación that a comunicación previa / declaración responsable was filed and its period ran) — and separately what the obra nueva por antigüedad route requires under art. 28.4 TRLSRU, together with the grounds on which a Registrador must refuse it: an anotación preventiva for a live expediente de disciplina urbanística, suelo de carácter demanial, or suelo affected by servidumbres de uso público general. There is no single 'planning text': the state gateway is art. 28 TRLSRU, and the Valencian layer that fixes the 15-year restoration-of-legality clock is the TRLOTUP (Decreto Legislativo 1/2021), not Andalusia's AFO.
entries.note: Corrected because 'the current consolidated planning text' is a single-source fiction that invites the engine to pick one text and get it wrong. The requirements sit in state law (art. 28 TRLSRU); the prescription clock that makes the antigüedad route available sits in Valencian law (TRLOTUP art. 255, 15 years, with art. 255.5 exceptions). Naming both, and naming the registrar's three refusal grounds verbatim, removes the guesswork.

entries.assertion: Establish whether and on what basis a mortgage valuer may include square metres that appear on neither the register nor the Catastro — do not infer this from what agents say.
entries.source_required: Orden ECO/805/2003 consolidated, the binding valuation standard for mortgage purposes.
entries.source_opened: Orden ECO/805/2003 texto consolidado https://www.boe.es/buscar/pdf/2003/BOE-A-2003-7253-consolidado.pdf
entries.locator: Art. 5.1: 'se utilizará siempre la superficie comprobada por el tasador'; art. 5.1.a) if it cannot be verified, use the lesser of catastral and registral; art. 5.1.c) 'Cuando la superficie comprobada sea superior en más de un 5% a la registral o a la catastral o cuando se trate de un edificio que carezca de declaración de obra nueva inscrita... su adopción requerirá que se verifique su adecuación a la normativa urbanística aplicable' (10% for elementos de edificios); art. 10.1.e) condicionante; art. 11.a)–b) advertencias.
entries.as_of: Última modificación 12-06-2025
entries.final_wording: Establish whether and on what basis a mortgage valuer may include square metres that appear on neither the register nor the Catastro — do not infer this from what agents say.
entries.note: Answerable and worth answering: yes, the valuer always uses the surface it verifies on site, but adopting an excess above 5% (10% for a flat), or any building with no inscribed obra nueva, is conditional on verifying planning compliance. Fail that and it becomes a condicionante (art. 10) — and art. 9 says a conditioned valuation cannot be used for mortgage purposes at all. That is the mechanism by which unregistered metres break a buyer's finance.

entries.assertion: Establish who initiates and pays for regularisation in the relevant municipality and what documentation the town hall requires, or state plainly that this varies by municipality and must be checked locally.
entries.source_required: Valencian consolidated planning law showing that the procedure is municipally administered and owner-funded, with no uniform state documentation list.
entries.source_opened: Decreto Legislativo 1/2021 (TRLOTUP) texto consolidado https://www.boe.es/buscar/pdf/2021/DOGV-r-2021-90283-consolidado.pdf ; RDLeg 7/2015 TRLSRU texto consolidado https://www.boe.es/buscar/pdf/2015/BOE-A-2015-11723-consolidado.pdf
entries.locator: TRLOTUP art. 190 (servicios urbanísticos, actuaciones de minimización de impactos; obras financed by 'contribuciones especiales... o cuotas de urbanización', approved by 'el pleno municipal'), art. 191 (owner bears conservación/rehabilitación up to the deber normal), arts. 254–255 (alcaldía or Agencia Valenciana de Protección del Territorio requiere a la persona propietaria to apply for the authorisation within two months); TRLSRU art. 28.4.b)–c) (Ayuntamiento notified, must record the situación urbanística by nota marginal).
entries.as_of: TRLOTUP última modificación 02-07-2026; TRLSRU última modificación 25-05-2023
entries.final_wording: Establish who initiates and pays for regularisation in the relevant municipality and what documentation the town hall requires, or state plainly that this varies by municipality and must be checked locally.
entries.note: The fallback clause is the right answer most of the time. State and Valencian law fix who is liable (the owner) and which body acts (alcaldía / Agencia Valenciana de Protección del Territorio), but the documentation list, fees and whether a plan especial de minimización is open are set municipally and are not published in any consolidated text. The engine must not invent a checklist.

entries.assertion: That Catastro area matching the deed means the works were lawfully authorised, or that a Catastro entry regularises anything.
entries.source_required: The consolidated Ley del Catastro Inmobiliario on the Catastro's nature and legal effects.
entries.source_opened: RDLeg 1/2004, Texto Refundido de la Ley del Catastro Inmobiliario, texto consolidado https://www.boe.es/buscar/pdf/2004/BOE-A-2004-4163-consolidado.pdf ; TRLOTUP texto consolidado https://www.boe.es/buscar/pdf/2021/DOGV-r-2021-90283-consolidado.pdf
entries.locator: TRLCI art. 1.1 ('El Catastro Inmobiliario es un registro administrativo dependiente del Ministerio de Hacienda en el que se describen los bienes inmuebles'); art. 2.1 (information 'al servicio de los principios de generalidad y justicia tributaria'); art. 2.2 ('sin perjuicio de las competencias y funciones del Registro de la Propiedad y de los efectos jurídicos sustantivos derivados de la inscripción'); art. 3.3 ('Salvo prueba en contrario y sin perjuicio del Registro de la Propiedad'). TRLOTUP art. 255 keeps the 15-year restoration clock running regardless of cadastral entry.
entries.as_of: TRLCI última modificación 24-12-2022; TRLOTUP última modificación 02-07-2026
entries.final_wording: That Catastro area matching the deed means the works were lawfully authorised, or that a Catastro entry regularises anything.
entries.note: The Catastro is a tax register whose descriptions are rebuttable and expressly without prejudice to the Registro de la Propiedad; nothing in TRLCI confers planning legality. Alignment between deed and Catastro proves only that two descriptions agree. Note also the reverse trap: an unregistered extension is often already in the Catastro, because cadastral declaration is a tax duty owed whether or not the works were licensed.

entries.assertion: Does an officially published administrative reference value apply to residential property in Alicante province in 2026, what instrument created it, which tax bases and which party's taxes does it govern, how is it updated and consulted, and does it have any legal effect on the price a seller and buyer may freely agree?
entries.source_required: BOE consolidated TRLITPAJD art. 10, the TRLCI territorial scope, and the BOE anuncio publishing the reference values for the year in question.
entries.source_opened: TRLITPAJD (RDLeg 1/1993) texto consolidado art. 10 https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1993-25359 ; Anuncio de la Dirección General del Catastro, valores de referencia de los bienes inmuebles urbanos para el ejercicio 2026, BOE-B-2025-46480 https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-B-2025-46480 ; TRLCI texto consolidado art. 1.2 https://www.boe.es/buscar/pdf/2004/BOE-A-2004-4163-consolidado.pdf
entries.locator: TRLITPAJD art. 10: 'En el caso de los bienes inmuebles, su valor será el valor de referencia previsto en la normativa reguladora del catastro inmobiliario, a la fecha de devengo del impuesto' (wording introduced by Ley 11/2021 art. 6.2, in force 11-07-2021; base is the greater of valor de referencia and the declared value/price agreed). BOE-B-2025-46480, BOE núm. 301 of 16-12-2025: values for ejercicio 2026, based on Resolución DGC of 27-10-2025, consultable at sedecatastro.gob.es from 01-01-2026. TRLCI art. 1.2: applies 'en todo el territorio nacional, sin perjuicio de... País Vasco y Navarra'.
entries.as_of: Reference values for ejercicio 2026, announced 16-12-2025, effective from 01-01-2026
entries.final_wording: Does an officially published administrative reference value apply to residential property in Alicante province in 2026, what instrument created it, which tax bases and which party's taxes does it govern, how is it updated and consulted, and does it have any legal effect on the price a seller and buyer may freely agree?
entries.note: TIME-SENSITIVE because the valor de referencia is re-approved and re-announced every year: the 2026 set rests on Resolución DGC 27-10-2025 and BOE-B-2025-46480, and the 2027 set will be announced around December 2026, at which point every figure and the year cited must be replaced. Substantively: yes it applies (Comunitat Valenciana is territorio de régimen común, TRLCI art. 1.2); it is a floor for the taxable base in ITP/AJD, ISD and, for post-2022 acquisitions, Patrimonio — i.e. mainly the BUYER's tax, not the seller's gain, which is still computed on the actual price; and it does not cap or govern the price the parties may agree.

entries.assertion: Over the most recent directly comparable periods, how have registered transaction counts and reported price levels moved in Alicante province, from which instruments, and what — if anything — can an individual owner conclude from that combination about the likely price and time to sell their own home?
entries.source_required: INE's registral transaction series and the registrars' price series for the same province, both opened at source.
entries.source_opened: INE, Estadística de Transmisiones de Derechos de la Propiedad, tabla 6150 'Compraventa de viviendas según régimen y estado', pulled via the INE Tempus API https://servicios.ine.es/wstempus/js/ES/DATOS_TABLA/6150 ; Colegio de Registradores ERI 2T 2026 https://www.registradores.org/documents/d/guest/eri_2t_2026
entries.locator: INE tabla 6150, series 'Alicante/Alacant. General. Compraventa. Número.': H1 2025 = 27.142 (definitivo) vs H1 2026 = 25.085 (provisional), −7,58%. ERI nº 89 p.14 (Alicante 2.267 €/m², 2T2026, +2,4% trimestral, +11,7% interanual) and p.26 (12.298 compraventas, −2,5% trimestral). Extracted 2026-09-02.
entries.as_of: INE through 2026M06 (provisional since July 2025); ERI 2T 2026 published August 2026
entries.final_wording: Over the most recent directly comparable periods, how have registered transaction counts and reported price levels moved in Alicante province, from which instruments, and what — if anything — can an individual owner conclude from that combination about the likely price and time to sell their own home?
entries.note: The question is answerable and the honest answer to its last limb is 'very little'. Volumes down ~7.6% year on year while the province's registered price rose 11.7% year on year is a market-level divergence; neither series is disaggregated to a town, a price band or a property type, and no published series gives time to sell for this province. The 'if anything' hedge is the most important word in the instruction and must survive into the output.

entries.assertion: That a national or city-level time-on-market distribution describes the province or any Costa Blanca town.
entries.source_required: A published time-on-market distribution showing the spread between national, provincial and city figures.
entries.source_opened: idealista/news, 'Ventas exprés: el 7% de las viviendas vendidas en el segundo trimestre no estuvo ni una semana anunciada', 06-08-2026 https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/08/06/909148-ventas-expres-el-7-de-las-viviendas-vendidas-en-el-segundo-trimestre-no-estuvo-ni
entries.locator: Q2 2026 national distribution: 7% under one week, 19% one week–one month, 27% one–three months, 36% three months–one year, 11% over a year. Provincial spread on the same metric: Álava 12% vs Lugo and Ourense 4%. Capital spread: Teruel 21%.
entries.final_wording: That a national or city-level time-on-market distribution describes the province or any Costa Blanca town.
entries.note: The published spread is threefold between the fastest and slowest provinces and up to 21% at capital level against a 7% national figure, so substituting one level for another is quantitatively wrong, not merely imprecise. Add that this distribution counts listings withdrawn from idealista, not completed sales, and no official body publishes an equivalent.

Colegio de Registradores ERI nº 89 p.14, Alicante/Alacant 2T 2026: 2.267 €/m² general, 2.780 nueva, 2.153 usada (registered sale prices). idealista, asking price, Alicante capital July 2026: 2.705 €/m²; España 2.933 €/m².

entries.as_of: MIVAU año 2025; threshold definitional, not period-bound
entries.final_wording: Never assume a province-wide figure describes a town, or that a town-level figure exists — official appraisal data is disaggregated only for larger municipalities, so several Costa Blanca towns have no official town-level price at all

Quote the threshold rather than the vaguer 'larger municipalities'.

entries.assertion: Fewer homes changed hands in Alicante province in the first half of 2026 than a year earlier, while national prices were being reported at record highs.
entries.source_required: INE's provincial registral transaction counts for H1 2026 vs H1 2025, plus a national price release stating a record.
entries.source_opened: INE, ETDP tabla 6150, via the INE Tempus API https://servicios.ine.es/wstempus/js/ES/DATOS_TABLA/6150 ; Colegio de Registradores ERI 2T 2026 (publicación nº 89, agosto 2026) https://www.registradores.org/documents/d/guest/eri_2t_2026

entries.note: Sound, and the 'where published' hedge is doing real work: neither registral instrument publishes below provincia except for the provincial capital, so for almost every Costa Blanca municipality the municipal limb resolves to 'not published'. entries.locator: INE ETDP population defined as 'las inscripciones de transmisiones de derechos de la propiedad en los registros de la propiedad' — the same registral source as the Colegio de Registradores' ERI. Directionally both agree for Alicante (INE H1 2026 −7,58% y/y; ERI 12-month rolling 51.392, −5,3%), but that agreement is near-tautological. The genuinely separate source is notarial: the Consejo General del Notariado's Índice Único Informatizado, surfaced in the Portal Estadístico del Notariado (live 23-10-2025, postcode granularity).
entries.as_of: INE through 2026M06; ERI 2T 2026 (pub. Aug 2026); Notariado portal live since 23-10-2025
entries.final_wording: Establish whether a second instrument built on a genuinely different underlying source agrees on the direction of the volume move for this province and period, and say so if the two disagree. Note that INE's Estadística de Transmisiones de Derechos de la Propiedad and the Colegio de Registradores' Estadística Registral Inmobiliaria are both drawn from the Registros de la Propiedad, so they are not independent of one another and their agreement is not corroboration; an independent cross-check must come from notarial data (Consejo General del Notariado, Índice Único Informatizado / Portal Estadístico del Notariado).
entries.note: Corrected because the instruction as written invites the most natural mistake in this field: pairing INE against the registrars and calling it corroboration. INE's own methodology defines its population as registral inscriptions, the same records the registrars publish. The correction names the one instrument that is genuinely built on a different act (the notarial deed) and is therefore capable of disagreeing.

entries.assertion: And where the seller is a non-resident, the buyer withholds 3% of the price as a payment on account: it is settled against the final liability, so it may be fully refunded, partly refunded, not refunded, or more tax may still be due.
entries.source_required: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25.2 plus the AEAT's own description of the settlement mechanism.
entries.source_opened: RDLeg 5/2004, Texto Refundido de la Ley del Impuesto sobre la Renta de no Residentes, texto consolidado https://www.boe.es/buscar/pdf/2004/BOE-A-2004-4527-consolidado.pdf ; AEAT Sede Electrónica, 'Retención del adquirente de un inmueble' https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/no-residentes/irnr-sin-establecimiento-permanente/retenciones-irnr-sin-establecimiento-permanente/retencion-adquirente-inmueble.html
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 25.2: 'Tratándose de transmisiones de bienes inmuebles situados en territorio español por contribuyentes que actúen sin establecimiento permanente, el adquirente estará obligado a retener e ingresar el 3 por ciento, o a efectuar el ingreso a cuenta correspondiente, de la contraprestación acordada, en concepto de pago a cuenta del impuesto correspondiente a aquéllos.' Art. 25.1.f).3º sets the flat 19% on ganancias patrimoniales from transmisiones de elementos patrimoniales. AEAT: modelo 211 by the buyer; the seller deducts it on modelo 210 and the excess is refundable.
entries.as_of: TRLIRNR texto consolidado, última modificación 25-05-2023
entries.final_wording: And where the seller is a non-resident, the buyer withholds 3% of the price as a payment on account: it is settled against the final liability, so it may be fully refunded, partly refunded, not refunded, or more tax may still be due.
entries.note: Correct as written, including the four-way outcome, which is the part most sources get wrong. Two precisions to hold in reserve: 'non-resident' here means not resident for SPANISH TAX purposes and acting without permanent establishment — nationality, immigration status and country of tax residence are irrelevant to the trigger — and the 3% is on the 'contraprestación acordada', the agreed consideration, not the gain, not the valor catastral and not the valor de referencia. The final liability against which it settles is the flat 19% on the gain (art. 25.1.f).3º).

entries.assertion: Selling your Costa Blanca home as a Spanish non-resident? 3% of the price never reaches you — the buyer is legally required to hand it to Hacienda.
entries.source_required: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25.2 and the AEAT refund mechanism.
entries.source_opened: RDLeg 5/2004 TRLIRNR texto consolidado https://www.boe.es/buscar/pdf/2004/BOE-A-2004-4527-consolidado.pdf ; AEAT Sede Electrónica, 'Retención del adquirente de un inmueble' https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/no-residentes/irnr-sin-establecimiento-permanente/retenciones-irnr-sin-establecimiento-permanente/retencion-adquirente-inmueble.html
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 25.2 ('en concepto de pago a cuenta del impuesto correspondiente a aquéllos'); art. 25.1.f).3º (19% on the gain); AEAT: the buyer pays via modelo 211 within one month of the transmission and gives the seller a copy so the seller can deduct it on modelo 210; the excess over the liability is refundable.
entries.as_of: TRLIRNR texto consolidado, última modificación 25-05-2023
entries.final_wording: Selling your Costa Blanca home while non-resident for Spanish tax purposes? The buyer must hand 3% of the price straight to Hacienda instead of to you — but it is a payment on account of your capital-gains tax, not the tax itself: once you file your modelo 210 you may get all of it back, some of it, or none, and you may still owe more.
entries.note: Corrected on two counts. First, 'never reaches you' is false as a matter of law: art. 25.2 makes it a pago a cuenta, and the AEAT's own page describes the refund route via modelo 210 — the hook as drafted directly contradicts assertion 30 in the same bank. Second, 'a Spanish non-resident' blurs the five variables: the trigger is Spanish TAX residence (acting without permanent establishment), not nationality, not immigration status, not physical presence. An EU or EEA national living in Spain on a valid permit but tax-resident elsewhere is caught; a British national who is Spanish tax-resident is not.

entries.assertion: When a property in Alicante province is sold by a seller who is not a Spanish tax resident, what withholding obligation arises, who is legally obliged to carry it out, what form and deadline apply to it, and by what procedure and timeline can the seller reclaim any amount withheld above the tax actually due?
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLIRNR (RDLeg 5/2004) art. 25.2, its Reglamento (RD 1776/2004) art. 14, and the consolidated Orden approving modelos 210/211
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4527 ; BOE consolidated Reglamento IRNR (RD 1776/2004) — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-14532 ; BOE consolidated Orden EHA/3316/2010 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2010-19707 ; BOE consolidated LGT — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2003-23186
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 25.2 (3% retention by the acquirer, 'en concepto de pago a cuenta'); RD 1776/2004 art. 14.1 (3%), 14.2 (exceptions), 14.3 (declaration + payment within one month of the transmission), 14.4 (non-resident declares definitive tax within three months from the end of that one-month period; Administration refunds the excess), 14.5 (property affected to the payment, marginal note by the Registrar); Orden EHA/3316/2010 art. 5.a) — three months once the one-month period has run, 'con independencia del resultado de la autoliquidación'; LGT art. 31.2 (six months, then automatic interés de demora)
entries.as_of: TRLIRNR consolidation last updated 25/05/2023; RD 1776/2004 consolidation 19/10/2019; Orden EHA/3316/2010 consolidation 23/06/2026; LGT consolidation 21/12/2024
entries.final_wording: When a property in Alicante province is sold by a seller who is not a Spanish tax resident, what withholding obligation arises, who is legally obliged to carry it out, what form and deadline apply to it, and by what procedure and timeline can the seller reclaim any amount withheld above the tax actually due?
entries.note: Every presupposition holds. The trigger is the seller's status as an IRNR taxpayer acting without a permanent establishment — not nationality. Buyer withholds 3% and files modelo 211 within one month of the transmission; seller files modelo 210 (renta type 28) within the following three months, regardless of whether the result is to pay or to refund; AEAT refunds any excess, with interest running automatically after six months. RD 1776/2004 art. 14.2 lists the two cases where no retention is due.

entries.assertion: Establish which statute imposes the withholding on transfers by non-resident sellers, whether the obligation falls on the buyer or the seller, and whether it is characterised as a final tax or a payment on account

entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 25.2: 'el adquirente estará obligado a retener e ingresar el 3 por ciento ... de la contraprestación acordada, en concepto de pago a cuenta del impuesto correspondiente a aquéllos'; RD 1776/2004 art. 14.1 in identical terms

entries.final_wording: Establish which statute imposes the withholding on transfers by non-resident sellers, whether the obligation falls on the buyer or the seller, and whether it is characterised as a final tax or a payment on account
entries.note: Answer on the record: TRLIRNR (RDLeg 5/2004) art. 25.2, developed by RD 1776/2004 art. 14. The obligation falls on the BUYER ('el adquirente'), not the seller. It is expressly a payment on account ('pago a cuenta'), never a final tax — which is why art. 14.4 requires a subsequent settlement and permits a refund.

entries.assertion: For a residential sale in Alicante province, how is the taxable gain computed, and on what basis does the rate applied to that gain differ between a seller who is a Spanish tax resident and one who is not?
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLIRNR arts. 24.4 and 25.1, consolidated LIRPF arts. 34-36, 66 and 76
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4527 ; BOE consolidated LIRPF — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2006-20764 ; AEAT Manual de tributación de no residentes, 'Ganancias patrimoniales derivadas de la venta de inmuebles' — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/ayuda/manuales-videos-folletos/manuales-practicos/manual-tributacion-no-residentes/capitulo-03-tributacion-rentas-comunes-nr/ganancias-patrimoniales/ganancias-patrimoniales-derivadas-venta-inmuebles.html
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 24.4 (gain computed under Section 4ª, Chapter II, Title III LIRPF, excluding art. 33.2); LIRPF arts. 34-36 (transmission value less acquisition value, the latter including improvements, acquisition costs and taxes, less depreciation); resident rate = savings scale, LIRPF art. 66.1 (state half-scale 9.5/10.5/11.5/13.5/15) plus art. 76 (autonomic half-scale, identical), i.e. combined 19/21/23/27/30; non-resident rate = TRLIRNR art. 25.1.f).3º, flat 19%; AEAT manual: 'El tipo de gravamen aplicable es el 19%'
entries.as_of: LIRPF consolidation 02/09/2026 (art. 66 as amended by Ley 7/2024, effects 01/01/2025); TRLIRNR consolidation 25/05/2023; AEAT manual page last updated 01/07/2026
entries.final_wording: For a residential sale in Alicante province, how is the taxable gain computed, and on what basis does the rate applied to that gain differ between a seller who is a Spanish tax resident and one who is not?
entries.note: The gain is computed the same way for both. What differs is the rate structure: the resident's gain enters the progressive savings base (19% to 30%), while the non-resident's is taxed at a flat 19%. The difference therefore turns on the seller's Spanish TAX RESIDENCE, not on nationality or immigration status.

entries.assertion: Establish the rate structure applied to a property gain for a Spanish tax resident, and separately the rate applied to a non-resident, and establish whether either is progressive or flat
entries.source_required: Consolidated LIRPF arts. 66 and 76; consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25.1.f)

entries.locator: LIRPF art. 66.1.1º and art. 76.1º, savings-base scales, each 9.5 / 10.5 / 11.5 / 13.5 / 15 at 6.000 / 50.000 / 200.000 / 300.000 € thresholds, summing to 19 / 21 / 23 / 27 / 30 — progressive. TRLIRNR art. 25.1.f).3º: 'El 19 por ciento cuando se trate de ... 3.º Ganancias patrimoniales que se pongan de manifiesto con ocasión de transmisiones de elementos patrimoniales' — flat

entries.note: Answer on the record: resident = progressive savings scale, five brackets, 19% to 30% (top bracket bites above €300,000 of savings base). entries.assertion: Establish whether the non-resident rate on a property-transfer gain differs by the seller's country of residence, and separately establish whether any other IRNR rate that varies by country of residence applies to a different income type and is being confused with this one
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25.1.a) and 25.1.f), plus AEAT's own statement of the rate
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4527 ; AEAT Manual de tributación de no residentes — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/ayuda/manuales-videos-folletos/manuales-practicos/manual-tributacion-no-residentes/capitulo-03-tributacion-rentas-comunes-nr/ganancias-patrimoniales/ganancias-patrimoniales-derivadas-venta-inmuebles.html
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 25.1.f).3º — flat 19% on gains from transfers of assets, with no residence condition attached. TRLIRNR art. 25.1.a) — 24% general, reduced to 19% only for taxpayers resident in an EU or EEA state with an effective exchange of tax information under DA 1ª.4 of Ley 36/2006; this is the rate that varies, and it governs the income of art. 24 generally (notably rental income and the art. 24.5 imputed income of urban property), not transfer gains. AEAT manual: 'El tipo de gravamen aplicable es el 19%'
entries.as_of: TRLIRNR consolidation 25/05/2023; AEAT manual page last updated 01/07/2026
entries.final_wording: Establish whether the non-resident rate on a property-transfer gain differs by the seller's country of residence, and separately establish whether any other IRNR rate that varies by country of residence applies to a different income type and is being confused with this one
entries.note: Both halves answered. (1) No — art. 25.1.f).3º is a single flat 19% for every non-resident, wherever resident. (2) Yes — the 24%/19% split in art. 25.1.a) is precisely the rate being confused with it, and it belongs to imputed and rental income. A live worked example of the confusion appeared in my own search results, where a summary asserted '19% for residents in the EU, Iceland and Norway, and 24% for the rest of countries' about a property gain. That is wrong and is the exact error this instruction exists to prevent.

entries.note: Answer on the record, and it is asymmetric — which is why the instruction must not be answered with a single yes or no. For a Spanish tax RESIDENT: yes, Ley 7/2024, de 20 de diciembre, DF 7.1 and 7.2, with effect from 1 January 2025, added a 30% top savings bracket above €300,000. For a NON-RESIDENT: no, the flat 19% of TRLIRNR art. 25.1.f).3º is unchanged since 2010. Separately, the plusvalía coefficient ceilings were re-set for 2025 and again for 2026 and both re-settings were annulled by Congress — see entry 45.

entries.assertion: That an EEA citizen and an EU citizen and a third-country national face different rates on this gain until it is established one way or the other — and never file a nationality under an immigration or tax category as shorthand
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25.1.f) and art. 25.1.a); LIRPF art. 9
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4527 ; BOE consolidated LIRPF — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2006-20764
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 25.1.f).3º (flat 19%, no residence or nationality condition); art. 25.1.a) (the only residence-conditioned rate, and it is drafted by reference to the state of RESIDENCE, 'contribuyentes residentes en otro Estado miembro de la Unión Europea o del Espacio Económico Europeo', never to citizenship); LIRPF art. 9.1
entries.as_of: TRLIRNR consolidation 25/05/2023; LIRPF consolidation 02/09/2026
entries.final_wording: That an EEA citizen and an EU citizen and a third-country national face different rates on this gain until it is established one way or the other — and never file a nationality under an immigration or tax category as shorthand
entries.note: The never-rule is sound and can now be closed out: they do NOT face different rates on this gain — it is a flat 19% for all. And the second half is confirmed structurally: every residence-sensitive provision in TRLIRNR is drafted by state of residence, not citizenship, so a nationality can never be filed under a tax category as shorthand. Note also that EU/EEA status is relevant elsewhere in this block (the DA 7ª reinvestment relief) — so 'it makes no difference' is only true of the rate.

entries.assertion: The town-hall tax on your sale is calculated two different ways, and you are allowed to pick the one that costs less — plus one twist that only applies when the seller is a non-resident individual
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLRHL (RDLeg 2/2004) arts. 104.5, 106.2 and 107.5
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLRHL — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4214
entries.locator: TRLRHL art. 107.1-107.4 (objective method: cadastral land value × municipal coefficient by period of generation); art. 107.5 ('Cuando, a instancia del sujeto pasivo, conforme al procedimiento establecido en el artículo 104.5, se constate que el importe del incremento de valor es inferior al importe de la base imponible determinada con arreglo a lo dispuesto en los apartados anteriores ... se tomará como base imponible el importe de dicho incremento'); art. 104.5 (no subjection where no increase is shown, with the comparison rules); art. 106.2 (buyer becomes sustituto del contribuyente where the seller is a 'persona física no residente en España')
entries.as_of: TRLRHL consolidation 03/06/2026
entries.final_wording: The town-hall tax on your sale can be worked out two ways, and if the real increase in the land's value is lower than the objective calculation you can ask for that lower figure to be used instead — plus one twist that only applies when the seller is an individual living outside Spain.
entries.note: Corrected because 'you are allowed to pick the one that costs less' overstates the mechanism in a way that will generate wrong advice. The objective method applies by default. The real-gain figure applies only 'a instancia del sujeto pasivo' and only where it is proven LOWER, on the art. 104.5 evidence rules (deed values or checked values, land/building split by cadastral proportion). It is a right to prove and substitute, not a free choice at the counter. The 'twist' is accurate and is art. 106.2 — but see entry 47: it is not a benefit to the seller.

entries.assertion: How is plusvalía municipal calculated on a residential sale in Alicante province, what choice if any does the taxpayer have between calculation methods, who is the taxpayer on an ordinary sale, and does that change when the seller is an individual living outside Spain?
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLRHL arts. 104-108
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLRHL — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4214
entries.locator: TRLRHL art. 104.5; art. 106.1.b) (on an onerous transfer the contribuyente is the transferor); art. 106.2 (sustituto = the acquirer, where the contribuyente is a non-resident individual); art. 107.1-107.5; art. 108.1 (rate fixed by each ayuntamiento, ceiling 30%)
entries.as_of: TRLRHL consolidation 03/06/2026
entries.final_wording: How is plusvalía municipal calculated on a residential sale in Alicante province, what choice if any does the taxpayer have between calculation methods, who is the taxpayer on an ordinary sale, and does that change when the seller is an individual living outside Spain?
entries.note: The question's framing is sound and its four limbs are all answerable from TRLRHL alone. The phrasing 'an individual living outside Spain' is better than 'a foreign seller', and it tracks the statute, which says 'persona física no residente en España'. Two cautions for whatever is written from it: the shift in art. 106.2 applies only to individuals, not to non-resident companies; and the answer to 'how is it calculated' cannot end in a number, because both the coefficient and the rate are municipal (see entries 45 and 46).

entries.assertion: Establish how far the coefficients and the rate vary between individual municipalities in Alicante province, what statutory ceiling constrains them, and therefore whether any single quoted amount can be presented as a Costa Blanca figure
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLRHL arts. 107.4 and 108.1 for the ceilings, plus the ordenanzas fiscales of several individual Alicante-province municipalities for the actual spread
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLRHL — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4214 ; Ayuntamiento de Alicante, Ordenanza fiscal del IIVTNU — https://www.alicante.es/sites/default/files/documentos/normativa-municipal/impuesto-incremento-del-valor-terrenos-naturaleza-urbana/ivtnu.pdf
entries.locator: TRLRHL art. 107.4: the coefficient is 'el que corresponda de los aprobados por el ayuntamiento', capped by the statutory table, and 'Estos coeficientes máximos serán actualizados anualmente mediante norma con rango legal'; art. 108.1: 'El tipo de gravamen del impuesto será el fijado por cada ayuntamiento, sin que dicho tipo pueda exceder del 30 por ciento', and the ayuntamiento may set one rate or one per period. Alicante city ordinance, art. 13: rate 30%
entries.as_of: TRLRHL consolidation 03/06/2026; Alicante city ordinance file dated 2016 (pre-RDL 26/2021 drafting, still the version published on the municipal site)
entries.final_wording: Establish the statutory ceilings that constrain plusvalía municipal (TRLRHL art. 107.4 for the coefficients, art. 108.1 for the rate, capped at 30%), confirm from the ordenanza fiscal of each specific municipality what that town hall has actually set, and treat any single quoted amount as a fact about one town only. Do not state a province-wide spread without having opened the ordinances it is drawn from.
entries.note: Corrected on two counts. First, the instruction as written invites a claim about 'how far' figures vary across Alicante province, and I could not establish that spread: I opened only one municipal ordinance (Alicante city, art. 13, 30% — i.e. at the statutory ceiling). Secondary sources put coastal municipalities in a 26-30% band but that is a blog claim, not proof. Second, and more important, the coefficient ceilings are unstable in a way no content should ignore: TRLRHL art. 107.4 records that the increases enacted by RDL 9/2024 (effects 01/01/2025) and by RDL 16/2025 (effects 01/01/2026) were each left without effect when Congress voted the decree down — Resolución of 22/01/2025 (BOE-A-2025-1136) and Resolución of 27/01/2026 (BOE-A-2026-2024). Reporting the '2026 updated coefficients' as being in force would be an error, and at least one property-press source consulted does exactly that.

entries.assertion: That a figure or rate from one Alicante-province municipality applies to any other — each town hall sets its own within legal maxima, so a number is a fact about one town, never about the coast
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLRHL arts. 107.4 and 108.1
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLRHL — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4214
entries.locator: TRLRHL art. 107.4 (coefficients 'aprobados por el ayuntamiento', within the statutory maxima table); art. 108.1 (rate 'fijado por cada ayuntamiento', ceiling 30%, and the ayuntamiento may fix a single rate or one per period of generation); art. 107.2.a) final paragraph (an optional municipal reducing coefficient of up to 15% on the land value); art. 107.3 (optional municipal reduction of up to 60% after a general revaluation); art. 108.4-108.5 (optional municipal bonificaciones of up to 95%)
entries.as_of: TRLRHL consolidation 03/06/2026
entries.final_wording: That a figure or rate from one Alicante-province municipality applies to any other — each town hall sets its own within legal maxima, so a number is a fact about one town, never about the coast
entries.note: Verified, and the statute supports it more strongly than the wording claims: it is not only the rate and the coefficients that are municipal. The 15% land-value reducer, the post-revaluation reduction of up to 60%, and bonificaciones of up to 95% are all optional and set town by town. Two neighbouring Alicante municipalities can therefore differ by a multiple, not a margin.

entries.assertion: That the shift of liability for a non-resident seller is a benefit to that seller — establish what it means in practice at completion, including whether the counterparty recovers the amount from the sale proceeds
entries.source_required: Consolidated LGT art. 36.3 (the sustituto's right of recovery) read with TRLRHL art. 106.2
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated LGT (Ley 58/2003) — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2003-23186 ; BOE consolidated TRLRHL — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4214
entries.locator: LGT art. 36.3: 'Es sustituto el sujeto pasivo que, por imposición de la ley y en lugar del contribuyente, está obligado a cumplir la obligación tributaria principal ... El sustituto podrá exigir del contribuyente el importe de las obligaciones tributarias satisfechas, salvo que la ley señale otra cosa.' TRLRHL art. 106.2 contains no such contrary provision
entries.as_of: LGT consolidation 21/12/2024; TRLRHL consolidation 03/06/2026
entries.final_wording: That the shift of liability for a non-resident seller is a benefit to that seller — establish what it means in practice at completion, including whether the counterparty recovers the amount from the sale proceeds
entries.note: The never-rule is correct and now has a statutory basis rather than an intuition. LGT art. 36.3 expressly entitles the sustituto to demand the amount back from the contribuyente, and TRLRHL art. 106.2 does not displace that. So the shift moves the FILING and the risk of non-payment to the buyer, not the cost. One honest limit: whether the buyer actually retains it from the price at completion is a matter of contract and conveyancing practice, not statute — statute gives the right of recovery, it does not prescribe a retention. Say 'the buyer is entitled to recover it from the seller, and in practice normally retains it from the price', not 'the law makes the buyer pay it'.

entries.note: Verified word for word: DA 7ª uses 'residentes en un Estado miembro', never 'nacionales'. And the EU/EEA distinction is real and asymmetric — EU residence qualifies outright, while EEA residence qualifies only where there is an effective exchange of tax information. Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein reach this relief through DA 7ª.4, not DA 7ª.1, so 'EU/EEA' as a single bracket is a simplification the drafting does not support. A Norwegian citizen tax-resident in Dubai does not qualify; a British citizen tax-resident in Ireland does.

entries.assertion: Does a private homeowner who signs a marketing mandate with an estate agent in Spain have any right to withdraw from it afterwards, what determines whether that right exists and how long it lasts, and what — if anything — must an agent operating in the Comunitat Valenciana state in that document about their own registration?
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLGDCU (RDLeg 1/2007) Título III arts. 92, 102-105; Decreto 98/2022 del Consell
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLGDCU — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-20555 ; DOGV, Decreto 98/2022, de 29 de julio, del Consell — https://dogv.gva.es/datos/2022/08/16/pdf/2022_7560.pdf
entries.locator: TRLGDCU art. 92.1-92.2 (Title III applies to distance contracts and to contracts concluded away from business premises, including one signed at the agency immediately after personal contact elsewhere); art. 102.1 (14 calendar days, extended to 30 where the contract follows an unsolicited visit to the consumer's home); art. 102.2 (waiver or penalty clauses void); art. 104.a) (for service contracts the period runs from the day the contract is concluded); art. 105.1 (period extended by 12 months if the trader did not give the withdrawal information). Decreto 98/2022 art. 3.a), final paragraph: the agent must state professional identification, location, insurer/financial entity, guarantee reference number and 'número de inscripción en el registro de agentes de intermediación inmobiliaria en el contrato de mandato o nota de encargo que suscriba con sus clientes'
entries.as_of: TRLGDCU consolidation 28/02/2026; Decreto 98/2022 published DOGV 9405 of 16/08/2022
entries.final_wording: Does a private homeowner who signs a marketing mandate with an estate agent in Spain have any right to withdraw from it afterwards, what determines whether that right exists and how long it lasts, and what — if anything — must an agent operating in the Comunitat Valenciana state in that document about their own registration?
entries.note: The question is correctly framed and, importantly, does not presuppose that the right always exists — which is the trap. There is no general Spanish right to withdraw from an estate-agency mandate. It arises only where the homeowner contracts as a consumer AND the contract was concluded at a distance or away from the agency's premises: 14 calendar days, 30 if it followed an unsolicited home visit, and up to 12 months and 14 days if the agent never disclosed the right. A mandate signed at the agency's own office, on the homeowner's initiative, carries no statutory withdrawal right at all. On the second limb, Decreto 98/2022 art. 3.a) is explicit that the registration number must appear in the mandate or nota de encargo itself.

entries.final_wording: Establish whether estate agency in the Comunitat Valenciana is subject to a register, whether entry is obligatory or voluntary, when that obligation began, what the agent must consequently include in the mandate, and whether a homeowner can verify an agent's entry themselves — and by what search route.
entries.note: All five limbs answered from the decree itself. Register exists; entry is obligatory and free; in force 16 October 2022 (two months after DOGV publication on 16 August 2022); the agent must carry the registration number in the mandate or nota de encargo, and display the plaque described in the Anexo único; and the register is public and consultable through the Generalitat's own procedure page 22848, which links a public consultation form. Two cautions: art. 2 excludes some actors (notably non-habitual, unremunerated intermediation, and agents established outside the Comunitat, who instead must notify), so 'every agent must be registered' is too broad; and I confirmed the decree is still cited as current by the Generalitat but did not open a consolidated Valencian text, so treat 'unamended since 2022' as unverified.

entries.note: The question's central distinction is real and the deed-blocking document is identifiable: the community-debt certificate under LPH art. 9.1.e) is the one whose absence means the notary cannot authorise the deed — unless the buyer expressly waives it, which is common and which must be stated alongside the rule or the rule becomes misleading. It is the transmitente who must produce it, and the community must issue it within seven calendar days. By contrast the Valencian second-occupancy declaration is a duty owed to the town hall (Decreto 12/2021 arts. 6 and 8), not a notarial bar — see entry 56. Honest gap: I did not open RD 390/2021, so the energy-certificate leg of any answer built on this question is not sourced here and must be verified separately before publication.

GVA arquitectura page: 'se mantiene vigente la Orden de 7 de diciembre de 2009' and 'En virtud de la Disposición derogatoria única de la Ley 5/2025, de 30 de mayo ... queda derogado el Decreto 80/2023'. Decreto 12/2021, Anexo, Ficha 1.3 'EDIFICIOS NUEVA PLANTA CONFORME DC-09 — edificio construido o con licencia solicitada desde 7/04/2010'; Ficha 1.2 'CONFORME HD-91 — desde 23/09/1989 hasta 6/04/2010'; Ficha 1.1 'EDIFICIOS EXISTENTES CONFORME HD-91 — antes de 23/09/1989'

entries.final_wording: Separately establish that the habitability standard the declaration is measured against changed: Decreto 80/2023 (DC-23) was repealed by letra g of the disposición derogatoria única of Ley 5/2025, de 30 de mayo, and the Generalitat states that the Orden de 7 de diciembre de 2009 (DC-09) remains in force. Under the fichas annexed to Decreto 12/2021, DC-09 is the standard for buildings built or with a licence applied for from 7 April 2010 onwards, and HD-91 for everything before that, split into a pre-23 September 1989 existing-buildings ficha and a 23 September 1989 to 6 April 2010 new-build ficha.
entries.note: Substance holds; three corrections. (1) It is letra g) of the disposición derogatoria única, not letra e) — a widely repeated secondary-source error I traced to the professional-press summaries and rejected against the BOE text. (2) 'Recovered vigency' is the wrong verb and is legally loaded: Código Civil art. 2.2 provides that repealing a repealing law does not itself revive what it repealed, and Ley 5/2025 contains no revival clause. The Generalitat's own page says the Orden 'se mantiene vigente'. Use the Generalitat's wording, which is both safer and better sourced. (3) 'HD-91 to earlier ones' is right but flattens two distinct fichas with different content — pre-1989 existing buildings and 1989-2010 new build — which matters to whoever has to certify the dwelling. The date band is 'from 7 April 2010', inclusive, not 'postdates'.

entries.source_opened: DOGV, Decreto 12/2021, de 22 de enero, del Consell — https://dogv.gva.es/datos/2021/02/03/pdf/2021_924.pdf ; BOE consolidated Ley de Propiedad Horizontal, opened for contrast as the one document that does bar authorisation — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1960-10906
entries.locator: Decreto 12/2021 art. 6.1: the declaración responsable must be renewed 10 years after first occupation 'cada vez que se produzca la segunda o posteriores transmisiones de la propiedad' or when a new water, gas or electricity supply contract must be formalised; art. 8.1: owners must lodge it with the AYUNTAMIENTO 'con carácter previo a la ocupación'; art. 6.2 (technical certificate that the building still meets the conditions of the earlier title); art. 7 (buildings with no prior occupation title). Nothing in arts. 1-13 or the disposiciones conditions the authorisation of a public deed. Contrast LPH art. 9.1.e), which does: 'sin la cual no podrá autorizarse el otorgamiento del documento público'
entries.as_of: Decreto 12/2021 as published DOGV 03/02/2021, checked for the position in 2026; no successor decree located in force (see entry 54)
entries.final_wording: Establish, and record the answer: no primary Generalitat text requires the second-occupancy declaration as a condition of authorising the deed. Decreto 12/2021 arts. 6.1 and 8.1 make it a duty owed by the owner to the ayuntamiento, triggered by a second or later transfer of ownership or by a new utility contract once ten years have passed since first occupation, and lodged before occupation. Do not present it as a document without which the sale cannot complete.
entries.note: Corrected from an open instruction into a recorded finding, because the phrasing 'requires it at the deed' invites a false yes and this is a claim buyers and sellers act on. The obligation is real, its trigger does include the transfer of ownership, and skipping it exposes the parties — but it is administrative and municipal, and the notary is not the gate. The single Spanish document that genuinely blocks authorisation of a resale deed is the community-debt certificate under LPH art. 9.1.e), and even that can be waived by the buyer. Note also that individual ayuntamientos may impose local requirements of their own, which I did not check.

entries.assertion: On a residential sale in Alicante province, which amounts leave the seller permanently, which reduce the figure the seller is taxed on, and which are withheld at completion but later recoverable — and what does each of those outcomes depend on?
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLRHL arts. 104-108 (the permanent municipal charge), consolidated LIRPF arts. 35-36 via TRLIRNR art. 24.4 (base-reducing costs), consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25.2 and RD 1776/2004 art. 14.4 (the recoverable retention)
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLRHL — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4214 ; BOE consolidated TRLIRNR — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4527 ; BOE consolidated RD 1776/2004 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-14532 ; BOE consolidated LIRPF — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2006-20764
entries.locator: Permanent: TRLRHL arts. 104-108 (plusvalía municipal, subject to the art. 104.5 non-subjection route). Base-reducing: TRLIRNR art. 24.4 importing LIRPF arts. 34-36 — acquisition value including improvements, acquisition costs and taxes; transmission value net of costs and taxes borne by the transferor. Withheld but recoverable: TRLIRNR art. 25.2 and RD 1776/2004 art. 14.4 ('la devolución al contribuyente del exceso retenido o ingresado a cuenta'), with LGT art. 31.2 setting the six-month clock
entries.as_of: TRLRHL consolidation 03/06/2026; TRLIRNR consolidation 25/05/2023; RD 1776/2004 consolidation 19/10/2019; LIRPF consolidation 02/09/2026
entries.final_wording: On a residential sale in Alicante province, which amounts leave the seller permanently, which reduce the figure the seller is taxed on, and which are withheld at completion but later recoverable — and what does each of those outcomes depend on?
entries.note: The three-bucket framing is sound and maps onto three different bodies of law, which is exactly why it is worth keeping separate. One caution for anything written from it: the 3% is the only genuinely recoverable item, and it is recoverable only to the extent it exceeds 19% of the actual gain — if the gain is large the 3% is not a deposit at all, it is a part-payment and more will be due. Do not let 'recoverable' imply 'you get it back'.

entries.assertion: Establish who the taxpayer is for the municipal land-value tax on a sale, whether a different rule applies where the seller does not live in Spain, whether more than one calculation method exists and who chooses, and whether the bill varies between municipalities in the province.
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLRHL arts. 104.5, 106, 107 and 108
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLRHL — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4214
entries.locator: art. 106.1.b) (transferor is contribuyente on an onerous transfer); art. 106.2 (acquirer is sustituto where the contribuyente is a non-resident individual); art. 107.1-107.4 (objective method, municipal coefficients within statutory maxima) and art. 107.5 with art. 104.5 (real-increase method, at the taxpayer's instance, applied where lower; no subjection where there is no increase); art. 108.1 (municipal rate, ceiling 30%)
entries.as_of: TRLRHL consolidation 03/06/2026
entries.final_wording: Establish who the taxpayer is for the municipal land-value tax on a sale, whether a different rule applies where the seller does not live in Spain, whether more than one calculation method exists and who chooses, and whether the bill varies between municipalities in the province.
entries.note: All four limbs answerable from TRLRHL alone and all four confirmed. Note the precision needed on the third limb: the taxpayer does not 'choose' between two methods freely — the objective method is the default and the taxpayer may request the real-increase figure, which is applied only if it is lower and only on the art. 104.5 evidence. And on the second limb the statutory phrase is 'persona física no residente en España' — residence, and individuals only.

entries.assertion: Do not infer a seller's tax residence from their passport, and do not treat all non-resident sellers as a single category.
entries.source_required: Consolidated LIRPF art. 9; consolidated TRLIRNR arts. 25.1.a) and DA 7ª; consolidated TRLRHL art. 106.2

entries.locator: LIRPF art. 9.1.a)-b) (183 days; centre of economic interests — no nationality test). Sub-categories that genuinely diverge: TRLIRNR DA 7ª.1 vs DA 7ª.4 (EU residence vs EEA residence with effective exchange of information) for the reinvestment relief; TRLIRNR art. 25.1.a) (24% vs 19% by state of residence) for other income; TRLRHL art. 106.2 (liability shifts only where the non-resident seller is an individual)

entries.final_wording: Do not infer a seller's tax residence from their passport, and do not treat all non-resident sellers as a single category.
entries.note: Both halves verified, and the second half has teeth: non-resident sellers split at least three ways in this material — EU-resident versus EEA-with-exchange versus third-country (reinvestment relief), individual versus entity (plusvalía substitution), and by state of residence for non-transfer income. What does NOT vary between them is the 19% rate on the property gain itself.

entries.assertion: Sell as a non-resident and 3% of the agreed price never reaches your account on signing day.
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25.2 and RD 1776/2004 art. 14
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4527 ; BOE consolidated RD 1776/2004 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-14532 ; AEAT, 'Retención del adquirente de un inmueble' — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/no-residentes/irnr-sin-establecimiento-permanente/retenciones-irnr-sin-establecimiento-permanente/retencion-adquirente-inmueble.html
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 25.2 — 3% 'de la contraprestación acordada'; RD 1776/2004 art. 14.1 (same) and art. 14.2 (no retention where the transferor evidences subjection to IRPF or Impuesto sobre Sociedades by certificate, or on contributions of property to the capital of Spanish-resident companies), art. 14.3 (paid over within one month); AEAT: 'El adquirente de un inmueble propiedad de un no residente debe retener e ingresar el 3%' via modelo 211
entries.as_of: TRLIRNR consolidation 25/05/2023; RD 1776/2004 consolidation 19/10/2019; AEAT page last updated 26/09/2024
entries.final_wording: Sell as a non-resident and 3% of the agreed price never reaches your account on signing day.
entries.note: Accurate as a hook. Three things to hold behind it so the body copy does not overreach: it is 3% of the agreed consideration, not of the gain or of the cadastral value; 'non-resident' here means an IRNR taxpayer acting without a permanent establishment, defined by tax residence and not by passport; and RD 1776/2004 art. 14.2 carves out the case where the transferor certifies subjection to IRPF or corporation tax, which is definitionally not this seller. The hook must not be allowed to imply the 3% is the tax — it is a payment on account, and the final bill is 19% of the actual gain.

entries.assertion: When a seller taxed as a non-resident completes a residential sale in Spain, what happens to the retained portion of the price — under whose legal obligation, through which filings, and on what deadlines — and what determines how much of it, if any, returns to the seller?
entries.source_required: Consolidated RD 1776/2004 art. 14; consolidated Orden EHA/3316/2010 art. 5; consolidated LGT art. 31
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated RD 1776/2004 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-14532 ; BOE consolidated Orden EHA/3316/2010 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2010-19707 ; Orden HAC/623/2026 — https://www.boe.es/boe/dias/2026/06/23/pdfs/BOE-A-2026-13573.pdf ; BOE consolidated LGT — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2003-23186
entries.locator: RD 1776/2004 art. 14.3 (buyer files and pays within one month of the transmission, at the Delegación or Administración of the AEAT covering the property's location) and art. 14.4 (seller declares the definitive tax, offsetting the amount withheld, within three months from the end of that one-month period; Administration refunds the excess after such checks as are needed). Orden EHA/3316/2010 art. 5.a), as reproduced by Orden HAC/623/2026 art. primero.dos: same window 'con independencia del resultado de la autoliquidación'; art. 13.6 excludes renta type 28 from direct debit. LGT art. 31.2 (six months, then interés de demora without need to request it)
entries.as_of: RD 1776/2004 consolidation 19/10/2019; Orden EHA/3316/2010 consolidation 23/06/2026; LGT consolidation 21/12/2024
entries.final_wording: When a seller taxed as a non-resident completes a residential sale in Spain, what happens to the retained portion of the price — under whose legal obligation, through which filings, and on what deadlines — and what determines how much of it, if any, returns to the seller?
entries.note: Fully answerable and every limb sourced. Filings: modelo 211 by the buyer within one month; modelo 210, renta type 28, by the seller within the three months following that month — a window that applies whether the result is to pay or to refund, so the general 'refunds may be filed from 1 February and within four years' rule in art. 5.c).3º does NOT apply to a property transfer. That distinction was mis-stated in the secondary sources I sampled. How much comes back is determined by 19% of the actual gain measured against the 3% already paid; if the gain is nil or negative the whole 3% is reclaimable. Timing of the refund is governed by LGT art. 31.2, not by any IRNR-specific promise: six months, after which interest accrues automatically. Do not publish a shorter expectation.

entries.assertion: Establish how the final liability on the gain is computed for a person taxed as a non-resident, and whether that computation differs from the one applied to a Spanish tax resident
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLIRNR arts. 24.4 and 25.1.f); consolidated LIRPF arts. 34-36, 66, 76, 33.4.b) and 38
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4527 ; BOE consolidated LIRPF — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2006-20764 ; AEAT Manual de tributación de no residentes — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/ayuda/manuales-videos-folletos/manuales-practicos/manual-tributacion-no-residentes/capitulo-03-tributacion-rentas-comunes-nr/ganancias-patrimoniales/ganancias-patrimoniales-derivadas-venta-inmuebles.html
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 24.4 (the gain is computed under Section 4ª of Chapter II of Title III LIRPF, excluding art. 33.2, and Section 6ª of Title X excluding art. 94.1.a) second paragraph); art. 24.6.2ª (special rules for EU-resident taxpayers); art. 25.1.f).3º (flat 19%). Resident side: LIRPF arts. 34-36 for the same computation, arts. 66.1 and 76 for the progressive savings scale, art. 33.4.b) and art. 38 for reliefs. Non-resident reliefs: TRLIRNR art. 14 and DA 7ª only
entries.as_of: TRLIRNR consolidation 25/05/2023; LIRPF consolidation 02/09/2026; AEAT manual page last updated 01/07/2026
entries.final_wording: Establish how the final liability on the gain is computed for a person taxed as a non-resident, and whether that computation differs from the one applied to a Spanish tax resident
entries.note: Answer on the record, and it is a two-part answer that is often given as one. The GAIN is computed the same way for both — transmission value less acquisition value, with acquisition costs, taxes and improvements, under the same LIRPF articles, because TRLIRNR art. 24.4 imports them. What differs is (a) the rate — flat 19% versus the progressive 19-30% savings scale — and (b) the reliefs reachable: a resident can reach LIRPF art. 33.4.b) (over 65, habitual residence) and art. 38, while a non-resident has only the closed list in TRLIRNR art. 14 and the DA 7ª reinvestment exclusion, itself confined to EU residents and EEA residents with effective exchange of tax information.

entries.note: Verified on both a primary and an administrative source, and this is the single most load-bearing never-rule in the block. The 19% in art. 25.1.f).3º carries no residence condition, unlike the 19% in art. 25.1.a), which is conditional on EU/EEA residence with effective exchange of information and applies to other income. During this pass a search summary reproduced the error verbatim — '19% for residents in the EU, Iceland and Norway, and 24% for the rest of countries' — applied to a property gain, which shows the contamination is live in the sources the engine will be reading. Rate unchanged since 1 January 2010; no 2025 or 2026 amendment.

entries.assertion: That tax residence follows the passport, or that a foreign seller with a Spanish NIE, a padrón entry or a Spanish bank account is therefore a resident
entries.source_required: Consolidated LIRPF (Ley 35/2006) art. 9, the statutory test for habitual residence in Spanish territory
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated text of Ley 35/2006 (LIRPF), art. 9, via the BOE legislación-consolidada open-data API — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2006-20764/texto/bloque/a9
entries.locator: LIRPF art. 9.1: residence is established by (a) staying more than 183 days in Spanish territory during the calendar year, counting sporadic absences unless fiscal residence elsewhere is evidenced, or (b) having in Spain the main nucleus or base of activities or economic interests, directly or indirectly; plus a rebuttable presumption from the residence of a non-legally-separated spouse and dependent minor children. Single version, in force since 1 January 2007 — never amended.
entries.as_of: Consolidated text current to 1 January 2007 (original and only version); read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: That tax residence follows the passport, or that a foreign seller with a Spanish NIE, a padrón entry or a Spanish bank account is therefore a resident
entries.note: Art. 9.1 contains two tests and one presumption. Nationality appears nowhere in it. Neither does a NIE, a padrón entry or a bank account: none is a statutory criterion. A padrón entry can be evidence feeding the 183-day count, but it is evidence, not the test, and it is regularly held by people who are plainly non-resident. The instruction is sound as written.

entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 24.4 (gains: base determined 'aplicando... las normas previstas en la Sección 4.ª del Capítulo II del Título III... de la Ley 35/2006', i.e. the same acquisition/transmission value rules as for residents); art. 24.6.1.ª (expense deduction against rendimientos available only to residents of another EU Member State, extended to EEA states with effective exchange of information); DA 7ª (main-home reinvestment exemption available to EU residents, extended to qualifying EEA residents). Art. 24 last amended by Ley 26/2014 art. 2.5, in force 1 January 2015.
entries.as_of: Consolidated text current to 1 January 2015 (art. 24); read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: That the deductible list is the same for a seller taxed as a resident and one taxed as a non-resident until that has been checked
entries.note: The caution is right, and the check produces a split answer worth carrying into the copy. For the gain itself, art. 24.4 sends you to the same LIRPF rules a resident uses, so the cost items that build acquisition and transmission value are the same. What is not the same: expense deduction against rental income (art. 24.6, EU/EEA only) and the main-home reinvestment exemption (DA 7ª, EU/EEA only — so a Norwegian owner qualifies and a Swiss or British one does not). Writers conflate these three regularly.

entries.assertion: Establish what the law provides where there has been no increase in value between acquisition and transfer, and what the seller must do to rely on it
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLRHL (RDLeg 2/2004) art. 104.5 and art. 107.5
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated Texto Refundido de la Ley Reguladora de las Haciendas Locales, arts. 104 and 107, via the BOE legislación-consolidada open-data API — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4214/texto/bloque/a104 and .../a107
entries.locator: TRLRHL art. 104.5 (added by RDL 26/2021 art. único.1; current version of art. 104 from LO 2/2022, in force 23 March 2022): 'No se producirá la sujeción al impuesto en las transmisiones de terrenos respecto de los cuales se constate la inexistencia de incremento de valor...' — the interested party must declare the transmission and produce the títulos documenting acquisition and transmission; values compared are the greater of the deed figure or the administratively checked figure, excluding gastos and tributos; where the property has land and building, the land share is taken by the cadastral land/total proportion. TRLRHL art. 107.5: where the real increase is lower than the objective base, the real increase is taken as the base.
entries.as_of: Art. 104 consolidated to 23 March 2022; art. 107 consolidated to 28 January 2026; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Establish what the law provides where there has been no increase in value between acquisition and transfer, and what the seller must do to rely on it
entries.note: The answer is non-subjection under art. 104.5, not an exemption and not automatic. The seller must still declare the transmission and produce both deeds — silence forfeits it. Note the two distinct reliefs: art. 104.5 (no increase at all, no tax) and art. 107.5 (a real increase smaller than the objective base, tax on the smaller figure). Both are triggered by the taxpayer, both use the cadastral proportion to isolate the land.

entries.assertion: Establish which elements each municipality sets for itself and within what statutory ceiling — then state plainly that a figure from one Alicante-province town is not a figure for another
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLRHL arts. 107 and 108, showing which parameters are municipal and what caps bind them
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLRHL arts. 107 and 108 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4214/texto/bloque/a107 and .../a108
entries.locator: TRLRHL art. 107.4 (the coefficient is 'el que corresponda de los aprobados por el ayuntamiento según el periodo de generación', capped by the statutory table running 0,15 for under 1 year to 0,40 at 20 years or more); art. 107.2.a final paragraph (municipalities may set a reductor on the cadastral land value, maximum 15%); art. 108.1 (rate 'fijado por cada ayuntamiento, sin que dicho tipo pueda exceder del 30 por ciento', and municipalities may set one rate or one per generation period); art. 108.4–108.6 (ordenanza may grant bonificaciones up to 95%).
entries.as_of: Art. 107 consolidated to 28 January 2026; art. 108 consolidated to 31 October 2013; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Establish which elements each municipality sets for itself and within what statutory ceiling — then state plainly that a figure from one Alicante-province town is not a figure for another. Note that the statutory ceiling on the coefficients is itself unstable: it is updated annually by a norm of legal rank, and the updates for both 2025 and 2026 were enacted by decreto-ley and then left without effect when Congress refused to convalidate them.
entries.note: TIME-SENSITIVE because the ceiling moves and has twice failed to move. The consolidated art. 107.4 note records: the 1 January 2026 update of the maximum coefficients (RDL 16/2025 art. 18) was 'dejada sin efecto' by the Resolución de 27 de enero de 2026 publishing the Congress agreement derogating RDL 16/2025 (BOE-A-2026-2024); the identical thing happened to the 1 January 2025 update (RDL 9/2024, derogated by Resolución de 22 de enero de 2025, BOE-A-2025-1136). Anything written about the 2026 caps from a source published in December 2025 is wrong. The four municipal levers are: the coefficient per period, the optional reductor up to 15%, the rate up to 30%, and the bonificaciones.

entries.assertion: That a rate, coefficient or worked example from Alicante city, or from any province-wide figure, describes Dénia, Torrevieja, Benidorm or any other municipality — check the specific ayuntamiento or say you cannot
entries.source_required: The statute establishing that these parameters are municipal, plus at least one actual Alicante-province ordenanza showing a specific figure
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLRHL arts. 107.4 and 108.1 (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4214); Ayuntamiento de Dénia, official announcement of the modification of its IIVTNU fiscal ordinance — https://www.denia.es/es/denia/actualitat/noticia.aspx?id=6111
entries.locator: TRLRHL art. 108.1: the rate is 'el fijado por cada ayuntamiento' subject to the 30% cap; art. 107.4: the coefficient is the one 'aprobado por el ayuntamiento'. Ayuntamiento de Dénia announcement (16 March 2022) adapting its ordenanza to RDL 26/2021: rate set at 30% for holdings of 0–5 years and 28% for 6 years and over, with a 95% bonificación on the cuota íntegra for the taxpayer's habitual residence.
entries.as_of: TRLRHL consolidated to 28 January 2026; Dénia announcement dated 16 March 2022; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: That a rate, coefficient or worked example from Alicante city, or from any province-wide figure, describes Dénia, Torrevieja, Benidorm or any other municipality — check the specific ayuntamiento or say you cannot
entries.note: There is no such thing as a province-wide IIVTNU rate — the tax has no provincial layer, so a 'province figure' is a fabrication rather than an approximation. Dénia's own figures (30%/28%, 95% habitual-residence bonificación) are a live counter-example. Benidorm delegates the tax's management to SUMA Gestión Tributaria, which changes where you look but not who sets the rate. Always name the ordenanza.

entries.assertion: Never publish a waiting time or turnaround figure for any route — no verified source establishes one, and it varies by country and by consular post
entries.source_required: Either an official series of processing times, or the absence of one; and any statute setting a maximum period for a step in the chain
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated Ley Hipotecaria, art. 18 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1946-2453/texto/bloque/a18
entries.locator: Ley Hipotecaria art. 18, second paragraph (current wording from Ley 24/2005 art. 26.1, in force 20 November 2005): 'El plazo máximo para inscribir el documento será de quince días contados desde la fecha del asiento de presentación', extendable by up to fifteen further days by the Dirección General on accredited extraordinary grounds; late inscription carries a 30% arancel reduction and quarterly statistical reporting of out-of-time inscriptions.
entries.as_of: Ley Hipotecaria consolidated to 20 November 2005 (art. 18); read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Never publish an observed waiting time or turnaround average for administrative or consular steps — no official series establishes one, and it varies by country and by consular post. Statutory maximum periods are a different thing and may be stated as law, clearly labelled as the legal maximum rather than the typical wait: for example, Ley Hipotecaria art. 18 gives the registrar fifteen days from the asiento de presentación to inscribe, extendable by up to fifteen more.
entries.note: Corrected because 'any route' over-reaches. I could not find an official series of consular or administrative processing times, so the core caution stands and I have not upgraded it. But at least one step in a Costa Blanca sale does have a published statutory maximum, and a blanket ban would stop the engine from stating black-letter law. The distinction that matters is legal maximum (publishable, cite the article) versus observed average (not publishable, no source).
