entries.assertion: When the seller of an Alicante-province home is not a Spanish tax resident, what amounts are withheld, deducted or held back at or around completion, who takes each one and under what instrument, and which of them — if any — is recoverable, by what filing and by when?
entries.source_required: TRLIRNR art. 25.2 and its reglamento for the retention; TRLRHL art. 106 for the municipal tax; the reglamento for the recovery route and deadlines
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25 (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4527); BOE consolidated Reglamento del IRNR, RD 1776/2004, arts. 14 and 16 (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-14532); BOE consolidated TRLRHL art. 106 (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4214)
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 25.2 (buyer retains and pays 3% of the agreed consideration as a pago a cuenta); RD 1776/2004 art. 14.1 and 14.3 (same 3%; the withholder declares and pays to the AEAT office covering the property's location within one month of the transmission); art. 14.4 (the non-resident declares and settles the definitive tax, offsetting the retention, within three months from the end of that one-month period; the Administration then refunds any excess); art. 16.1 (refund of the excess over the cuota by autoliquidación); TRLRHL art. 106.2 (buyer is sujeto pasivo sustituto for the plusvalía where the seller is a non-resident individual).
entries.as_of: TRLIRNR consolidated to 1 January 2015; RD 1776/2004 art. 14 consolidated to the RD 1576/2006 amendment; TRLRHL art. 106 consolidated to 17 October 2014; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: When the seller of an Alicante-province home is not a Spanish tax resident, what amounts are withheld, deducted or held back at or around completion, who takes each one and under what instrument, and which of them — if any — is recoverable, by what filing and by when?
entries.note: Well-formed question; every presupposition holds. The full answer has three layers, and the question is right to separate 'who takes each one': the 3% is a statutory retention taken by the buyer and paid to the State; the plusvalía is a municipal tax the buyer becomes statutorily liable for as substitute; and any further holdback (community fees, IBI, mortgage redemption) is contract, not statute. Only the 3% is recoverable as such, and only via the seller's own filing.

entries.assertion: Establish which withholdings or retentions arise specifically because the seller is not tax-resident in Spain, who is obliged to make each one, and the instrument that imposes it
entries.source_required: The two statutory provisions that switch on non-residence: TRLIRNR art. 25.2 and TRLRHL art. 106.2
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25 (https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4527/texto/bloque/a25); BOE consolidated TRLRHL art. 106 (https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4214/texto/bloque/a106); BOE consolidated RD 1776/2004 art. 14 (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-14532)
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 25.2: 'el adquirente estará obligado a retener e ingresar el 3 por ciento... de la contraprestación acordada, en concepto de pago a cuenta'; RD 1776/2004 art. 14.2 lists the only two exceptions (a certificate from the tax administration evidencing the transferor's liability to IRPF or IS, and contributions of property to Spanish company capital). TRLRHL art. 106.2: the acquirer 'tendrá la consideración de sujeto pasivo sustituto del contribuyente... cuando el contribuyente sea una persona física no residente en España'.
entries.as_of: TRLIRNR art. 25 consolidated to 1 January 2015; TRLRHL art. 106 consolidated to 17 October 2014; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Establish which withholdings or retentions arise specifically because the seller is not tax-resident in Spain, who is obliged to make each one, and the instrument that imposes it
entries.note: Two, and only two, are statutory and switch on non-residence. Both fall on the buyer. One drafting trap to flag: the two provisions use different tests. TRLIRNR art. 25.2 turns on being a contribuyente of the IRNR acting without a permanent establishment, i.e. on tax residence. TRLRHL art. 106.2 turns on being a 'persona física no residente en España' — an individual only, so a non-resident company selling does not trigger the substitution.

entries.assertion: Establish whether the municipal land-value tax liability sits with the seller or shifts to another party when the seller is a non-resident individual, and whether that changes what the buyer's side holds back at completion — labelling clearly which part is statute and which is market practice
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLRHL art. 106 in full, including the sustituto rule
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLRHL art. 106 via the BOE legislación-consolidada open-data API — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4214/texto/bloque/a106
entries.locator: TRLRHL art. 106.1.b (on transfers for consideration the contribuyente is the person who transfers the land) and art. 106.2 (the acquirer is sujeto pasivo sustituto del contribuyente 'cuando el contribuyente sea una persona física no residente en España'). Current version from Ley 18/2014 art. 123.2, in force 17 October 2014 (which suppressed the former apartado 3).
entries.as_of: Consolidated to 17 October 2014; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Establish whether the municipal land-value tax liability sits with the seller or shifts to another party when the seller is a non-resident individual, and whether that changes what the buyer's side holds back at completion — labelling clearly which part is statute and which is market practice
entries.note: The answer: the seller remains the contribuyente, and the buyer is added as sustituto — a substitution of the person who must pay and file, not a transfer of who economically bears it. The labelling the instruction demands is exactly right: the substitution is statute (art. 106.2); the holdback at completion is not — no provision requires a buyer to retain anything for the plusvalía. It is a contractual response to the buyer's own statutory exposure.

entries.assertion: Establish what a non-resident seller practically needs in order to receive the proceeds at all (identification number, Spanish account, fiscal representative), and whether each is a legal requirement or a bank requirement
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLIRNR art. 10 for the fiscal representative; separate primary sources for the NIE and the bank account
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR art. 10 via the BOE legislación-consolidada open-data API — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4527/texto/bloque/a10
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 10.1 (current wording from Ley 11/2021 art. 2.2, effects for tax periods from 1 January 2021, in force 11 July 2021): the duty to appoint a representative resident in Spain binds contribuyentes 'que no sean residentes en otro Estado miembro de la Unión Europea', and even then only where they operate through a permanent establishment, in the cases of arts. 24.2 and 38, or where the tax administration so requires given the amount and character of the income or the ownership of Spanish property. Second paragraph: the duty does not apply to EEA states with mutual-assistance rules on exchange of information and recovery. Art. 10.4: failure is a grave infringement, fixed fine of €2,000, rising to €6,000 for residents of jurisdictions without effective exchange of information.
entries.as_of: Consolidated to 11 July 2021 (art. 10); read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Establish what a non-resident seller practically needs in order to receive the proceeds at all (identification number, Spanish account, fiscal representative), and whether each is a legal requirement or a bank requirement
entries.note: Sound instruction, and the fiscal-representative limb is now settled: it is emphatically not a universal requirement. EU residents are outside it entirely; qualifying EEA residents (Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein) are outside it too; for everyone else it bites only in the enumerated cases or on the Administration's demand. Agencies routinely sell it as compulsory for all foreign sellers, which is wrong. Open in this pass: I did not open a primary source for the NIE limb or the Spanish-account limb, so treat those two as unsettled until checked — the account in particular looks like bank practice rather than law.

entries.locator: LIRPF art. 9.1 (183 days / centre of economic interests — nationality is not a criterion); LIRPF art. 66 as amended by Ley 7/2024 DF 7.1 with effect 1 January 2025 (progressive savings scale, combined rates 19% / 21% / 23% / 27% / 30%, the top band from €300,000); TRLIRNR art. 25.1.f.3.º (flat 19% on gains from transfers, for taxpayers without a permanent establishment).

entries.final_wording: Never treat nationality as the trigger — the rate and regime turn on where the seller is tax-resident, not on the passport, and residents and non-residents are taxed on entirely different scales
entries.note: Verified. One numerical coincidence worth guarding against, because it invites a wrong simplification: the resident scale's first band is also 19%, so on a small gain the two regimes can produce the same rate. That does not make them the same scale — one is flat and one is progressive to 30% — and a writer who notices the coincidence must not report the regimes as equivalent.

entries.assertion: Never let a city figure stand in for a province, or a province figure for a coastal town
entries.source_required: An official statistical source showing that distinct geographic levels are published separately, and that the levels are not interchangeable
entries.source_opened: Consejo General del Notariado, Centro de Información Estadística del Notariado — https://www.notariado.org/liferay/web/cien/inicio; plus BOE consolidated TRLRHL arts. 107.4 and 108.1 (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4214) and the Ayuntamiento de Dénia IIVTNU ordinance announcement (https://www.denia.es/es/denia/actualitat/noticia.aspx?id=6111)
entries.locator: CIEN publishes monthly housing-sale statistics drawn from the Índice Único Informatizado Notarial — deed/transaction prices, not asking prices — with roughly a two-month lag (June 2026 data published 27 August 2026; May 2026 data published 30 July 2026). On the tax side, TRLRHL art. 108.1 makes the IIVTNU rate municipal, so no provincial rate exists at all, and Dénia's own 30%/28% rates are a worked counter-example.
entries.as_of: CIEN latest reference period June 2026, published 27 August 2026; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Never let a city figure stand in for a province, or a province figure for a coastal town
entries.note: Verified in both directions. For tax parameters, a provincial figure does not merely differ from a municipal one — for the IIVTNU it does not exist, so quoting one is invention. For prices, an official municipal- and postcode-level notarial series does exist, so substituting a provincial average is a choice to use a worse number when a better one is free. Whichever level is used, name it, and name the price concept: the notarial series is deed price, not asking price, and the two diverge.

entries.assertion: From the date of death to the moment an inherited Comunitat Valenciana property can legally be transferred, which obligations run on which clocks, what does asking for more time require and what does it cost, and what follows for an heir who misses each one?
entries.source_required: Consolidated Reglamento del ISD (RD 1629/1991), the articles governing filing periods, extension and suspension
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated Reglamento del Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones, RD 1629/1991, Sección segunda 'plazos de presentación, prórroga y suspensión', arts. 67–69 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1991-27678
entries.locator: Art. 67.1.a: six months from the day of death (or from when a declaration of death becomes firm). Art. 68.1: the competent office may grant an extension 'por un plazo igual al señalado para su presentación'. Art. 68.2: applied for by heirs, executors or administrators within the first five months of the filing period, with the death certificate and the prescribed particulars. Art. 68.6: the extension runs from the end of the six months and 'llevará aparejada la obligación de satisfacer el interés de demora' to the day of filing. Art. 68.7: if nothing is filed by the end of the extension, a provisional liquidation may be raised on the Administration's own data, without prejudice to penalties. Art. 69: interruption where litigation or a juicio voluntario de testamentaría is raised.
entries.as_of: RD 1629/1991 as consolidated (Sección segunda unamended in substance); read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: From the date of death to the moment an inherited Comunitat Valenciana property can legally be transferred, which obligations run on which clocks, what does asking for more time require and what does it cost, and what follows for an heir who misses each one?
entries.note: Well-formed, and the question's three parts each have a clean statutory answer. The trap the question correctly anticipates: the extension is not free and not automatic. It must be asked for inside the first five months — a request in month six is out of time — it doubles the period rather than extending it indefinitely, and it carries interés de demora from month six onward. Heirs abroad who assume the extension is a formality routinely miss the five-month cut-off.

entries.assertion: Establish what relief the Comunitat Valenciana currently applies to the inheritance-tax cuota for each relationship group as at the publication date, reading the consolidated Generalitat article rather than commentary, and establish whether the filing obligation survives that relief
entries.source_required: The Generalitat's own statement of the reliefs in force, keyed to the article of Ley 13/1997
entries.source_opened: Generalitat Valenciana, Conselleria de Hisenda, 'Beneficios fiscales 2026' (https://hisenda.gva.es/es/web/tributos/beneficis-fiscals-2026); Agència Tributària Valenciana, 'Entra en vigor la nueva bonificación del Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones' (https://atv.gva.es/es/novedades/-/asset_publisher/4DsaTMdH9ZRB/content/entra-en-vigor-la-nueva-bonificacion-del-impuesto-sobre-sucesiones-y-donaciones); BOE consolidated Ley 29/1987 DA 2ª Dos (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1987-28141)
entries.locator: Ley 13/1997 art. 12 bis.1: 99% bonificación on the cuota for mortis causa acquisitions by Grupo I and Grupo II relatives, and for persons with physical/sensory disability of 65% or more or psychic disability of 33% or more. Ley 13/1997 art. 12 bis.2: 25% bonificación for Grupo III collaterals (siblings, uncles/aunts, nephews/nieces), applying to hechos imponibles from 1 June 2026. Grupo IV: no bonificación listed. Introduced by Ley 6/2023, de 22 de noviembre (DOGV 23 November 2023), with effects retroactive to 28 May 2023 (ATV). Ley 29/1987 DA 2ª Dos: taxpayers accounting to the State Administration must file an autoliquidación.
entries.as_of: Generalitat benefits page current for 2026; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Establish what relief the Comunitat Valenciana currently applies to the inheritance-tax cuota for each relationship group as at the publication date, reading the consolidated Generalitat article rather than commentary, and establish whether the filing obligation survives that relief. As at 1 September 2026 the position is: Grupos I and II, 99% (art. 12 bis.1 Ley 13/1997); Grupo III collaterals, 25%, but only for hechos imponibles arising on or after 1 June 2026 (art. 12 bis.2); Grupo IV, none.
entries.note: TIME-SENSITIVE, and this is the live trap in the whole seller bank. The Grupo III 25% bonificación is date-gated to hechos imponibles from 1 June 2026 — three months old at the publication date — so every source written before mid-2026 says Grupo III gets nothing, and every source that reports the 25% without the date gate will be wrong for a death that occurred earlier. Since ISD accrues at death, the gate turns on the date of death, not the date of filing. Open limb: I could not open the consolidated text of art. 12 bis itself, only the Generalitat's benefits page keyed to it, so any timely-filing condition inside the article remains unchecked. The general filing duty plainly survives — a bonificación reduces the cuota, it does not remove the hecho imponible — and for non-resident heirs accounting to the State, DA 2ª Dos of Ley 29/1987 requires an autoliquidación regardless.

entries.assertion: Do not assume the municipal calculation is identical across Alicante province — coefficients and rates are set municipality by municipality, and more than one calculation method may be available
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLRHL arts. 104.5, 107 and 108, showing both the municipal parameters and the alternative base
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLRHL arts. 104, 107 and 108 via the BOE legislación-consolidada open-data API — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4214/texto/bloque/a104 (and .../a107, .../a108); Ayuntamiento de Dénia IIVTNU ordinance announcement (https://www.denia.es/es/denia/actualitat/noticia.aspx?id=6111)
entries.locator: TRLRHL art. 107.4 (coefficients approved by the ayuntamiento within the statutory maxima), art. 107.2.a (optional municipal reductor up to 15% on the cadastral land value), art. 108.1 (rate set by each ayuntamiento, cap 30%, one rate or one per generation period); the second method is art. 107.5 read with art. 104.5 — at the taxpayer's instance, where the real increase is lower than the objective base, the real increase becomes the base. Dénia: 30% for 0–5 years, 28% from 6 years, 95% habitual-residence bonificación.
entries.as_of: Arts. 104 and 107 consolidated to 2022 and 28 January 2026 respectively; art. 108 to 31 October 2013; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Do not assume the municipal calculation is identical across Alicante province — coefficients and rates are set municipality by municipality, and more than one calculation method may be available
entries.note: Both limbs verified. On the second limb, be precise about what the choice is: the objective method (art. 107.1–107.4) is the default, and the real-gain method (art. 107.5) is not an alternative the town offers but a right the taxpayer must invoke, using the art. 104.5 procedure and producing both deeds. The taxpayer takes the lower of the two. A writer who describes it as 'the town lets you choose' has it wrong.

entries.assertion: Do not assume an heir living abroad is taxed on the same scale as a resident, and do not file a heir's nationality as if it settled their tax residence or their EU/EEA/third-country status
entries.source_required: Consolidated Ley 29/1987 DA 2ª, including the post-2021 amendment state
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated Ley 29/1987 del Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones, disposición adicional segunda — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1987-28141
entries.locator: Ley 29/1987 DA 2ª Uno.1.b: 'si el causante hubiera sido residente en una Comunidad Autónoma, los contribuyentes no residentes tendrán derecho a la aplicación de la normativa propia aprobada por dicha Comunidad Autónoma' — with no EU/EEA restriction in the current wording. Amended by Ley 11/2021, de 9 de julio, art. 4.6; consolidated note: 'Última actualización, publicada el 10/07/2021, en vigor a partir del 11/07/2021'. DA 2ª Dos: those accounting to the State Administration file an autoliquidación.
entries.as_of: Consolidated to 11 July 2021; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Do not assume an heir living abroad is taxed on a worse scale than a resident heir. Since Ley 11/2021 (in force 11 July 2021) removed the EU/EEA limit from DA 2ª of Ley 29/1987, a non-resident heir — including one resident in a third country — is entitled to the rules of the Comunidad Autónoma where the deceased resided, so the Valencian reliefs apply to them. What does change is the competent administration (the State, under DA 2ª Dos, not the Generalitat) and the scope of the charge (obligación real — Spanish-situs assets only). And never file an heir's nationality as if it settled their tax residence or their EU/EEA/third-country status.
entries.note: Corrected because the instruction as written points a writer toward the pre-2015/pre-2021 error in the opposite direction. The historic problem was Spain taxing non-resident heirs worse; CJEU C-127/12 and then Ley 11/2021 fixed it, and the current consolidated text says 'los contribuyentes no residentes' flat, with no EU/EEA qualifier. An engine told 'do not assume the same scale' will reach for a difference in the scale that no longer exists. The real differences are administrative and territorial, and those are the ones to state. The second clause of the assertion is correct and is kept.

entries.assertion: Do not assume the heirs' passports determine their tax or immigration treatment — EEA citizens, Swiss citizens and third-country nationals are separate categories, and tax residence is separate again
entries.source_required: Provisions that actually draw the EU / EEA / third-country lines, plus the residence test
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR art. 10 and disposición adicional séptima (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4527); BOE consolidated LIRPF art. 9 (https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2006-20764/texto/bloque/a9); BOE consolidated Ley 29/1987 DA 2ª (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1987-28141)
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 10.1 draws three tiers: EU Member State residents (no representative duty); EEA states with mutual assistance on exchange of information and recovery (duty disapplied); everyone else. TRLIRNR DA 7ª.1 and .4 grant the main-home reinvestment exemption to EU residents and extend it to qualifying EEA residents only. LIRPF art. 9.1 sets residence by days and economic interests, with no nationality criterion. Ley 29/1987 DA 2ª Uno.1.b (as amended 11 July 2021) applies regional rules to all non-residents without an EU/EEA filter.
entries.as_of: TRLIRNR art. 10 consolidated to 11 July 2021; DA 7ª as consolidated; LIRPF art. 9 to 1 January 2007; Ley 29/1987 DA 2ª to 11 July 2021; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Do not assume the heirs' passports determine their tax or immigration treatment — EEA citizens, Swiss citizens and third-country nationals are separate categories, and tax residence is separate again
entries.note: Verified, and worth making concrete because the categories bite unevenly. Switzerland is neither EU nor EEA, so for TRLIRNR art. 10 and DA 7ª a Swiss resident sits with third countries, notwithstanding the free-movement agreements. Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein are EEA and do qualify. But for the ISD regional rules the EU/EEA/third distinction no longer bites at all after Ley 11/2021 — so the same three passports produce different answers in IRNR and identical answers in ISD. State which tax you are talking about before you state the category.

entries.assertion: When an individual who is not tax-resident in Spain sells a Costa Blanca home with a mortgage still outstanding, what amounts are legally withheld, retained or paid out of the price at or around completion, which of those are statutory obligations and which are contractual practice, and by what procedure and on what timetable is each one recovered, if at all?
entries.source_required: The statutory retention and substitution provisions, plus the recovery route, so the statute/practice line can be drawn
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25.2 (https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4527/texto/bloque/a25); BOE consolidated RD 1776/2004 arts. 14 and 16 (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-14532); BOE consolidated TRLRHL art. 106.2 (https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4214/texto/bloque/a106)
entries.locator: Statutory: TRLIRNR art. 25.2 (3% retention by the buyer as pago a cuenta) and TRLRHL art. 106.2 (buyer as sujeto pasivo sustituto for the plusvalía). Recovery: RD 1776/2004 art. 14.4 (seller's declaration within three months of the end of the buyer's one-month period, offsetting the retention, with refund of the excess) and art. 16.1. Nothing in either text imposes any further holdback; mortgage redemption at completion rests on the loan contract and the need to cancel the charge, not on tax law.
entries.as_of: TRLIRNR consolidated to 1 January 2015; RD 1776/2004 art. 14 as consolidated; TRLRHL art. 106 to 17 October 2014; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: When an individual who is not tax-resident in Spain sells a Costa Blanca home with a mortgage still outstanding, what amounts are legally withheld, retained or paid out of the price at or around completion, which of those are statutory obligations and which are contractual practice, and by what procedure and on what timetable is each one recovered, if at all?
entries.note: Well-formed, and the statute/practice split it insists on is the right axis. Answering it: two statutory items (3% retention, plusvalía substitution), and everything else — mortgage redemption, community-fee and IBI apportionments, agency retentions — is contract. Only the 3% has a recovery route, and 'if at all' is well chosen, because the plusvalía is not recovered by the seller: under LGT art. 36.3 the substitute can come after the seller for it.

entries.assertion: 25.2 TRLIRNR who is obliged to withhold the retention on a sale by a non-resident, what it is calculated on, what instrument it is paid with, and what legal character it has — a payment on account is not a final tax
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25.2 verbatim, plus the reglamento and the ministerial order fixing the form
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25 via the BOE legislación-consolidada open-data API (https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4527/texto/bloque/a25); BOE consolidated RD 1776/2004 art. 14 (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-14532); Orden EHA/3316/2010 approving modelos 210, 211 and 213 (https://www.boe.es/buscar/doc.php?id=BOE-A-2010-19707)
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 25.2, first paragraph, verbatim: 'Tratándose de transmisiones de bienes inmuebles situados en territorio español por contribuyentes que actúen sin establecimiento permanente, el adquirente estará obligado a retener e ingresar el 3 por ciento, o a efectuar el ingreso a cuenta correspondiente, de la contraprestación acordada, en concepto de pago a cuenta del impuesto correspondiente a aquéllos.' Third paragraph: if unpaid, the transferred property is affected to the lesser of the retention and the tax. RD 1776/2004 art. 14.3 (filing and payment within one month of the transmission, at the AEAT office covering the property). Form: modelo 211 (Orden EHA/3316/2010).
entries.as_of: TRLIRNR art. 25 consolidated to 1 January 2015; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: 25.2 TRLIRNR who is obliged to withhold the retention on a sale by a non-resident, what it is calculated on, what instrument it is paid with, and what legal character it has — a payment on account is not a final tax
entries.note: Every element checks out against the article. The buyer withholds; the base is the agreed consideration, not the gain and not the cadastral value; the instrument is modelo 211 within one month; and the statute itself supplies the legal character in words — 'en concepto de pago a cuenta'. The instruction's closing clause is therefore not an interpretation but a restatement of the text. Cosmetic only: the assertion is grammatically truncated — it reads as if 'Establish under art.' was lost from the front — so the substance is verified but the sentence should be repaired before it is used as a prompt.

entries.assertion: Establish who the plusvalía municipal taxpayer is on an onerous transfer, whether that changes when the individual seller is non-resident, and what that does to a buyer's willingness to retain funds at completion
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLRHL art. 106 in full
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLRHL art. 106 via the BOE legislación-consolidada open-data API — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4214/texto/bloque/a106
entries.locator: TRLRHL art. 106.1.b: on transfers of land for consideration ('a título oneroso') the contribuyente is the person or entity 'que transmita el terreno'. Art. 106.2: in those same cases the acquirer 'tendrá la consideración de sujeto pasivo sustituto del contribuyente... cuando el contribuyente sea una persona física no residente en España'. Version in force from Ley 18/2014 art. 123.2, 17 October 2014.
entries.as_of: Consolidated to 17 October 2014; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Establish who the plusvalía municipal taxpayer is on an onerous transfer, whether that changes when the individual seller is non-resident, and what that does to a buyer's willingness to retain funds at completion
entries.note: Answered: seller is the contribuyente on an onerous transfer; the buyer is added as sustituto where the contribuyente is a non-resident individual. Two limits to hold on to. It applies to onerous transfers only — on an inheritance or gift, art. 106.1.a already makes the acquirer the contribuyente, so no substitution question arises. And it applies to a 'persona física', so a non-resident company selling does not trigger it. The effect on the buyer's behaviour is rational rather than legal: the buyer is now the one the ayuntamiento will pursue, which is why a retention appears in the contract, but no rule obliges one.

TRLIRNR DA 7ª.1 and .4 (main-home reinvestment exemption for EU residents, extended to qualifying EEA residents). LIRPF art. 9.1 (residence by days or economic interests; nationality absent).
entries.as_of: TRLIRNR art. 10 consolidated to 11 July 2021; DA 7ª as consolidated; LIRPF art. 9 to 1 January 2007; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Do not treat nationality as residence or as immigration status — a Norwegian, a Swiss and a British owner may each sit differently, and a passport does not decide where someone is tax-resident
entries.note: Verified, and the three examples chosen are genuinely different under the same two articles. Norway is EEA with mutual assistance: no fiscal-representative duty, and the DA 7ª reinvestment exemption is available. Switzerland is neither EU nor EEA: outside both. The UK has been outside both since Brexit and is likewise outside both. So on identical facts a Norwegian and a British owner get different answers — from nationality-linked residence, not from nationality itself, which is precisely the distinction the instruction protects.

entries.assertion: Do not assume the liability shift on plusvalía for a non-resident seller means the seller ends up not bearing the cost
entries.source_required: TRLRHL art. 106.2 for the substitution, and the general rule on what a sustituto may recover
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLRHL art. 106 (https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4214/texto/bloque/a106); BOE consolidated Ley 58/2003 General Tributaria, art. 36 (https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2003-23186/texto/bloque/a36)
entries.locator: TRLRHL art. 106.2 (acquirer as sujeto pasivo sustituto where the contribuyente is a non-resident individual). LGT art. 36.3: 'Es sustituto el sujeto pasivo que, por imposición de la ley y en lugar del contribuyente, está obligado a cumplir la obligación tributaria principal... El sustituto podrá exigir del contribuyente el importe de las obligaciones tributarias satisfechas, salvo que la ley señale otra cosa.' LGT art. 36 has a single version, in force 1 July 2004.
entries.as_of: TRLRHL art. 106 consolidated to 17 October 2014; LGT art. 36 in force since 1 July 2004, never amended; read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Do not assume the liability shift on plusvalía for a non-resident seller means the seller ends up not bearing the cost
entries.note: Verified from the general part of the LGT, which is where the answer actually lives. Substitution changes who must pay the Administration; art. 36.3 expressly preserves the substitute's right to demand the amount back from the contribuyente, and TRLRHL says nothing to the contrary. So the seller remains the economic bearer, either by reimbursing the buyer or, in practice, by the buyer retaining the sum from the price at completion. Copy that tells a non-resident seller 'the buyer pays the plusvalía' is wrong in substance even though it is right about who files.

entries.assertion: Establish what the seller must hold on a Comunitat Valenciana sale in the way of an energy certificate and a second-occupancy licence, and confirm the current instrument — the framework changed in 2025 and the groundwork marks the at-signing requirement as unverified

Ley 5/2025 disposición derogatoria única, letra g) repeals Decreto 80/2023 (DC-23); the Generalitat records the Orden de 7 de diciembre de 2009 (DC-09) as remaining in force. Decreto 12/2021 (DOGV 3 February 2021) establishes a declaración responsable for first and successive occupation, with municipalities able to retain an express licence by ordenanza.
entries.as_of: RD 390/2021 as consolidated; Ley 5/2025 published 14 June 2025; GVA habitability page read 1 September 2026
entries.final_wording: Establish what the seller must hold on a Comunitat Valenciana sale in the way of an energy certificate and a second-occupancy declaración responsable — not a 'licence', which survives only in those municipalities that have retained an express licence regime by ordenanza — and confirm the current instrument. The framework changed in 2025: Decreto 80/2023 (DC-23) was repealed by Ley 5/2025 and the Orden de 7 de diciembre de 2009 (DC-09) is again the habitability standard, while Decreto 12/2021 continues to govern the occupancy declaration. The at-signing requirement remains unverified: RD 390/2021 art. 17.2 does require the registered energy certificate and label to be annexed to the sale contract, but no equivalent provision requiring the occupancy declaration at the moment of signing was found.
entries.note: Corrected on the naming, which is not pedantry — 'second-occupancy licence' is the pre-2021 instrument, and telling a Valencian seller to obtain a licence sends them to the wrong procedure in most municipalities. On the two limbs separately: the energy-certificate requirement at signing is now settled and statutory (art. 17.2, annexed to the contract). The occupancy limb is not — Decreto 12/2021 sets up the declaración responsable but I found no provision tying it to the deed, so the groundwork's 'unverified' flag should stay, and the copy should describe it as what buyers, notaries and utility suppliers require rather than as a statutory condition of signing.

TRLIRNR art. 25.1.f.3.º (non-residents without permanent establishment): a single 19% on 'ganancias patrimoniales que se pongan de manifiesto con ocasión de transmisiones de elementos patrimoniales'. entries.final_wording: Do not call the non-resident property-gain rate contested: AEAT applies a flat 19% to a capital gain on a transfer for every non-resident taxpayer acting without a permanent establishment in Spain — the rate in TRLIRNR art. 25.1.f.3.º carries no EU/EEA/third-country distinction.
entries.note: Corrected only to add the qualifier the statute's own structure imposes. 'Every non-resident' is true of the overwhelming majority of sellers the engine will address and is right to resist the common blog claim that third-country sellers pay 24%. But arts. 24–25 govern income obtained without a permanent establishment; a non-resident operating through a PE is taxed under Capítulo III on the PE's base, not at the 25.1.f flat rate. Adding six words removes an unforced error without weakening the point. Note also this is the rate only — the reliefs on top of it are not uniform (DA 7ª reinvestment is EU/EEA only), so 'the rate is the same for everyone' must not slide into 'the outcome is the same for everyone'.

entries.note: Verified, and this pairs with id 64 as the same rule stated from the other side. Worth carrying into the copy: the EU/EEA qualifier in art. 25.1.a is not automatic for EEA states — it requires effective exchange of tax information under DA 1ª.4 of Ley 36/2006 — so 'EEA' is a condition to check, not a label to apply. And note the asymmetry that causes most of the confusion: the same Norwegian owner pays 19% on rental income because of where they live, and 19% on the sale gain regardless of where they live. Same number, two different reasons.

STS 620/2026, de 21 de mayo de 2026 (appeal by the Generalitat Valenciana), annulling the Registro Único de Arrendamientos of RD 1312/2024 for lack of state competence while upholding the ventanilla única digital and platform data-transmission duties

entries.final_wording: Establish what registration, number or licence a short-let dwelling must hold in 2026 in order to be advertised or transferred, whether it attaches to the property or to the operator, and what becomes of it on a sale — treat transferability to a new owner as an open question to be answered from the instrument, not assumed. Note that the answer moved during 2026: the Supreme Court (STS 620/2026, 21 May 2026) annulled the state single rental registry of RD 1312/2024, so the state registration number is no longer required to advertise, while the Valencian registration remains — and under art. 23 bis.3 it does not simply pass to a buyer.
entries.note: The instruction's caution is right and the instrument answers it: the Valencian registration is NOT freely transferable — the new owner must file a fresh declaración responsable with an up-to-date municipal urban-compatibility report. Flagged TIME-SENSITIVE for two reasons: (1) the state layer changed mid-2026 when STS 620/2026 struck down the NRUA, and the State may legislate again; (2) the Valencian registration itself now carries a five-year validity, so 'holds a number' is a statement with an expiry date. Anything written in 2026 that still tells sellers they need the state NRUA number is wrong.

entries.note: The instruction lists the right four items and asks the right follow-up question. Two points to get right when it is answered: the competent body for the deposit in the Comunitat Valenciana is the Generalitat's treasury (Conselleria de Hacienda), not a national body or the town hall; and of the four, the only one whose absence is a statutory bar at the deed is a different document altogether — the community-debt certificate under LPH art. 9.1.e). The tenancy contract, rent record and deposit receipt are contractual due-diligence items a buyer demands, not documents the law compels the seller to produce.

entries.source_required: An official time-on-market series, or proof that none exists at that geography
entries.source_opened: INE — ETDP últimos datos, https://www.ine.es/dyngs/INEbase/es/operacion.htm?c=Estadistica_C&cid=1254736171438&menu=ultiDatos&idp=1254735576606 ; INE — IPV últimos datos, https://www.ine.es/dyngs/INEbase/es/operacion.htm?c=Estadistica_C&cid=1254736152838&idp=1254735976607&menu=ultiDatos ; MIVAU — Valor tasado de la vivienda, https://www.mivau.gob.es/el-ministerio/observatorios-y-estadisticas/estadisticas/valor-tasado-vivienda
entries.locator: None of the three official housing instruments (INE ETDP registered transaction counts; INE IPV price index; MIVAU appraisal-value €/m²) contains a duration, listing-date or listing-outcome variable. The circulating duration figures I could trace are private and mutually inconsistent: 73 days (Tecnocasa/UPF 2024 report), 136 days (a blog citing idealista), and idealista's quarterly distribution of homes sold in under a week / a month / three months
entries.final_wording: For a home in an Alicante-province coastal town, what published instruments (if any) measure how long a sale takes, what precise start and end event does each one use, and what share of listings end for a reason other than a completed sale?
entries.note: The question is correctly framed, including the 'if any', and the honest answer is that no official instrument measures it. The official series all begin at the registered deed, so nothing in them can date a listing. Everything circulating on 'days to sell' comes from private data sets with undisclosed or different start events (listing published vs. offer accepted vs. deed signed), which is why the numbers disagree by a factor of nearly two. On the last clause: I found no published source at any geography measuring what share of listings end without a sale — that part should be answered 'not published'.

entries.as_of: Notariado portal live since 2025-10-23; MIVAU latest quarter Q1 2026; idealista methodology as published Q3 2025
entries.final_wording: Establish all three published euro-per-m² series and name the publisher type for each, since only one of the three is official statistics: (1) the ministry — MIVAU's 'Valor tasado de la vivienda', a quarterly appraisal-based €/m² series covering provinces and municipalities over 25,000 inhabitants, and the only official statistic of the three; (2) a professional corporation — the Consejo General del Notariado's Portal Estadístico del Notariado, live since 23 October 2025, publishing average price per m² from notarised deeds down to postcode level (the Colegio de Registradores publishes a comparable deed-based series); and (3) a private listings portal — idealista or Fotocasa, publishing asking prices from their own advertisements. The notarial series is deed price, not an official statistic.
entries.note: Wrong as written, and wrong against itself. The assertion first says only one of the three publisher types is official statistics, then calls the Consejo General del Notariado series 'the third official euro-per-m2 series' — it cannot be both. The CGN is a corporación de derecho público, a professional body; its own launch material frames the portal as a transparency service and makes no official-statistics claim. The genuinely official €/m² series is the ministry's Valor tasado. Two further repairs: the launch date 'October 2025' is right (23 Oct 2025), so that part stands; and the assertion is truncated mid-sentence ('average price per m'), which is how the contradiction survived earlier passes. Note also that the INE's IPV is not a euro-per-m² series at all — it is an index — so it must not be counted as one of the three.

entries.assertion: In a Comunitat Valenciana residential sale, which documents does the law expressly prevent a notary from authorising the deed without, which ones instead affect only the price or the buyer's mortgage, and which merely expose the seller to a penalty after the event?
entries.source_required: Consolidated statutory texts containing (or not containing) an express bar on authorising the deed
entries.source_opened: BOE — Ley 49/1960 LPH consolidated, art. 9.1.e), https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1960-10906/texto/bloque/anoveno ; BOE — Ley 5/2019, de contratos de crédito inmobiliario, art. 15, https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2019-3814/texto/bloque/ar-15 ; BOE — Real Decreto 390/2021, art. 17, https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2021-9176/texto
entries.locator: LPH art. 9.1.e): community-debt certificate — '…sin la cual no podrá autorizarse el otorgamiento del documento público, salvo que fuese expresamente exonerado de esta obligación por el adquirente'. Ley 5/2019 art. 15.5: where the acta previa cannot be completed, 'no podrá autorizarse la escritura pública de préstamo' — the mortgage deed only. RD 390/2021 art. 17.2: a registered energy performance certificate and label 'se anexará al contrato de compraventa' — an annexation duty, enforced by the Ley 8/2013 penalty regime, not a bar on the notary
entries.as_of: All three consolidated texts current to 2026-09-01
entries.final_wording: In a Comunitat Valenciana residential sale, which documents does the law expressly prevent a notary from authorising the deed without, which ones instead affect only the price or the buyer's mortgage, and which merely expose the seller to a penalty after the event?
entries.note: The three-way split the question asks for is exactly the split the statutes make, and it is worth spelling out because sellers are routinely told everything is a blocker. Only one document expressly bars authorisation of the SALE deed: the community-debt certificate (LPH art. 9.1.e), and even that can be waived by the buyer in the deed. The Ley 5/2019 acta previa bars only the LOAN deed, so it is the buyer's mortgage that stalls, not the sale. The energy certificate is an annexation duty with a fine attached, not a bar. The Valencian second-occupation declaración responsable (Decreto 12/2021, still in force — it was Decreto 80/2023 that Ley 5/2025 repealed, not this one) belongs in the third bucket too; I confirmed its continued existence but not its articles, so open it before writing about it.

entries.assertion: Establish whether an agent operating in the Comunitat Valenciana must appear in a public register, when that obligation took effect, what the entry requires of the agent, and exactly how a seller can search it and what the search cannot do.
entries.source_required: The Valencian decree creating the register, plus the Generalitat's own public search facility
entries.source_opened: Iberley reproduction of DECRETO 98/2022, de 29 de julio, del Consell (Registro de Agentes de Intermediación Inmobiliaria de la Comunitat Valenciana), https://www.iberley.es/legislacion/decreto-98-2022-29-julio-consell-regula-registro-agentes-intermediacion-inmobiliaria-comunitat-valenciana-requisitos-inscripcion-27135412 ; Generalitat Valenciana, Conselleria de Vivienda — 'Registros en materia de vivienda' (public RAICV search), https://habitatge.gva.es/es/registres-en-materia-habitatge
entries.locator: Decreto 98/2022, DOGV núm. 9405 de 16.08.2022; entry into force two months after publication, i.e. 16.10.2022. Art. 4.1: the register is 'de titularidad pública, y naturaleza administrativa, gratuito y de carácter obligatorio'. Art. 3 requirements: open establishment to the public (or a physical address in the Comunitat if operating exclusively online), professional civil-liability insurance of €600,000 per claim (€1,000,000 if exclusively telematic), a €60,000 per-establishment annual bond or caution insurance, and professional qualification (agent title, relevant degree, or 200+ accredited training hours). Disposición transitoria primera: one year to register for agents already trading. Public consultation is offered from the Conselleria's 'Registros en materia de vivienda' page
entries.as_of: Decreto 98/2022 in force since 2022-10-16; GVA register page as published at 2026-09-01
entries.final_wording: Establish whether an agent operating in the Comunitat Valenciana must appear in a public register, when that obligation took effect, what the entry requires of the agent, and exactly how a seller can search it and what the search cannot do.
entries.note: All four limbs are answerable. The last one matters most and is the one sector pages omit: entry rests on a declaración responsable by the agent, so a hit in the register proves the agent has declared insurance, a bond, an establishment and a qualification — it is not a competence examination, not a licence, not a solvency check, and not evidence that any of the declared cover is currently in force. Treat a positive result as a minimum threshold, not a recommendation. Caveat on my evidence: DOGV's own PDF and BOE's mirror were unreachable, so the article text came from the Iberley legal database reproduction rather than the DOGV directly; the public-search facility I confirmed on the Generalitat's own site.

entries.final_wording: Which published instruments can and cannot tell a Costa Blanca seller whether holding out for a better offer has paid off, and what do the most recent readings of each show for this province and — where such a series exists at all — for the specific town?
entries.note: Well framed, and the 'cannot' half is the important one. Nothing published measures whether a particular seller's decision to wait paid off, because no series tracks the same property from listing to deed. What the instruments can do is bound the question, and their reach differs sharply: the notarial portal goes down to postcode, the ministry's appraisal series stops at 25,000-inhabitant municipalities, the INE index stops at the autonomous community. The 'where such a series exists at all' hedge is doing real work — for smaller Costa Blanca towns only the portal and notarial figures descend far enough, and neither is official statistics.

entries.assertion: Establish who the law names as taxpayer for the municipal land-value tax on an onerous transfer, whether that changes when the seller is a non-resident individual, and whether a clause agreed between buyer and seller binds the town hall.
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLRHL art. 106 and LGT art. 17
entries.source_opened: BOE — Texto Refundido de la Ley Reguladora de las Haciendas Locales (RDLeg 2/2004), art. 106, https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4214/texto/bloque/a106 ; BOE — Ley 58/2003 General Tributaria, art. 17, https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2003-23186/texto/bloque/a17
entries.locator: TRLRHL art. 106.1.b): on an onerous transfer the contribuyente is the person who transfers the land (the seller). Art. 106.2: 'tendrá la consideración de sujeto pasivo sustituto del contribuyente… que adquiera el terreno… cuando el contribuyente sea una persona física no residente en España.' LGT art. 17.5: 'Los elementos de la obligación tributaria no podrán ser alterados por actos o convenios de los particulares, que no producirán efectos ante la Administración, sin perjuicio de sus consecuencias jurídico-privadas.'
entries.as_of: TRLRHL art. 106 consolidated text current to 2026-09-01 (apartado 3 added by RDL 6/2012 and deleted by RDL 8/2014; apartados 1 and 2 unchanged); LGT art. 17.5 current since renumbering by RDL 20/2011 with effect 2012-01-01
entries.final_wording: Establish who the law names as taxpayer for the municipal land-value tax on an onerous transfer, whether that changes when the seller is a non-resident individual, and whether a clause agreed between buyer and seller binds the town hall.
entries.note: All three limbs are answered squarely by the consolidated texts, and the middle one is the trap. On a sale the seller is the taxpayer; but where that seller is a non-resident INDIVIDUAL, art. 106.2 makes the buyer the sujeto pasivo sustituto — the town hall can pursue the buyer. Note the precise scope: 'persona física no residente en España'. A non-resident company selling does not trigger the substitution, and residence here is Spanish residence, not nationality and not tax residence in some third country. On the third limb, LGT art. 17.5 is explicit — a who-pays clause in the contract has private effects between the parties only and does not bind the administration.

entries.final_wording: Establish which certificates and documents the seller must produce for the sale, who bears the cost of each, and whether there is any the notary is legally barred from proceeding without.
entries.note: Answerable, and the answer to the last limb is: exactly one for the sale deed itself — the community-debt certificate under LPH art. 9.1.e), and the buyer can expressly waive even that. The energy certificate is a duty to annex with a penalty behind it, not a bar. The acta previa under Ley 5/2019 bars only the mortgage deed. On cost allocation the instruction is right to ask separately, because most of it is contractual (art. 1455 Código Civil default and local custom) rather than fixed by statute — the one item the statute does fix is the acta previa, which under Ley 5/2019 art. 15.8 'no generará coste arancelario alguno'. The Valencian second-occupation declaración responsable (Decreto 12/2021, not repealed) should be checked at article level before it is described.

entries.final_wording: Establish, and distinguish, the sums that may leave the price at completion: any statutory withholding on a non-resident's sale, and any voluntary retention a buyer's side asks for — and on what basis each is claimed.
entries.note: The distinction is the right one, but the binary as written is slightly too clean and the answer should say so: there are two statutory deductions, not one. First, the 3% IRNR withholding under art. 25.2, which the buyer must withhold and pay over (modelo 211) whenever the seller acts without a permanent establishment — it is a payment on account, not the tax itself, and the tax on the gain is 19% under art. 25.1.f).3º. Second, where the seller is a non-resident individual, the buyer is the plusvalía sustituto under TRLRHL art. 106.2, so a retention for that is also statutorily grounded, not a favour asked. Genuinely voluntary retentions — IBI, community arrears, unpaid utilities — are contractual, though the buyer has a real reason to ask, because LPH art. 9.1.e) attaches community debts of the current and previous year to the property itself. Keep the five variables apart when applying this: it turns on the seller acting without a permanent establishment and, for plusvalía, on non-residence in Spain of an individual — not on nationality, not on immigration status, and not on tax residence elsewhere.

entries.assertion: That a document issued inside the EU needs no legalisation — Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 lists its scope exhaustively in Article 2(1) (civil-status facts only;
entries.source_required: The Regulation's own Article 2 text

entries.locator: Art. 2(1) enumerates: birth, a person being alive, death, name, marriage (incl. capacity and marital status), divorce/legal separation/annulment, registered partnership (incl. capacity and status), dissolution/legal separation/annulment of a registered partnership, parenthood, adoption, domicile and/or residence, nationality, and absence of a criminal record. entries.as_of: 2026-09-02 (Regulation applicable since 16 February 2019)
entries.final_wording: That a document issued inside the EU needs no legalisation — Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 lists its scope exhaustively in Article 2(1), and that list covers only the facts named there (birth, life, death, name, marriage, divorce, registered partnership, parenthood, adoption, domicile/residence, nationality and absence of a criminal record);
entries.note: The parenthetical 'civil-status facts only' is wrong as written: Article 2(1) also reaches domicile/residence, nationality and absence of a criminal record, none of which is a civil-status fact. The instruction's thrust — that the list is closed and a property document is not on it — survives; the shorthand does not.

entries.final_wording: Which of Decreto 98/2022's requirements for acting as an estate agent in the Comunitat Valenciana actually survive after the TSJCV judgment of January 2025 annulled the qualification, establishment, aval and professional-liability-insurance requirements — and is that judgment now firm or under cassation? entries.assertion: Establish which official instruments publish residential property prices covering Alicante province and its municipalities, precisely what each one measures, and at what geographic level each is published — including which coastal towns are too small to appear at municipal level.
entries.source_required: The publishers' own methodology documents
entries.source_opened: MIVAU, 'Estadística de Valor Tasado de Vivienda. Metodología' (marzo 2025) — https://www.mivau.gob.es/recursos_mfom/comodin/recursos/metodologia_valor_tasado_de_vivienda.pdf ; INE IPV operation page — https://www.ine.es/dyngs/INEbase/es/operacion.htm?c=Estadistica_C&cid=1254736152838&menu=ultiDatos&idp=1254735976607 ; Consejo General del Notariado, Portal Estadístico — https://www.penotariado.com/
entries.locator: MIVAU valor tasado: source = appraisal reports from AEV member firms; quarterly; four table blocks, the fourth being 'Valor medio de vivienda libre de los municipios mayores de 25000 habitantes'; the methodology also notes territorial breakdowns beyond province are limited. INE IPV: notarial transaction data, index numbers base 2025, national and CCAA, Q1 2026 published 8 June 2026. CGN Portal Estadístico: price per m², average surface, average total, number of sales, from notarial deeds; national, CCAA, provincial, municipal, postcode and user-drawn areas; monthly updates.
entries.final_wording: Establish which official instruments publish residential property prices covering Alicante province and its municipalities, precisely what each one measures, and at what geographic level each is published — including which coastal towns are too small to appear at municipal level.
entries.note: Instruction is exactly right and its premise checks out: MIVAU's municipal table has a hard 25,000-inhabitant floor, which excludes a large part of the Costa Blanca resort coast. Three different things get called 'the price': appraisal value (MIVAU), an index of notarial transaction prices (INE IPV), and notarial deed price per m² (CGN portal). entries.assertion: What does Spanish law actually impose on an estate-agency mandate signed by a private seller in the Comunitat Valenciana, what is left entirely to the parties, and which terms have been challenged?
entries.source_required: Civil Code provisions on freedom of contract plus consumer-protection law on unfair terms
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated Código Civil arts. 1255 and 1258 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1889-4763/texto/bloque/art1255 and .../art1258 ; BOE consolidated TRLGDCU (RDLeg 1/2007) art. 82 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2007-20555/texto/bloque/a82
entries.locator: CC art. 1255 (freedom of pacts, unamended since 1889); CC art. 1258 (contracts bind to what good faith, usage and law require); TRLGDCU art. 82.1, in force since 2007-12-01: unfair terms are those 'no negociadas individualmente' that cause 'un desequilibrio importante de los derechos y obligaciones', with art. 82.4 referring to arts. 85–90
entries.final_wording: What does Spanish law actually impose on an estate-agency mandate signed by a private seller in the Comunitat Valenciana, what is left entirely to the parties, and which terms have been challenged?
entries.note: Well-posed and the framing is correct: there is no statute of the estate-agency mandate. It is an atypical contract under CC arts. 1255/1258, so almost everything — duration, exclusivity, fee, when the fee is earned — is left to the parties. The one hard constraint when the seller is a consumer is TRLGDCU arts. 82 and 85–90 on unfair terms, and that is where exclusivity, automatic renewal and penalty clauses get attacked. I did not open any specific judgment, so the 'which terms have been challenged' limb must be researched against actual case law, not asserted.

entries.source_required: LIRPF on transfer value, LGT on evidence of deductible expenses, TRLIRNR on how non-residents compute the gain
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated LIRPF art. 35 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2006-20764/texto/bloque/a35 ; BOE consolidated LGT art. 106 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2003-23186/texto/bloque/a106 ; BOE consolidated TRLIRNR art. 24 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4527/texto/bloque/a24
entries.locator: LIRPF art. 35.2 (in force 2015-01-01): from the transfer value 'se deducirán los gastos y tributos a que se refiere la letra b) del apartado 1 en cuanto resulten satisfechos por el transmitente'. LGT art. 106.4 (in force 2015-10-12): deductible expenses arising from operations by empresarios or profesionales 'deberán justificarse, de forma prioritaria, mediante la factura', and the factura is 'no... un medio de prueba privilegiado'. TRLIRNR art. 24.4 (in force 2015-01-01): the non-resident's gain is computed under the LIRPF rules.
entries.final_wording: Establish what the seller must hold in writing for commission actually paid to count as a deductible cost of the sale, and whether that route differs for a seller taxed as a non-resident.
entries.note: The answer the instruction will find: a proper factura from the agency in the seller's name, plus proof it was actually paid — and the factura alone is not conclusive once AEAT questions it (LGT art. 106.4, second paragraph). On the second limb, watch the trap: the computation route is the SAME for a non-resident because TRLIRNR art. 24.4 imports the LIRPF rules. What differs is the filing and the rate (see id 147), not whether commission is deductible.

entries.assertion: that a non-resident seller deducts selling costs through the same filing, or against the same rate, as a Spanish tax resident
entries.source_required: TRLIRNR rate and filing rules against LIRPF savings-income rates
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4527/texto/bloque/a25 ; BOE consolidated LIRPF art. 66 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2006-20764/texto/bloque/a66 ; AEAT non-resident capital gains page — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/no-residentes/irnr-sin-establecimiento-permanente/cuestiones-especificas-sobre-tributacion-inmuebles/ganancia-patrimonial-derivada-transmision.html
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 25.1.f).3º (in force 2015-01-01): 19% on 'ganancias patrimoniales que se pongan de manifiesto con ocasión de transmisiones de elementos patrimoniales' — a flat rate, declared on Modelo 210. LIRPF art. 66, version in force 2024-12-22: a progressive savings scale (state half 9.5/10.5/11.5/13.5/15, doubled with the autonomic half), declared in the ordinary IRPF return.
entries.final_wording: that a non-resident seller deducts selling costs through the same filing, or against the same rate, as a Spanish tax resident
entries.note: Correct as written and worth keeping: the filing (Modelo 210, one-off, after a 3% Modelo 211 withholding) and the rate (flat 19% vs a progressive savings scale reaching 30%) genuinely differ. But do not let the engine over-extend it — the deduction MECHANISM is identical, because TRLIRNR art. 24.4 applies the LIRPF rules to the non-resident's gain. The difference is the wrapper, not the arithmetic.

entries.assertion: Establish, from AEAT's own material and the IRPF/IRNR rules it cites, what qualifies as 'inversiones y mejoras' addable to acquisition value, and whether any category of spending is expressly excluded — do not infer the boundary from a builder's or blog's description of it.
entries.source_required: AEAT's own manual plus the statutory article it rests on
entries.source_opened: AEAT, Manual práctico de Renta 2025, Capítulo 11, 'Reglas generales de cálculo' — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/ayuda/manuales-videos-folletos/manuales-practicos/irpf-2025/c11-ganancias-perdidas-patrimoniales/determinacion-importe-ganancias-perdidas-patrimon-generales/derivadas-transmisiones-onerosas-lucrativas/reglas-generales-calculo.html ; BOE consolidated LIRPF art. 35 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2006-20764/texto/bloque/a35
entries.locator: LIRPF art. 35.1.b): 'El coste de las inversiones y mejoras efectuadas en los bienes adquiridos y los gastos y tributos inherentes a la adquisición, excluidos los intereses, que hubieran sido satisfechos por el adquirente'. AEAT Manual de Renta 2025: 'sin que se computen, a estos efectos, los gastos de conservación y reparación'.
entries.final_wording: Establish, from AEAT's own material and the IRPF/IRNR rules it cites, what qualifies as 'inversiones y mejoras' addable to acquisition value, and whether any category of spending is expressly excluded — do not infer the boundary from a builder's or blog's description of it.
entries.note: Sound, and the 'expressly excluded' limb has a precise answer with a subtlety worth carrying: interest is excluded by the words of the statute, whereas the conservation-and-repair exclusion is AEAT's own formulation in the Manual, not literal statutory text. Copy should attribute each to the right source rather than presenting both as 'the law says'.

entries.assertion: Establish separately how a seller's own selling costs (agency commission, certificates, notary share, plusvalía) are treated in the calculation, and confirm whether that is the same mechanism as improvements or a different one.
entries.source_required: LIRPF art. 35 paragraphs 1 and 2
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated LIRPF art. 35 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2006-20764/texto/bloque/a35 ; AEAT Manual práctico de Renta 2025, Capítulo 11 — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/ayuda/manuales-videos-folletos/manuales-practicos/irpf-2025/c11-ganancias-perdidas-patrimoniales/determinacion-importe-ganancias-perdidas-patrimon-generales/derivadas-transmisiones-onerosas-lucrativas/reglas-generales-calculo.html
entries.locator: LIRPF art. 35.1.b) adds improvements and acquisition costs TO the valor de adquisición; art. 35.2 deducts 'los gastos y tributos... en cuanto resulten satisfechos por el transmitente' FROM the valor de transmisión
entries.final_wording: Establish separately how a seller's own selling costs (agency commission, certificates, notary share, plusvalía) are treated in the calculation, and confirm whether that is the same mechanism as improvements or a different one.
entries.note: The instruction is right to force the separation, and the answer is that they are two different mechanisms operating on two different sides of the subtraction — improvements raise the acquisition value, selling costs lower the transfer value. The arithmetic effect on the gain is similar, which is exactly why writers merge them; the documentary and timing requirements are not the same.

entries.assertion: Establish whether the position differs for a seller filing under IRPF and one filing Modelo 210 as a non-resident, and what happens where the work was carried out by a previous owner or before an inheritance.
entries.source_required: TRLIRNR art. 24 on how the non-resident gain is computed, plus LIRPF arts. 35 and 36
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR art. 24 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4527/texto/bloque/a24 ; BOE consolidated LIRPF arts. 35 and 36 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2006-20764/texto/bloque/a35 and .../a36 ; AEAT non-resident capital gains page — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/no-residentes/irnr-sin-establecimiento-permanente/cuestiones-especificas-sobre-tributacion-inmuebles/ganancia-patrimonial-derivada-transmision.html
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 24.4 (in force 2015-01-01) applies the LIRPF Título III, Capítulo II, Sección 4ª rules to the non-resident's gain; LIRPF art. 35.1.b) counts improvements 'que hubieran sido satisfechos por el adquirente'; LIRPF art. 36 (version in force 2021-07-11) sets acquisition value on a lucrative acquisition at the Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones value, capped at market value
entries.final_wording: Establish whether the position differs for a seller filing under IRPF and one filing Modelo 210 as a non-resident, and what happens where the work was carried out by a previous owner or before an inheritance.
entries.note: Both limbs are answerable and both contain traps. Filing: Modelo 210 vs the IRPF return, flat 19% vs the savings scale — but the same computation rules, because art. 24.4 imports them. Reliefs are the real divergence and must be checked separately against the TRLIRNR disposiciones adicionales rather than assumed. Previous owner: art. 35.1.b) only counts spending 'satisfechos por el adquirente', and on an inheritance art. 36 resets the acquisition value to the ISD value — so a deceased owner's renovation does not add to the heir's base. Do not let content promise otherwise.

entries.assertion: Do not assume a foreign owner is a non-resident.
entries.source_required: The statutory test of Spanish tax residence
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated LIRPF art. 9 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2006-20764/texto/bloque/a9
entries.locator: LIRPF art. 9.1, original text in force since 2007-01-01: residence where (a) 'permanezca más de 183 días, durante el año natural, en territorio español' or (b) 'radique en España el núcleo principal o la base de sus actividades o intereses económicos', with a rebuttable presumption from the residence of spouse and minor children
entries.final_wording: Do not assume a foreign owner is a non-resident.
entries.note: Correct and important. Nationality appears nowhere in the test — a Dutch or British owner living on the Costa Blanca for more than 183 days is a Spanish tax resident and files IRPF, not Modelo 210, which flips the rate, the filing and the available reliefs. Keep the five variables apart: nationality, immigration status, Spanish residence, Spanish tax residence, country of tax residence.

entries.assertion: Establish whether any published, sourced evidence exists for Alicante province on how unregistered surface area affects a mortgage valuation or an achieved sale price;
entries.source_required: A published study quantifying the effect, plus the valuation rules that create the mechanism
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated Orden ECO/805/2003, arts. 7, 8, 10 and 11 — https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2003-7253/texto/bloque/a7 , .../a8 , .../a10 , .../a11 (no study found; nothing quantifying a price effect for Alicante province was located)
entries.locator: Orden ECO/805/2003 art. 7.2.a): the valuer must identify the property physically 'comprobando si su superficie y demás características coinciden con la descripción que conste en la documentación'. Art. 11.a) (version in force 2025-08-12, as amended by Orden ECM/599/2025): an 'advertencia' arises where there are 'discrepancias entre la realidad física del inmueble y sus descripciones registral o catastral'. Art. 8.1 requires registral certification/nota simple and cadastral information dated within three months; art. 10.1.d) turns their absence into a 'condicionante'.
entries.final_wording: Establish whether any published, sourced evidence exists for Alicante province on how unregistered surface area affects a mortgage valuation or an achieved sale price;
entries.note: The instruction is right to demand evidence, and the honest finding is that none exists: no publisher quantifies a price or valuation effect of unregistered surface in Alicante province. What can be stated with a citation is the mechanism, not a number — the valuer is obliged to compare surface against the registral and cadastral description and to record a formal advertencia when they diverge, which is how the discrepancy reaches the lender's file. Content must stop there and not invent a percentage.

entries.assertion: Establish the current Comunitat Valenciana position on the second-occupancy licence or declaración responsable following the 2025 legislative change — name the operative instrument, and confirm from the Generalitat's own text whether it is required at the deed rather than relying on law-firm summaries.
entries.source_required: Disposición derogatoria of Ley 5/2025 (Generalitat Valenciana) as published in BOE, plus the Generalitat's own housing page

III tít. VI of Ley 8/2010, and the Orden of 15/05/2015 — Decreto 12/2021 is NOT in that list). GVA page: «En virtud de la Disposición derogatoria única de la Ley 5/2025, de 30 de mayo… queda derogado el Decreto 80/2023, de 26 de mayo», and separately lists «Revisión del Decreto 12/2021, de 22 de enero, del Consell»
entries.as_of: Ley 5/2025 published BOE 12/06/2025; GVA page read 2026-09-02
entries.final_wording: Establish the current Comunitat Valenciana position on the second-occupancy declaración responsable. The operative instrument is still Decreto 12/2021, de 22 de enero, del Consell — it was NOT touched by the 2025 legislative change. What Ley 5/2025 (DD única, g) repealed was Decreto 80/2023 on design and quality of dwellings, which is a different subject; the Generalitat's own page confirms Decreto 12/2021 remains in force and is under review, and that the Orden of 7 December 2009 on design and quality revives in Decreto 80/2023's place. Separately confirm, from the Generalitat's own text, whether the declaración responsable is required at the deed rather than relying on law-firm summaries.
entries.note: This is the landmine the brief itself walked into: the instruction presupposes that 'the 2025 legislative change' hit the second-occupancy regime. It did not. On the deed question I could not close the loop from a Generalitat-published full text of Decreto 12/2021 (the DOGV PDF endpoint returned HTML, not the document); a secondary summary of art. 6 says the declaración responsable is required on each transmission of ownership and for new water/gas/electricity contracts, but no Spanish state instrument makes it a notarial blocker in the way LPH art. 9.1.e is. Treat 'required at the deed' as OPEN until the DOGV text of Decreto 12/2021 art. 6 is read directly.

entries.assertion: Nobody publishes what a new kitchen adds to a sale price on the Costa Blanca.
entries.source_required: A published, primary-sourced measurement (registry, notarial, INE, MIVAU or peer-reviewed) of renovation effect on achieved sale price in Alicante province — or a documented absence
entries.source_opened: Searched and reviewed the available published material; the only Costa Blanca-specific figures found are vendor and agency marketing pages (kitchen-fitting and estate-agency blogs) and a consumer-magazine analysis. No registry, notarial, INE or MIVAU series measuring renovation effect on achieved price was located. Instruments checked for such a breakdown and found not to carry one: Colegio de Registradores, Estadística Registral Inmobiliaria 4T 2025 — https://www.registradores.org/documents/d/guest/eri_4t_2025 ; Consejo General del Notariado / Colegio Notarial de Valencia, 'Compraventa de Inmuebles de la provincia de Alicante', extraction 13/11/2025 — https://valencia.notariado.org/portal/documents/81893/4712529/
entries.locator: ERI 4T 2025 methodology section (pp. 116–118) lists its dimensions: price index of repeated sales, mean price per m², counts, nationality, dwelling type, surface — no renovation or works variable. Notarial Alicante report, 'Condiciones Particulares' (final page): counting is on act 0501 compraventa de inmuebles, objects vivienda-piso/unifamiliar libre or protegida — no works or refurbishment variable
entries.as_of: ERI reference period 4T 2025; notarial report extraction date 13/11/2025; searches run 2026-09-02
entries.final_wording: No published, primary-sourced measurement of what a new kitchen adds to a Costa Blanca sale price could be found — the percentages that circulate come from kitchen-fitting and estate-agency marketing pages, not from any registry, notarial or statistical series.
entries.note: 'Nobody publishes' is wrong as written, and wrong in a way that will get the piece caught: figures ARE published and are easy to find (one Costa Blanca page claims 'up to 15%', others 80–120% of spend). What does not exist is a measurement. The honest claim is about the absence of primary measurement, not the absence of numbers. Neither the registry nor the notarial series carries a renovation variable at all, so the gap is structural, not just unsearched.

entries.final_wording: Establish whether any published, primary-sourced study measures the effect of specific pre-sale works on achieved sale price or time to sell in Alicante province.
entries.note: Well-posed, and the answer on this pass is no. Neither primary Alicante instrument records a works/refurbishment variable, and 'time to sell' is not a field in either — the registry series measures registered sales, the notarial series measures deeds, and neither observes listing dates. Anyone answering this must state that absence rather than substituting a national or marketing figure.

entries.assertion: For a residential sale in Alicante province completing in 2026, what sits between the agreed price and the seller's net receipt: which amounts are deducted or withheld at or around completion, which are a final cost, which are a payment on account that is later settled or refunded — and what, if anything, differs for a seller who is tax-resident in Spain versus one who is not?
entries.source_required: Consolidated TRLIRNR and TRLRHL, plus Agencia Tributaria's own guidance on the retention and refund route
entries.source_opened: BOE, consolidated RDLeg 5/2004 (TRLIRNR) — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4527 ; BOE, consolidated RDLeg 2/2004 (TRLRHL) — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4214 ; Agencia Tributaria, 'Ganancia patrimonial derivada de la transmisión' (IRNR sin establecimiento permanente) — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/no-residentes/irnr-sin-establecimiento-permanente/cuestiones-especificas-sobre-tributacion-inmuebles/ganancia-patrimonial-derivada-transmision.html
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 25.2 (3% retention by the acquirer, 'en concepto de pago a cuenta'); art. 25.1.f).3º (19% on the gain); TRLRHL art. 106.1.b) (seller is the plusvalía taxpayer on an onerous transfer) and art. 106.2 (buyer is sustituto del contribuyente when the seller is a non-resident individual); AEAT page (retention 3%, modelo 211 within one month, modelo 210 by the seller, refund of the excess)
entries.as_of: TRLIRNR consolidated to 25/05/2023; TRLRHL consolidated to 03/06/2026; AEAT page read 2026-09-02
entries.final_wording: For a residential sale in Alicante province completing in 2026, what sits between the agreed price and the seller's net receipt: which amounts are deducted or withheld at or around completion, which are a final cost, which are a payment on account that is later settled or refunded — and what, if anything, differs for a seller who is tax-resident in Spain versus one who is not?
entries.note: The question is correctly framed and its central distinction is real: the 3% is a payment on account (recoverable), plusvalía is a final cost, and the resident/non-resident line is the operative one. The trap the piece must not fall into is the one the question itself avoids — the difference turns on TAX RESIDENCE, not on nationality or on holding a residence permit. Note also that for a Spanish tax resident there is no 3% retention at all.
