entries.note: The citation is out of date. Ley 1/2019 amended the old LOTUP (Ley 5/2014); that law was superseded by the texto refundido approved by Decreto Legislativo 1/2021, which is what is in force now. Citing 'LOTUP as amended by Ley 1/2019' will send anyone checking to a repealed statute and to the wrong article numbers. The AFO caveat is correct and worth keeping. The assertion is truncated ('and that'), so its final clause could not be assessed. Practical point for copy: art. 230 is a route to regularisation, not an automatic cure — it needs a pleno declaration, a paisajística study, works, and a further occupation licence within four years.

Disposición transitoria: 'En tanto los ayuntamientos no adopten las medidas adecuadas para la puesta en marcha de la licencia de ocupación, será de aplicación la legislación autonómica vigente en materia de obtención y expedición de la cédula de habitabilidad'; preamble: renewal of the licencia de ocupación required on second or subsequent transfer after ten years. TRLOTUP: the string 'segunda ocupación' does not appear anywhere in the consolidated text; art. 214 is 'Actuaciones promovidas por particulares' in suelo no urbanizable. Valencia city procedure cites Ley 3/2004, Decreto 12/2021 (de 22 de enero, del Consell), Decreto Legislativo 1/2021 and Decreto 151/2009 — and does not mention the cédula de habitabilidad.
entries.final_wording: Second occupation in the Comunitat Valenciana is a DECLARACIÓN RESPONSABLE under Decreto 12/2021, de 22 de enero, del Consell, developing Ley 3/2004 (LOFCE) — not TRLOTUP art. 214, which governs private works in suelo no urbanizable and says nothing about occupation. Some municipalities' ordinances still require an express licencia de segunda ocupación, so establish which applies in the town in question. On the cédula: Ley 3/2004 replaced it with the municipal licencia de ocupación, but the law took effect on 2 January 2005 and its transitional provision kept the cédula regime alive in each municipality until that town brought the occupation licence into operation — so say 'replaced by Ley 3/2004, phased in from 2005', not 'not issued since 2004'. Also check outstanding community debts and derramas, and pending urbanisation charges under a PAI.
entries.note: Three separate errors. (1) The article reference is wrong — 'segunda ocupación' appears nowhere in the TRLOTUP; the surviving cross-reference to an art. 214 belongs to the OLD Ley 5/2014, cited in Decreto 12/2021's scope clause, and repeating it against the current text misleads. (2) The 2004 date is a year early and ignores a transitional period that ran municipality by municipality. (3) Decreto 12/2021 must be named as the operative instrument. The community-debt and PAI limbs are sound research items but I opened no source on them in this pass.

entries.assertion: The buyer's actual protection: what an arras contract clause can recover, and what is lost if the defect is found after signing
entries.source_required: Consolidated Código Civil on arras and on hidden defects
entries.source_opened: BOE, texto consolidado del Código Civil — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1889-4763 (arts. 1454, 1484, 1490 via the BOE legislación-consolidada API)
entries.locator: Art. 1454 CC (original 1889 wording, never amended): 'Si hubiesen mediado arras o señal en el contrato de compra y venta, podrá rescindirse el contrato allanándose el comprador a perderlas, o el vendedor a devolverlas duplicadas.' Art. 1484 CC (current wording from Ley 11/2021 era, in force 05/01/2022): seller liable for hidden defects making the thing unfit, but not for defects that were manifest or visible, nor for non-visible defects where the buyer is a professional who should easily have known them. Art. 1490 CC (unamended since 1889): 'Las acciones que emanan de lo dispuesto en los cinco artículos precedentes se extinguirán a los seis meses, contados desde la entrega de la cosa vendida.'
entries.final_wording: The buyer's actual protection: what an arras contract clause can recover (art. 1454 CC — arras penitenciales: the buyer who walks loses the deposit, the seller who walks returns it doubled), and what is lost if the defect is found after signing (arts. 1484-1490 CC saneamiento por vicios ocultos, with the action extinguished six months from delivery, and no remedy at all for defects that were visible or that a professional buyer should have spotted)
entries.note: Both limbs are answerable from the consolidated Civil Code and the answers are hard-edged and useful to a buyer. Two cautions for copy: art. 1454's doubling rule applies to arras PENITENCIALES — the contract's own wording decides which kind of arras were agreed, and confirmatorias or penales behave differently. And the six-month limit in art. 1490 is short enough that it is the single most valuable fact in the piece.

entries.assertion: The Registro de Agentes de Intermediación Inmobiliaria de la Comunitat Valenciana under Decreto 98/2022 (published DOGV 16 Aug 2022, in force 16 Oct 2022): that it is public, free and mandatory, and exactly how a buyer searches it today — the current GVA/habitatge URL, whether a working public search by name, province and municipality exists, and how long it really takes

DF 2ª: in force two months after DOGV publication of 16 Aug 2022 → 16 Oct 2022. Live tool, page title 'Consulta del registro de agentes de intermediación inmobiliaria', linked from habitatge.gva.es as 'Registro Público de Agentes de Intermediación Inmobiliaria'. Form controls present, read from the DOM on 1 Sep 2026: select W_PROVINCIA (TODAS/TOTES, ALICANTE/ALACANT, CASTELLÓN/CASTELLÓ, VALENCIA/VALÈNCIA), select W_MUNICIPIO (populates on province selection — TODOS/TOTS, AGOST, AGRES, AIGÜES, ALACANT/ALICANTE, ALBATERA, ALCALALÍ...), and a single 'Consultar' button. There is NO name or NIF search field.
entries.as_of: 2026-09-01 (search tool inspected live)
entries.final_wording: The Registro de Agentes de Intermediación Inmobiliaria de la Comunitat Valenciana under Decreto 98/2022 (DOGV nº 9405, 16 Aug 2022; in force 16 Oct 2022) is public, free of charge and obligatory (art. 4.1). A working public search does exist and is linked from habitatge.gva.es as 'Registro Público de Agentes de Intermediación Inmobiliaria'. It searches by PROVINCE and MUNICIPALITY ONLY — there is no search-by-name or by-NIF field — so a buyer browses the list for their town and looks for the agency in it, rather than typing the agency's name in.
entries.note: Dates and the public/free/obligatory character verified in the decree. The 'search by name' limb is wrong and matters: the whole point of the piece is telling a buyer how to check a specific agency, and the tool does not let them look one up by name. The realistic answer to 'how long it really takes' is therefore 'as long as it takes to read the list for your municipality', which for a town like Torrevieja is not a two-second check. I inspected the form's controls directly; I did not run a query, so I have not verified what fields the RESULTS show.

entries.assertion: The concrete disclosures Decreto 98/2022 requires an agent to make: registration number, insurer name and policy number (or guarantor and aval reference), stated in the nota de encargo or mandate and given to anyone who asks — plus what the solvency requirement actually is today, given that Sentencia TSJCV 706/2024 of 13 Dec 2024 (CNMC appeal) annulled the fixed aval and insurance minimums in art.
entries.source_required: Decreto 98/2022 for the article carrying the amounts, and the TSJCV judgment (or a reliable report of it) for what was annulled and whether it is final
entries.source_opened: Decreto 98/2022 art. 3 (via https://www.iberley.es/legislacion/decreto-98-2022-29-julio-consell-regula-registro-agentes-intermediacion-inmobiliaria-comunitat-valenciana-requisitos-inscripcion-27135412); report of the judgment at LegalToday — https://www.legaltoday.com/practica-juridica/derecho-publico/derecho-administrativo/el-tsjcv-estima-un-recurso-de-la-cnmc-y-anula-varios-requisitos-del-registro-de-agentes-de-intermediacion-inmobiliaria-de-la-comunidad-valenciana-2025-01-20/
entries.locator: Decreto 98/2022 art. 3 'Requisitos, garantías y seguros para ejercer la actividad' — carries both the minimum aval / seguro de caución (60.000 €; 300.000 € for exclusively telematic agents) and the professional civil liability insurance (100.000 €; 600.000 € telematic), AND the disclosure duty in its final paragraph. TSJCV, Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo, Sección 4ª, judgment of 13 December 2024 on a CNMC appeal: annulled the fixed aval/insurance minimums and further requirements for want of the qualified motivation the Supreme Court requires; the report states the judgment 'puede ser recurrida en casación ante el Tribunal Supremo' — i.e. NOT final when reported. No sentencia number, recurso number or ECLI obtained from a primary source.
entries.as_of: 2025-01-20 (date of the report); firmeza not established as at 2026-09-01
entries.final_wording: The concrete disclosures Decreto 98/2022 requires are all in ARTICLE 3: the agent must state the guarantee/insurance details (insurer or guarantor, policy or aval reference) in the nota de encargo or contrato de mandato and give them to anyone who asks. On solvency, the fixed minimums that art. 3 originally set (60.000 € aval, 300.000 € for exclusively telematic agents; 100.000 € professional liability, 600.000 € telematic) were annulled by the TSJCV (Sala CA, Sección 4ª) on 13 December 2024 on a CNMC appeal, for lack of the qualified motivation required. So do NOT publish any of those four figures as a current requirement. The disclosure duty and the obligatory character of the register were not annulled. Before publishing, confirm from CENDOJ whether that judgment is now firme and whether any replacement rule has been made.
entries.note: Assertion is truncated at 'in art.' so the article it names cannot be checked — but the amounts and the disclosure duty both live in art. 3, not in a separate article. Two gaps I could not close and will not paper over: I did not open the judgment itself (no ECLI or recurso number), and I found no source establishing whether it became firme or whether the Consell has re-enacted the minimums with better reasoning. Both must be settled before any figure is published.

entries.assertion: The jurisdictional edge: what applies to an agency trading in Murcia region rather than Alicante province, and whether any national qualification requirement exists for estate agents in Spain
entries.source_required: Consolidated national statute on access to the estate-agency profession, plus any Región de Murcia register instrument
entries.source_opened: BOE, texto consolidado del Real Decreto-ley 4/2000, de 23 de junio, de Medidas Urgentes de Liberalización en el Sector Inmobiliario y Transportes — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2000-11834
entries.locator: Art. 3 RDL 4/2000, 'Condiciones para el ejercicio de la actividad de intermediación inmobiliaria': 'Las actividades enumeradas en el artículo 1 del Decreto 3248/1969... podrán ser ejercidas libremente sin necesidad de estar en posesión de título alguno ni de pertenencia a ningún Colegio oficial.' Article not shown as amended or annulled (arts. 1 and 3.3 of the same RDL were affected by TC rulings; art. 3 was not). No Región de Murcia source opened.
entries.final_wording: National limb (verified): there is NO national qualification requirement for estate agents in Spain — art. 3 of Real Decreto-ley 4/2000 provides that real-estate intermediation may be exercised freely, without any qualification and without belonging to any professional college. Regulation is autonomic, which is why the Comunitat Valenciana register exists at all. Murcia limb (NOT verified): whether the Región de Murcia operates an equivalent mandatory register must be checked against a Región de Murcia source before anything is published about it — no such source was opened here.
entries.note: Half the question is answered from primary law and half is genuinely open. I am not asserting that Murcia has no register; I am recording that I did not open a Murcia source. This is a live risk for the copy because Costa Cálida and Costa Blanca sit either side of that line and agencies routinely trade across it.

entries.assertion: How widely the register is actually complied with, and whether the Generalitat has published enforcement or sanction data — so the piece does not claim an unregistered agency is automatically a fraud

entries.locator: habitatge.gva.es 'Registros en materia de vivienda' lists the register and links a public consultation form (province + municipality). No compliance statistics, inspection totals or sanction resolutions are published there.
entries.final_wording: No published Generalitat data on compliance rates, inspections or sanctions under Decreto 98/2022 was found. State that plainly rather than estimating a compliance rate. The editorial caution stands and is independently well founded: art. 3 of RDL 4/2000 means estate agency is a free profession nationally, and the TSJCV annulled Decreto 98/2022's fixed solvency minimums in December 2024, so absence from the register is a reason to ask questions, not evidence of fraud.
entries.note: The instruction's own instinct is right and the guardrail is supportable from two primary sources even though the compliance data is not. Do not let a generated piece fill this gap with a plausible-sounding percentage.

entries.assertion: The real stage-by-stage timeline with sources: NIE application, opening a Spanish bank account, reserva to arras, arras to completion at notary, non-resident mortgage approval, and inscription at the Registro de la Propiedad after signing — with realistic ranges rather than a single number
entries.source_required: A published legal deadline or service standard for each stage — Ley Hipotecaria for registration, Reglamento de Extranjería / Policía Nacional for the NIE, and lender or supervisory sources for mortgage timing
entries.source_opened: BOE, texto consolidado de la Ley Hipotecaria (Decreto de 8 de febrero de 1946) — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1946-2453 (art. 18 via the BOE legislación-consolidada API)
entries.locator: Art. 18 LH, current wording from Ley 24/2005 (BOE-A-2005-19005, in force 20/11/2005): 'El plazo máximo para inscribir el documento será de quince días contados desde la fecha del asiento de presentación' — with the clock restarting on return, subsanación or inscription of a prior title, and an extension of up to fifteen further days available from the Dirección General on accredited extraordinary grounds. No source opened for NIE, bank account, reserva/arras or mortgage-approval timings.
entries.final_wording: One stage has a hard published deadline and should be stated as such: after signing, the registrar has a MAXIMUM OF FIFTEEN DAYS from the asiento de presentación to inscribe the title (art. 18 Ley Hipotecaria), with the clock restarting if the title is withdrawn, has correctable defects, or waits behind an earlier title, and an extension of up to fifteen further days available on accredited extraordinary grounds. The other stages — NIE, bank account, reserva to arras, arras to completion, non-resident mortgage approval — have no published legal deadline or official service standard that I could open. Either source each one to a named authority at generation time, or describe them without numbers.
entries.note: The instruction is right to demand ranges rather than a single number, but only the registration limb is currently sourceable to primary law. The others are exactly where invented 'typically 4-6 weeks' figures get manufactured. Note also that art. 18's fifteen days is the registrar's calificación/inscription window, not the elapsed time from the notary appointment to a registered title — do not let copy conflate the two.

entries.assertion: Whether any published data supports a typical or average purchase duration for foreign buyers in Alicante province — and if none exists, say so rather than inventing an average

entries.source_opened: Colegio de Registradores ERI 2T 2026 — https://www.registradores.org/documents/d/guest/eri_2t_2026 (full 122-page contents index reviewed)
entries.locator: ERI pub. nº 89 (Aug 2026) contents: repeat-sales price index, average price per m², number of registered purchases, buyer nationality, collective vs single-family split, surface area, new mortgage credit volume/amount/rates/duration, mortgage quota vs salary cost, certificaciones hipotecarias, daciones en pago, methodology. There is no transaction-duration series, and nothing crossing duration with buyer nationality or with Alicante province.
entries.final_wording: No published series on typical or average purchase duration for foreign buyers in Alicante province was found. The Registradores ERI — the most granular official property series for this province — publishes nothing on transaction duration at all. Say so explicitly rather than inventing an average, and do not substitute a conveyancing firm's marketing estimate for a statistic.
entries.note: I checked the most likely producer's full contents and found no such series; I did not exhaustively survey every producer, so this is 'not found', not 'proved not to exist'. Either way the instruction's own fallback is the correct behaviour and should be enforced, because this is a question buyers ask constantly and therefore a high-pressure spot for a fabricated number.

entries.assertion: The genuine trade-off levers and what each is worth in euros: moving a few kilometres inland, an older property needing renovation, a smaller plot, a resale instead of a new build, a different municipality with the same climate
entries.source_required: A price series granular enough to price a municipality-to-municipality or inland-vs-coastal move, and a new-build vs resale differential for the province
entries.source_opened: Colegio de Registradores ERI 2T 2026 — https://www.registradores.org/documents/d/guest/eri_2t_2026
entries.locator: ERI pub. nº 89 (Aug 2026), Q2 2026, provincial average price table: Alicante/Alacant total 2.267 €/m², NEW-BUILD 2.780 €/m², USED 2.153 €/m² (quarterly); interannual 2.194 / 2.799 / 2.054 €/m². Only ONE of the five levers — resale vs new build — is priceable from this source (roughly a 630 €/m² gap on the quarterly figures). No municipal, inland-vs-coastal, plot-size or condition-adjusted price series exists in the ERI.
entries.final_wording: Only one of these levers can currently be priced from an official source: resale versus new build in Alicante province, where Registradores' Q2 2026 average was 2.153 €/m² used against 2.780 €/m² new-build. The other four — moving a few kilometres inland, an older property needing renovation, a smaller plot, a different municipality with the same climate — have no official price series behind them at that granularity. Either derive them from the agency's own completed-sale data and label them as such, or describe the direction of the trade-off without attaching euro figures.
entries.note: This instruction as written invites five euro figures where the data supports one. The new-build/used gap is real and citable, with the series type named (Registradores average price per m² of registered transactions, Q2 2026). Everything else at municipal or sub-municipal level would have to be invented or laundered from portal asking prices, which are not transaction prices.

entries.source_opened: Colegio de Registradores ERI 2T 2026 — https://www.registradores.org/documents/d/guest/eri_2t_2026
entries.locator: ERI publicación trimestral nº 89, published August 2026, ref. period Q2 2026, provincial average price of registered purchases. Alicante/Alacant: 2.267 €/m² total (+2,4% on the quarter), new-build 2.780 €/m² (−0,1%), used 2.153 €/m² (+3,3%); interannual 2.194 €/m² (+11,7%), new 2.799 €/m² (+10,7%), used 2.054 €/m² (+12,2%). Alicante capital 2.219 €/m² (+13,3% interannual). National context: IPVVR repeat-sales index +3,14% on the quarter and +16,7% on the year, a new historical maximum. Alicante purchase volumes fell: 12.298 in Q2 2026 (−2,5% on the quarter), 51.392 interannual (−5,3%).
entries.final_wording: Yes — and the movement is large enough that any stated Alicante figure must carry its date. Registradores' Q2 2026 provincial average was 2.267 €/m², up 2,4% in a single quarter and 11,7% on the year (used stock 2.153 €/m², +12,2% year on year), while purchase volumes fell 5,3% year on year. At that rate a price quoted without a quarter is misleading within about three months. Always publish the figure with its quarter, its producer and its series type (registered-transaction average price per m²), and re-check when the next quarterly ERI appears.
entries.note: TIME-SENSITIVE because the ERI is republished every quarter — publication nº 89 came out in August 2026 for Q2 2026, so a Q3 edition is due around November 2026 and will move these numbers. Also flag the divergence for copy: prices up double digits while transaction volumes fall — a piece that quotes only the price direction tells half the story.

entries.assertion: Your home has three published price tags on the Costa Blanca - only one of them official, and only one of them money a buyer actually handed over.
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLCI (RDLeg 1/2004) disposición final tercera 'Valor de referencia' https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4163/texto/bloque/df ; BOE consolidated Ley Hipotecaria art. 221 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1946-2453/texto/bloque/a221 ; INE standardised methodological report, Estadística de Transmisión de Derechos de la Propiedad https://www.ine.es/dynt3/metadatos/es/RespuestaPrint.html?oper=7
entries.locator: TRLCI DF3ª (valor de referencia fixed by the Dirección General del Catastro, published annually in the BOE and permanently consultable per property in the Sede Electrónica del Catastro); Ley Hipotecaria art. 221 (the Registro is public only to those with a 'interés conocido'); INE ETDP methodology (source = Registros de la Propiedad via CORPME, 2004 convenio)
entries.final_wording: Your Costa Blanca home carries more than one price, and they are different instruments rather than versions of one number: the asking price the agency publishes (private, not official); the Catastro's valor de referencia (official — set by the Dirección General del Catastro and consultable for a specific property); and official transaction-price statistics built from what buyers actually paid (INE, Colegio de Registradores, Notariado, MIVAU), which are published only as area averages and never as a figure attached to your address. Two of the three are official, and none of them is a published record of what a buyer paid for your particular home.
entries.note: Two failures. (1) 'Only one of them official' is wrong: the Catastro's valor de referencia is an official administrative value under TRLCI DF3ª, AND the transaction-price series (INE IPV/ETDP, Registradores ERI, MIVAU valor tasado) are official statistics. At least two of the three are official. (2) 'Money a buyer actually handed over' is not published as a price tag on your home at all — registered/notarised prices reach the public only as area aggregates; the Registro itself is open only to someone with a proven legitimate interest (LH art. 221). The hook's real, defensible point is that the three are different instruments, which is what gid 4 already protects.

entries.assertion: [NEVER assume] that municipal-level official data exists for smaller Costa Blanca towns — some publishers only disaggregate above a population threshold, so check before naming a town.
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: MIVAU/Ministerio de Transportes 'Valor tasado de la vivienda' series, mirrored dataset record 'Valor tasado de la vivienda libre por municipios de más de 25.000 habitantes' https://datos.gob.es/es/catalogo/a13002908-valor-tasado-de-la-vivienda-libre-por-municipios-de-mas-de-25-00-habitantes-total-base-20054 ; INE Índice de Precios de Vivienda methodology https://www.ine.es/daco/daco42/ipv/metodologia2015.pdf (via INE IPV metadata) ; INE ETDP standardised methodological report https://www.ine.es/dynt3/metadatos/es/RespuestaPrint.html?oper=7
entries.locator: MIVAU 'Valor tasado de vivienda libre' — municipal breakdown published only for municipios de más de 25.000 habitantes; INE IPV — published for Spain and the 17 CCAA plus Ceuta and Melilla, not by province or municipality; INE ETDP — transmission counts do go down to municipality
entries.final_wording: Never assume municipal-level official data exists for smaller Costa Blanca towns, and never assume one threshold covers all of it: MIVAU's valor tasado publishes municipal figures only for municipalities over 25,000 inhabitants, INE's Índice de Precios de Vivienda never goes below autonomous community, while INE's transmission counts do reach municipality level. Check the specific series before naming a town, and check prices and counts separately.
entries.note: Sound prohibition, and the factual premise behind it checks out with a useful nuance the writer needs: the threshold is per-series, not universal. MIVAU's appraisal-price series stops at 25,000 inhabitants, which excludes many Costa Blanca towns. INE's IPV never goes below autonomous community — so it can never support any Alicante or town-level price claim. INE's ETDP does publish transmission counts by municipality. So 'check before naming a town' must mean check the specific series, and counts and prices must be checked separately.

entries.assertion: There is an administrative value attached to your property that you never commissioned and cannot see on your deed — find out what it governs and what it does not
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLCI (RDLeg 1/2004), disposición final tercera 'Valor de referencia' https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4163/texto/bloque/df
entries.locator: TRLCI disposición final tercera, in the wording given by art. 14.8 of Ley 11/2021 de 9 de julio: 'La Dirección General del Catastro determinará de forma objetiva y con el límite del valor de mercado... el valor de referencia'; approved annually by resolution, published by edict in the Sede Electrónica del Catastro before 30 October, with a BOE notice in the first 20 days of December, and permanently consultable because it is not personal data
entries.final_wording: There is an administrative value attached to your property that you never commissioned and cannot see on your deed — find out what it governs and what it does not
entries.note: Every element holds. The valor de referencia is set unilaterally by the Dirección General del Catastro from notarised sale prices with a ministerial minoración factor, so the owner never commissions it; it is not an element of the deed of sale; and it is nonetheless attached to the specific property and publicly consultable. The hook only asserts existence and invites the reader to learn its scope, which is the right shape — it does not claim what the value governs, so nothing here needs the ITP/ISD tax-base link to be verified.

entries.assertion: Never assume the three instruments are versions of one number: they must never be subtracted from, averaged with, or corrected against one another
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLCI DF3ª https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4163/texto/bloque/df ; INE ETDP methodological report https://www.ine.es/dynt3/metadatos/es/RespuestaPrint.html?oper=7
entries.locator: n/a — method rule
entries.final_wording: Never assume the three instruments are versions of one number: they must never be subtracted from, averaged with, or corrected against one another
entries.note: Correct as a method rule, and the sources confirm why: an asking price, the Catastro's valor de referencia (an objective administrative value capped at market and cut by a ministerial minoración factor) and a registered or notarised transaction price are produced by different bodies from different inputs on different reference dates. Arithmetic across them produces a number that measures nothing. This is a prohibition, not a sourced factual claim, and must not be published as though it were a finding about prices.

entries.assertion: Establish whether a second instrument built on a genuinely different underlying source agrees on the direction of the volume move for this province and period, and say so if the two disagree. Note that INE's Estadística de Transmisiones de Derechos de la Propiedad and the Colegio de Registradores' Estadística Registral Inmobiliaria are both drawn from the Registros de la Propiedad, so they are not independent of one another and their agreement is not corroboration; an independent cross-check must come from notarial data (Consejo General del Notariado, Índice Único Informatizado / Portal Estadístico del Notariado).

entries.locator: INE ETDP methodology: 'La información sobre transmisiones de derechos de la propiedad se obtiene a partir de la información contenida en los Registros de la Propiedad', supplied under a 2004 convenio between CORPME and INE; geographic scope national, CCAA, province and municipality. CORPME ERI: compiled by the Servicio de Estadística Registral from the Registros de la Propiedad. Notariado: Índice Único Informatizado, built from notarial deeds, searchable by CCAA, province, municipality and postcode.
entries.final_wording: Establish whether a second instrument built on a genuinely different underlying source agrees on the direction of the volume move for this province and period, and say so if the two disagree. INE's Estadística de Transmisiones de Derechos de la Propiedad and the Colegio de Registradores' Estadística Registral Inmobiliaria are both drawn from the Registros de la Propiedad (INE receives the data under a 2004 convenio with CORPME), so they are not independent of one another and their agreement is not corroboration; an independent cross-check must come from notarial data (Consejo General del Notariado, Índice Único Informatizado / Portal Estadístico del Notariado).
entries.note: The provenance claim is exactly right and is the substantive content of this instruction. ETDP and ERI share one upstream source (the property registries), so their agreement is not corroboration. The notarial Índice Único is genuinely independent. One addition the writer should know: INE's own Índice de Precios de Vivienda is built from notarial data supplied through ANCERT, not from the registries — so the IPV, not just the Notariado portal, can serve as the independent leg, though the IPV is a price index published only at CCAA level and cannot speak to provincial volume.

entries.assertion: Selling your Costa Blanca home while non-resident for Spanish tax purposes? The buyer must hand 3% of the price straight to Hacienda instead of to you — but it is a payment on account of your capital-gains tax, not the tax itself: once you file your modelo 210 you may get all of it back, some of it, or none, and you may still owe more. Here is who takes it, why, and how you settle it afterwards — whether any of it comes back depends on the gain.
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR (RDLeg 5/2004) art. 25.2 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4527/texto/bloque/a25 ; AEAT Sede Electrónica, modelo 210 instrucciones https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/todas-gestiones/impuestos-tasas/impuesto-sobre-renta-no-residentes/modelo-210-irnr______a-no-residentes-permanente_/instrucciones.html
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 25.2: 'Tratándose de transmisiones de bienes inmuebles situados en territorio español por contribuyentes que actúen sin establecimiento permanente, el adquirente estará obligado a retener e ingresar el 3 por ciento... de la contraprestación acordada, en concepto de pago a cuenta del impuesto correspondiente a aquéllos.' AEAT: modelo 210 for gains on property transfers is filed 'en el plazo de tres meses una vez transcurrido el plazo de un mes desde la fecha de la transmisión', with the retention entered in casilla 29 and any excess refundable.
entries.final_wording: Selling your Costa Blanca home while non-resident for Spanish tax purposes? The buyer must hand 3% of the agreed price straight to Hacienda instead of to you, on modelo 211 — but it is a payment on account of your capital-gains tax, not the tax itself: once you file your modelo 210 (due within three months after the one-month period that follows the sale) you may get all of it back, some of it, or none, and you may still owe more. Here is who takes it, why, and how you settle it afterwards — whether any of it comes back depends on the gain.
entries.note: Correct on every load-bearing point, including the one most often got wrong: the 3% is a pago a cuenta, not the tax, so a refund is possible even where a gain exists, and a further payment is possible where the gain is large. The hook also keeps tax residence distinct from nationality and from immigration status, which is the right discipline. Two small tightenings in final_wording: the statute measures the 3% on the 'contraprestación acordada' (the agreed consideration), not loosely 'the price'; and the buyer's instrument is modelo 211, which is worth naming because the seller needs that receipt to claim the credit on the modelo 210.

AEAT: modelo 210 for gains on property transfers is filed 'en el plazo de tres meses una vez transcurrido el plazo de un mes desde la fecha de la transmisión', with the retention entered in casilla 29 and any excess refundable.

entries.assertion: Establish what happens where there was no increase in land value between acquisition and transmission — specifically whether that is a case of non-liability or of an exemption that must be claimed
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLRHL (RDLeg 2/2004) art. 104 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4214/texto/bloque/a104
entries.locator: TRLRHL art. 104.5, added by art. único.1 of RDL 26/2021: 'No se producirá la sujeción al impuesto en las transmisiones de terrenos respecto de los cuales se constate la inexistencia de incremento de valor...' and 'el interesado en acreditar la inexistencia de incremento de valor deberá declarar la transmisión, así como aportar los títulos que documenten la transmisión y la adquisición'
entries.final_wording: Establish what happens where there was no increase in land value between acquisition and transmission — specifically whether that is a case of non-liability or of an exemption that must be claimed, and separately what the seller must still file or produce to establish it
entries.note: Sound instruction, and it is asking the right question rather than asserting an answer — which matters, because the answer is a hybrid that content routinely garbles. It is non-liability (no sujeción), not an exemption: the taxable event does not arise. But the taxpayer still has to declare the transfer and produce the acquisition and transfer títulos to establish it, so in practice it behaves like something you must claim. Writing 'exempt' would be wrong; writing 'automatic, nothing to file' would also be wrong.

entries.assertion: Establish the statutory ceilings that constrain plusvalía municipal (TRLRHL art. 107.4 for the coefficients, art. 108.1 for the rate, capped at 30%), confirm from the ordenanza fiscal of each specific municipality what that town hall has actually set, and treat any single quoted amount as a fact about one town only. Do not state a province-wide spread without having opened the ordinances it is drawn from.

entries.locator: TRLRHL art. 107.4 (wording from art. único.2 of RDL 26/2021): table of maximum coefficients by years elapsed, 'Estos coeficientes máximos serán actualizados anualmente mediante norma con rango legal'. TRLRHL art. 108.1: 'El tipo de gravamen del impuesto será el fijado por cada ayuntamiento, sin que dicho tipo pueda exceder del 30 por ciento.'
entries.final_wording: Establish the statutory ceilings that constrain plusvalía municipal (TRLRHL art. 107.4 for the maximum coefficients, art. 108.1 for the rate, capped at 30%), confirm from the ordenanza fiscal of each specific municipality what that town hall has actually set, and treat any single quoted amount as a fact about one town only. Do not state a province-wide spread without having opened the ordinances it is drawn from. Re-check the coefficient maxima before quoting one: they are updated annually by a norm of legal rank and the 2025 and 2026 updates were both voided when Congress repealed the decrees carrying them.
entries.note: Both article references and the 30% ceiling are correct in the consolidated text in force today, and the instruction's discipline — that the ceilings are state law but the actual figures are per-municipality, so a quoted amount is a fact about one town — is right. Volatility warning for whoever writes from this: the coefficient maxima are updated annually by a norm of legal rank, and the last two attempts failed — the update in RDL 9/2024 was voided when Congress repealed that decree (Resolution of 22 January 2025) and the update in RDL 16/2025 was voided the same way (Resolution of 27 January 2026). The maxima in force are therefore still those set with effect from 1 January 2024 by art. 24 of RDL 8/2023. Re-check before quoting any coefficient value; the article numbers and the 30% cap are stable.

TRLRHL art. 108.1: 'El tipo de gravamen del impuesto será el fijado por cada ayuntamiento, sin que dicho tipo pueda exceder del 30 por ciento.'

entries.assertion: Establish the precise condition each exemption attaches to the property itself — in particular whether it must have been the seller's habitual residence, and how that status is defined and over what period it is tested
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated Reglamento del IRPF (RD 439/2007) art. 41 bis https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2007-6820/texto/bloque/a41bis
entries.locator: RIRPF art. 41 bis: habitual residence for arts. 7.t), 33.4.b) and 38 LIRPF = the dwelling that is the taxpayer's residence for a continuous period of at least three years, effectively and permanently occupied within twelve months of acquisition or completion of works; art. 41 bis.3 treats the dwelling as habitual if it held that status on any day in the two years before the transfer
entries.final_wording: Establish the precise condition each exemption attaches to the property itself — in particular whether it must have been the seller's habitual residence, how that status is defined, and over what period it is tested (there is more than one clock). Establish separately whether the exemption requires Spanish tax residence, since nationality and property ownership do not confer it.
entries.note: Sound instruction and it is aimed at the right trap. The definition is not intuitive and has three separate clocks — three continuous years of residence, occupation within twelve months, and a two-year look-back window at the moment of sale — so 'it was my home' is not the test. One thing the writer must not lose when this instruction is executed: these are IRPF exemptions, which turn on Spanish tax residence, not on nationality or on owning the property. A non-resident seller is outside them, subject to the separate EU/EEA reinvestment route in the IRNR rules.

entries.assertion: Do not assume a withdrawal right exists for every mandate — it is conditional, and the seed must publish the condition rather than the conclusion.
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLGDCU (RDLeg 1/2007) arts. 92 and 102 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2007-20555/texto/bloque/a92 and .../a102
entries.locator: TRLGDCU art. 102.1: fourteen calendar days to withdraw without giving a reason, 'salvo las excepciones previstas en el artículo 103', extended to thirty days for contracts concluded during unsolicited visits to the consumer's home; art. 92 fixes the scope — distance contracts and contracts concluded away from the trader's business premises, with art. 92.4 presuming off-premises contracts fall within the title unless the trader proves otherwise
entries.final_wording: Do not assume a withdrawal right exists for every mandate — it is conditional on the seller being a consumer and on the contract having been concluded at a distance or away from the agency's business premises, and the seed must publish the condition rather than the conclusion.
entries.note: Correct, and the conditionality is real and load-bearing. The withdrawal right attaches to the circumstances of signing, not to the mandate: a seller who is a consumer and signs at home, at a property viewing, or online has it; the same seller signing inside the agency's office after walking in does not. There is also a longer thirty-day window where the agent called at the seller's home unsolicited, and art. 92.4 puts the burden of proof on the agency. Publishing 'you have fourteen days to cancel' as a flat statement would be wrong in a large share of real cases.

freshness.source_locator: TRLGDCU art. 102.1: fourteen calendar days to withdraw without giving a reason, 'salvo las excepciones previstas en el artículo 103', extended to thirty days for contracts concluded during unsolicited visits to the consumer's home; art. 92 fixes the scope — distance contracts and contracts concluded away from the trader's business premises, with art. 92.4 presuming off-premises contracts fall within the title unless the trader proves otherwise

entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated RD 390/2021 arts. 17 and 21 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2021-9176/texto/bloque/a1-9 and .../a2-3
entries.locator: RD 390/2021 art. 17.2 (on a sale of an existing building a copy of the duly registered certificate and the label 'se anexará al contrato de compraventa'); art. 21 (breach is sanctioned under DA 12ª of the TRLSRU, RDLeg 7/2015, and, where it amounts to a consumer-protection infringement, under arts. 49.1.f) and n) TRLGDCU)
entries.final_wording: Establish whether a missing energy certificate blocks the notary or only creates a sanction and buyer exposure; these two are routinely conflated and the answer must come from the instrument, not from a summary of it. Contrast it explicitly with the community-debt certificate, which sits on the other side of that line.
entries.note: Sound instruction and the conflation it warns about is real. RD 390/2021 imposes a duty to annex the registered certificate to the contract and backs it with an administrative sanction regime plus consumer-law exposure — it nowhere bars the notary from authorising the deed. That is the opposite of the community-debt certificate at gid 13, which does bar authorisation. Anything that writes 'you cannot sell without an EPC' is wrong; 'you are exposed to a fine and to the buyer' is right.

entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated RD 390/2021 art. 6.6 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2021-9176/texto/bloque/a6
entries.locator: RD 390/2021 art. 6.6: the certificate and the XML energy assessment report 'deben presentarse, por el promotor, propietario, o la persona autorizada por los mismos' to the CCAA body competent for energy certification; 'Para que el certificado de eficiencia energética del edificio tenga validez legal tiene que estar debidamente registrado'; filing period set by the CCAA or, failing that, one month from issue
entries.final_wording: Do not assume a certificate issued by a technician is a registered certificate; establish whether registration is a separate step, who must do it, and by when.
entries.note: Correct, and the distinction is decisive rather than pedantic: an unregistered certificate has no legal validity at all, so a seller holding a signed technician's report holds nothing usable. Registration is a separate step, and the duty to file sits on the owner or promoter (or someone they authorise), not automatically on the technician — which is exactly the assumption sellers make and the reason deadlines get missed.

entries.assertion: Establish whether commission rates are capped or regulated by any Spanish statute or set purely by contract, and where the agreed figure is required to be recorded.
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated RDL 4/2000, de 23 de junio, art. 3 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2000-11834/texto/bloque/a3
entries.locator: RDL 4/2000 art. 3, 'Condiciones para el ejercicio de la actividad de intermediación inmobiliaria': the activities listed in art. 1 of Decreto 3248/1969 'podrán ser ejercidas libremente sin necesidad de estar en posesión de título alguno ni de pertenencia a ningún Colegio oficial'
entries.final_wording: Establish whether commission rates are capped or regulated by any Spanish statute or set purely by contract, and where the agreed figure is required to be recorded. Note that the liberalisation of estate-agency intermediation in 2000 left no title, colegio or fee scale requirement for sales, and do not carry across the residential-letting rule that puts agency fees on the landlord — that governs rentals, not sales.
entries.note: Sound instruction. The answer to its first half is a negative one, which is why the instruction must be executed rather than assumed: estate agency intermediation was liberalised in 2000, there is no qualification requirement, no compulsory colegio, and no statutory cap or scale on sale commissions — the figure is pure freedom of contract. Note the sharp exception the writer must not generalise from: for residential lettings, agency fees were placed on the landlord and made non-waivable by the 2023 housing law. That rule is about rentals and says nothing about a sale. The second half — where the agreed figure must be recorded — has no state statutory answer either and falls back on the mandate contract itself and on consumer transparency rules where the seller is a consumer.

entries.assertion: Do not assume a Costa Blanca median commission exists — a nationally published band is not a local measurement and must never be presented as one.
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: Searched for an official measurement of estate-agency commissions for Alicante province or the Costa Blanca across INE, MIVAU/Ministerio de Transportes and Colegio de Registradores statistical portals; none exists. Only commercial and trade-press bands (e.g. '3% to 7%') were found, with no stated sample, geography or period.
entries.locator: n/a — no publisher of any authority measures this
entries.final_wording: Do not assume a Costa Blanca median commission exists. No official statistics producer measures estate-agency commissions in Spain at any geography, so the commonly quoted bands are commercial claims with no stated sample, period or method — they are not a national measurement to be localised, and must never be presented as one.
entries.note: Correct prohibition, and the search behind it produced a finding worth recording in its own right: there is no official statistics producer in Spain that measures estate-agency commissions at all, at any geography. The widely repeated '3–7%' band traces only to agency and portal marketing copy with no sample, no period and no method. So there is no national figure to localise in the first place — the guardrail is if anything understated, and the honest position is that the evidence does not exist rather than that it exists nationally but not locally.

entries.assertion: Establish which items in the resulting list are permanent costs and which are payments on account that can be recovered, and what filing a seller must make, and by when, to recover anything recoverable.
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: AEAT Sede Electrónica, modelo 210 instrucciones https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/todas-gestiones/impuestos-tasas/impuesto-sobre-renta-no-residentes/modelo-210-irnr______a-no-residentes-permanente_/instrucciones.html ; BOE consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25.2 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4527/texto/bloque/a25
entries.locator: AEAT modelo 210 instructions: returns for gains on transfers of immovable property are filed 'en el plazo de tres meses una vez transcurrido el plazo de un mes desde la fecha de la transmisión'; the 3% retention is entered as retenciones/ingresos a cuenta and any excess over the final liability is refundable
entries.final_wording: Establish which items in the resulting list are permanent costs and which are payments on account that can be recovered, and what filing a seller must make, and by when, to recover anything recoverable — recovery is never automatic.
entries.note: Sound instruction, and the sorting it demands is the whole point of the topic. For a non-resident seller the only recoverable item in the usual list is the 3% retention, and recovery is not automatic — it requires the seller to file modelo 210 within three months after the one-month period following the sale, using the modelo 211 receipt from the buyer as evidence of the credit. Everything else on a normal completion list (notary, plusvalía where finally due, EPC, agency invoice) is a permanent cost. A seller who never files simply forfeits the refund.

entries.assertion: Do not assume a sum withheld at completion is a cost — a payment on account, a tax finally due and an invoice are three different things and must never be added into one headline number.
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated TRLIRNR art. 25.2 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2004-4527/texto/bloque/a25
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 25.2: the buyer withholds and pays over 3% of the agreed consideration 'en concepto de pago a cuenta del impuesto correspondiente' to the non-resident seller
entries.final_wording: Do not assume a sum withheld at completion is a cost — a payment on account, a tax finally due and an invoice are three different things and must never be added into one headline number.
entries.note: Correct, and it is the single most useful prohibition in this topic. Adding the 3% retention into a 'cost of selling' total double-counts against the capital-gains tax it is credited to and overstates the seller's cost by up to the full retention, since an excess is refundable. The three categories the rule separates are real and behave differently: a payment on account can come back, a tax finally due cannot, and an invoice is a price for a service.

entries.assertion: Establish what evidentiary standard applies — whether an invoice, a bank trace, or a registered work declaration is required — and what is excluded outright, financing costs included
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated LIRPF (Ley 35/2006) art. 35 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2006-20764/texto/bloque/a35
entries.locator: LIRPF art. 35.1.b): the acquisition value includes 'el coste de las inversiones y mejoras efectuadas en los bienes adquiridos y los gastos y tributos inherentes a la adquisición, excluidos los intereses, que hubieran sido satisfechos por el adquirente'
entries.final_wording: Establish what evidentiary standard applies — whether an invoice, a bank trace, or a registered work declaration is required — and present it as administrative and case-law practice, not as a statutory list, because no statute prescribes one. Establish separately what is excluded outright: financing interest is excluded by the express words of the statute.
entries.note: Sound instruction, with an asymmetry the writer must respect. The exclusion half has a clean statutory answer: interest is excluded by the express words of art. 35.1.b), so mortgage financing costs never enter the acquisition value. The evidentiary half does not — no statute prescribes invoice versus bank trace versus registered declaration of works. That standard comes from the general burden-of-proof rules of the Ley General Tributaria as applied by the Administration and the tribunals, so it must be presented as practice and as risk, never as a statutory list. Note too that art. 35 distinguishes improvements from repairs and maintenance; only the former raise the acquisition value.

entries.assertion: Which costs of selling a Costa Blanca home fall on the seller under Spanish law by default, which are allocated instead by agreement or local custom, and which certificates must the seller obtain, pay for and register before a deed can be completed?
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated Código Civil art. 1455 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1889-4763/texto/bloque/art1455 ; BOE consolidated LPH artículo noveno https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1960-10906/texto/bloque/anoveno ; BOE consolidated RD 390/2021 arts. 6, 17, 21 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2021-9176/texto/bloque/a6
entries.locator: CC art. 1455 (default allocation of deed costs, 'salvo pacto en contrario'); LPH art. 9.1.e) (community-debt certificate: produced to the notary, not registered anywhere, and a bar on authorisation unless the buyer expressly waives); RD 390/2021 arts. 6.6 and 21 (EPC: must be registered with the autonomous community for legal validity, but a breach is sanctioned, not a bar on the deed)
entries.final_wording: Which costs of selling a Costa Blanca home fall on the seller under Spanish law by default, which are allocated instead by agreement or local custom, which certificates must the seller obtain and pay for, which of those must additionally be registered with a public body to be valid, and which — separately — a notary is actually barred from proceeding without?
entries.note: The first two limbs of the question are well framed. The third bundles three separate tests into one — obtain, pay for, register, and 'before a deed can be completed' — and no certificate satisfies all of them, so the question as written cannot be answered truthfully and invites the exact conflation that gid 14 and gid 24 exist to prevent. The community-debt certificate is the one that gates the deed, and it is not registered with any body. The energy certificate must be registered with the autonomous community for legal validity, and it does not gate the deed. Splitting the limb is the fix.

entries.assertion: Establish which certificates the law obliges the seller to hold or produce — energy performance, the Valencian second-occupancy instrument, the community-debt certificate — which body each must be registered with, and which of them a notary is actually barred from proceeding without
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated RD 390/2021 arts. 6.6 and 21 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2021-9176/texto/bloque/a6 ; BOE consolidated LPH artículo noveno https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1960-10906/texto/bloque/anoveno ; Ajuntament de València sede, Declaración Responsable de segunda ocupación de viviendas (Decreto 12/2021 del Consell) https://sede.valencia.es/sede/registro/procedimiento/UR.DU.50?lang=1
entries.locator: RD 390/2021 art. 6.6 (EPC registered with the CCAA body) and art. 21 (sanction regime, no notarial bar); LPH art. 9.1.e) (debt certificate produced to the notary, bar on authorisation unless expressly waived by the buyer, seven calendar days to issue); Decreto 12/2021 del Consell and TRLOTUP art. 233.1.f) (Valencian occupancy handled by declaración responsable filed with the town hall by the owner, unless the municipality has required an express licence by ordinance)
entries.final_wording: Establish which certificates the law obliges the seller to hold or produce — energy performance, the Valencian second-occupancy instrument, the community-debt certificate — which body each must be filed or registered with, and which of them a notary is actually barred from proceeding without. Keep those three questions apart; the three certificates answer them differently. Check the Valencian item town by town, since its nature depends on whether the municipality has opted for an express licence.
entries.note: Sound instruction, and it is right to keep the three questions apart — hold or produce, register with whom, and bar the notary — because the three certificates answer them differently and no two align. It is also right to call the Valencian item an 'instrument' rather than a licence or a certificate: in the Comunitat Valenciana second and successive occupancy runs on a declaración responsable filed with the town hall by the owner, required where ten years have passed since first occupancy and there is a transfer or a new utility contract, except in municipalities that have opted by ordinance for an express licence — so its very nature varies by town.

entries.assertion: [NEVER claim] that 'the buyer pays everything' is the law rather than a customary term that must appear in the contract to bind anyone
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated Código Civil art. 1455 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1889-4763/texto/bloque/art1455
entries.locator: Código Civil art. 1455: 'Los gastos de otorgamiento de escrituras serán de cuenta del vendedor, y los de la primera copia y los demás posteriores a la venta serán de cuenta del comprador, salvo pacto en contrario.'
entries.final_wording: Never claim that 'the buyer pays everything' is the law. The Civil Code's default splits the costs and applies unless the parties agree otherwise, so 'the buyer pays everything' is a customary term that must appear in the contract to bind anyone.
entries.note: Correct, and the statute is unambiguous on the point. The Civil Code's default splits the costs — the seller bears the cost of granting the deed, the buyer the first copy and everything after the sale — and it applies only 'salvo pacto en contrario'. So 'the buyer pays everything' is the opposite of the default: it is a contractual term that displaces the law and binds nobody unless it is actually written into the contract. This is a prohibition on a legal misstatement, not a sourced factual claim in itself.

freshness.source_locator: Código Civil art. 1455: 'Los gastos de otorgamiento de escrituras serán de cuenta del vendedor, y los de la primera copia y los demás posteriores a la venta serán de cuenta del comprador, salvo pacto en contrario.'

entries.assertion: [NEVER assume] that the Valencian occupancy and energy-certificate requirements are as they were a year ago, or that a missing certificate stops a signing — one of these is a hard statutory stop and the others are not, and which is which must be verified before it is written
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE, Real Decreto 659/2025, de 22 de julio, amending RD 390/2021 https://www.boe.es/buscar/doc.php?id=BOE-A-2025-15230 ; BOE consolidated RD 390/2021 arts. 2, 6, 10, 13, 17, 21 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2021-9176/texto/bloque/a1-9 ; BOE consolidated LPH artículo noveno https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1960-10906/texto/bloque/anoveno ; Ajuntament de València sede, DR de segunda ocupación https://sede.valencia.es/sede/registro/procedimiento/UR.DU.50?lang=1
entries.locator: RD 659/2025 (in force 23 July 2026) replaces the 'técnico competente' regime of RD 390/2021 with new arts. 4 bis, 4 ter and 4 quáter, a mandatory training course, a declaración responsable before practising and a central registry of technicians, and rewrites arts. 2 and 10; RD 390/2021 art. 21 sanctions a missing EPC under DA 12ª TRLSRU and consumer law, with no notarial bar; LPH art. 9.1.e) is the only notarial bar in this family, and yields to express waiver by the buyer
entries.final_wording: Never assume the Valencian occupancy and energy-certificate requirements are as they were a year ago — the energy-certificate regime changed on 23 July 2026, when RD 659/2025 replaced the rules on who may issue a certificate. And never assume a missing certificate stops a signing: neither the energy certificate nor the Valencian second-occupancy declaración responsable bars the notary. The only certificate that does is the community-of-owners debt certificate under LPH art. 9.1.e, and even that yields where the buyer expressly waives it.
entries.note: The first half is right and is now concretely right: RD 659/2025 amended RD 390/2021 with effect from 23 July 2026, six weeks before today, changing who may issue an energy certificate. Anyone writing from a pass older than that is out of date. The second half is wrong as written. Of the two items this rule names, neither is a hard statutory stop — a missing energy certificate produces a sanction and consumer exposure, not a bar on the notary, and the Valencian second-occupancy declaración responsable is filed with the town hall and has no notarial bar either. The only statutory bar in the seller's certificate bundle is the community-debt certificate under LPH art. 9.1.e), which this rule does not name, and even that is not absolute: the buyer can expressly waive it. As written the rule would lead a writer to hunt for a hard stop among two items that do not contain one.

entries.assertion: What must a power of attorney contain, and by which routes can an owner living outside Spain create one, for a Spanish notary to accept it for the sale of a specific property — and how do the available routes differ in the steps and formalities each demands?
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: NONE
entries.locator: n/a — research question, no assertion made
entries.final_wording: What must a power of attorney contain, and by which routes can an owner living outside Spain create one, for a Spanish notary to accept it for the sale of a specific property — and how do the available routes differ in the steps and formalities each demands? Keep the routes apart: granting before a Spanish consul and granting before a foreign notary do not carry the same formalities.
entries.note: Well-framed research question with no false presupposition, so nothing here is a factual claim to verify or correct. It correctly separates the three things that get merged in this topic: the content the power must have (a special power identifying the specific property and the acts authorised, not a general one), the route by which it is created abroad, and the formalities each route demands. Left UNRESOLVED-free but flagged for the execution pass: the answer must distinguish a power granted before a Spanish consular notary from one granted before a foreign notary, since only the second raises legalisation or apostille and sworn translation, and it must not be answered from a summary — the acceptance test is the Spanish notary's, applied to the document in front of them.

entries.assertion: Establish whether a general power of administration is sufficient to sell, or whether express authority to dispose is required, and name the instrument that says so
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE — Código Civil, texto consolidado, art. 1713 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1889-4763/texto/bloque/art1713
entries.locator: Código Civil art. 1713, párrafos 1-2 (consolidated text in force 2 Sep 2026)
entries.final_wording: Establish whether a general power of administration is sufficient to sell, or whether express authority to dispose is required, and name the instrument that says so
entries.note: Method rule, not a sourced factual claim — but it is answerable and I opened the answer. CC art. 1713: 'El mandato, concebido en términos generales, no comprende más que los actos de administración. Para transigir, enajenar, hipotecar o ejecutar cualquier otro acto de riguroso dominio, se necesita mandato expreso.' So a general power of administration is NOT sufficient; express authority to dispose (enajenar) is required, and the instrument is CC art. 1713.

Statutory maximum periods are a different thing and may be stated as law, clearly labelled as the legal maximum rather than the typical wait: for example, Ley Hipotecaria art. 18 gives the registrar fifteen days from the asiento de presentación to inscribe, extendable by up to fifteen more.

entries.final_wording: Never publish an observed waiting time or turnaround average for administrative or consular steps — no official series establishes one, and it varies by country and by consular post. Art. 18 §2 verbatim: 'El plazo máximo para inscribir el documento será de quince días contados desde la fecha del asiento de presentación… Por razones extraordinarias, debidamente acreditadas, la Dirección General… podrá, a solicitud del registrador competente formulada dentro de los dos primeros días de plazo de inscripción, ampliar hasta quince días más como máximo dicho plazo.' The extension is discretionary and administrator-granted, not automatic — the original wording read as if the registrar simply has up to thirty days. entries.assertion: You can accept an offer on a house that is still in your mother's name. What you cannot do is let the buyer register it — and that is a different problem with a same-day solution.
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE — Ley Hipotecaria, texto consolidado, arts. 17, 20 y 24 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1946-2453/texto/bloque/a20
entries.locator: Ley Hipotecaria art. 20 §§1-2 (tracto sucesivo, denegación) and arts. 17 and 24 (priority by asiento de presentación)
entries.final_wording: You can accept an offer on a house that is still in your mother's name — the heirs own it, and the contract is valid. What you cannot do is let the buyer register it: Ley Hipotecaria art. 20 requires the seller's own right to be inscribed first, and says registrars shall refuse where the registered owner is someone else. In practice the two deeds are usually signed and lodged on the same day, the inheritance first and the sale second, because the registry despatches titles in order of presentation — that is standard practice built on the priority rule, not a right to same-day treatment.
entries.note: The first two claims verify. Art. 20 §1 requires the disponent's right to be previously inscribed or annotated; §2 'los Registradores denegarán la inscripción solicitada' where the registered holder is someone else. The exceptions in §5 for heirs (ratifying a private contract signed by the deceased, selling to a co-heir, judicial adjudication decrees) do not cover an ordinary sale to a third-party buyer. The 'same-day solution' is the part that needed correcting: nothing in the LH entitles a seller to same-day treatment. It works because arts. 17 and 24 rank titles by the asiento de presentación and the registry despatches in that order, so the inheritance deed is inscribed first and the sale immediately behind it. Stated as a bare 'same-day solution' the hook asserts as a rule exactly what this topic's own guardrail (gid 32) forbids assuming.

freshness.source_locator: Ley Hipotecaria art. 20 §§1-2 (tracto sucesivo, denegación) and arts. 17 and 24 (priority by asiento de presentación)

entries.assertion: Do not assume an heir living abroad is taxed on a worse scale than a resident heir. Since Ley 11/2021 (in force 11 July 2021) removed the EU/EEA limit from DA 2ª of Ley 29/1987, a non-resident heir — including one resident in a third country — is entitled to the rules of the Comunidad Autónoma where the deceased resided, so the Valencian reliefs apply to them. What does change is the competent administration (the State, under DA 2ª Dos, not the Generalitat) and the scope of the charge (obligación real — Spanish-situs assets only). And never file an heir's nationality as if it settled their tax residence or their EU/EEA/third-country status.
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE — Ley 29/1987 del ISD, DA 2ª (texto consolidado) https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1987-28141/texto/bloque/segunda ; Ley 11/2021 DF 7ª https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2021-11473/texto/bloque/df-7 ; Ley 22/2009 art. 32 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-2009-20375/texto/bloque/a32
entries.locator: Ley 29/1987 DA 2ª Uno.1.b) and Dos; Ley 11/2021 art. 4.6 and DF 7ª (BOE 10 Jul 2021, in force 11 Jul 2021); Ley 22/2009 art. 32.2
entries.final_wording: Do not assume an heir living abroad is taxed on a worse scale than a resident heir. Since Ley 11/2021 (in force 11 July 2021) removed the EU/EEA limit from DA 2ª of Ley 29/1987, a non-resident heir — including one resident in a third country — is entitled to the rules of the Comunidad Autónoma where the deceased resided, so the Valencian reliefs apply to them. What does change is the competent administration (the State, because Ley 22/2009 art. 32.2 cedes the yield only for taxpayers resident in Spain, so a non-resident heir self-assesses to the State under DA 2ª Dos rather than to the Generalitat) and the scope of the charge (obligación real — Spanish-situs assets only). And never file an heir's nationality as if it settled their tax residence or their EU/EEA/third-country status.
entries.note: Guardrail — correct in substance, so not dressed as a sourced fact, but every embedded element was checked. DA 2ª Uno.1.b) now reads 'los contribuyentes no residentes tendrán derecho a la aplicación de la normativa propia aprobada por dicha Comunidad Autónoma' with no EU/EEA qualifier, amended by Ley 11/2021 art. 4.6; DF 7ª of Ley 11/2021 puts it in force the day after BOE publication of 10 July 2021, i.e. 11 July 2021, and art. 4.6 is not among the deferred provisions. One citation was loose and I tightened it: DA 2ª Dos does not itself confer State competence — it is headed 'regulación de la declaración liquidación de los contribuyentes que deban tributar a la Administración Tributaria del Estado' and regulates their self-assessment. Competence flows from Ley 22/2009 art. 32.2, which attributes the yield to a Comunidad Autónoma only for 'sujetos pasivos residentes en España'. The residence/nationality warning at the end is exactly right and is the single most common error in this area.

entries.note: The scenario is illustrative but the load-bearing legal claim is sound and sourced. CC art. 399 lets each co-owner dispose only of his own undivided share ('Todo condueño tendrá la plena propiedad de su parte… pudiendo en consecuencia enajenarla'), and art. 397 bars any co-owner from acting on the common thing without the others' consent — so selling the whole house does need all of them; a single heir can sell only his share. Consent and form: art. 82 §1 LH — cancellation only by a judgment no longer open to casación, or by 'otra escritura o documento auténtico en la cual preste su consentimiento para la cancelación la persona a cuyo favor se hubiere hecho la inscripción' (the lender), so a paid-off loan alone does not clear the registry. entries.assertion: Establish what happens where the agreed price does not cover the outstanding loan balance plus these deductions — whether lender consent is required to complete, and on what basis
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE — Ley Hipotecaria, texto consolidado, arts. 104 y 82 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1946-2453/texto/bloque/a104

entries.final_wording: Establish what happens where the agreed price does not cover the outstanding loan balance plus these deductions — whether lender consent is required to complete, and on what basis
entries.note: Method rule, sound, and the 'on what basis' has a clean primary answer. The lender's consent is not needed to sell — art. 104 LH is why it does not need to be asked: the mortgage binds the property 'cualquiera que sea su poseedor', so a sale simply passes the charge to the buyer. Consent becomes decisive only for clearing the charge, because art. 82 §1 LH makes cancellation depend on the creditor's consent in escritura or documento auténtico. So where the price falls short, either the seller makes up the difference at completion or the lender must agree to release the charge for less than the balance; a buyer will not complete without a clean registry. Keep the two questions apart — the piece should not tell sellers the bank can block the sale itself.

Document: the certification on the state of debts with the community, matching the seller's declaration in the deed — 'sin la cual no podrá autorizarse el otorgamiento del documento público'. Waiver: only the buyer can waive it — 'salvo que fuese expresamente exonerado de esta obligación por el adquirente' — and it is the buyer's risk, because the same article makes the acquired flat itself liable for the previous owner's unpaid community charges for the current annuity and the three preceding calendar years.

entries.note: Sound, and the reachability warning is the important half — the gating is severe. Reinvestment relief (LIRPF art. 38.1) requires the property to have been the taxpayer's vivienda habitual; for non-residents it exists only through TRLIRNR DA 7ª, which reaches residents of an EU Member State and, under DA 7ª.4, of an EEA state with effective exchange of tax information — a third-country resident cannot reach it at all. Art. 38.3 (lifetime-annuity reinvestment, capped at €240,000) and DT 9ª (abatement coefficients, only for assets acquired before 31 December 1994) are the remaining routes. entries.assertion: Establish whether the buyer's position as a registered good-faith purchaser under the Ley Hipotecaria alters the result, and in which lease categories that argument is even available.
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE — Ley 29/1994 LAU, texto consolidado, arts. 14 y 29 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1994-26003/texto/bloque/a29
entries.locator: LAU art. 14 §§1-2 and art. 29, both referring to art. 34 Ley Hipotecaria
entries.final_wording: Establish whether the buyer's position as a registered good-faith purchaser under the Ley Hipotecaria alters the result, and in which lease categories that argument is even available.
entries.note: Sound, and the answer is narrower than most commentary suggests. For a residential lease under the current art. 14, art. 34 LH does not help within the protected period — the acquirer is subrogated 'aun cuando concurran en él los requisitos del artículo 34'. The argument only bites on the excess: where a term longer than five years (seven, legal person) was agreed, an art. 34 purchaser need only bear the lease to the end of that five- or seven-year floor, with the seller owing the tenant one month's rent per remaining year. For a lease of premises for a use other than dwelling, art. 29 reverses it — subrogation applies 'salvo que concurran en el adquirente los requisitos del artículo 34 de la Ley Hipotecaria'. And for residential contracts signed between 6 June 2013 and 5 March 2019 the Ley 4/2013 text makes an unregistered lease unopposable to an art. 34 purchaser outright.

entries.final_wording: Establish how the LAU distinguishes a lease of a dwelling from a lease for a use other than dwelling, and read the transfer-of-property article that applies to each — do not extrapolate one from the other, because the default may run in opposite directions.
entries.note: Sound, and the warning is literally correct — the two defaults are mirror images. Art. 14: the acquirer is subrogated for the first five years (seven if the previous landlord was a legal person) 'aun cuando concurran en él los requisitos del artículo 34 de la Ley Hipotecaria'. Art. 29, in full: 'El adquirente de la finca arrendada quedará subrogado en los derechos y obligaciones del arrendador, salvo que concurran en el adquirente los requisitos del artículo 34 de la Ley Hipotecaria.' entries.assertion: What rights, if any, does a sitting tenant have when a Costa Blanca landlord sells, what notice must the landlord give and in what form, what follows if it is not given, and can those rights be given up in advance?
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE — Ley 29/1994 LAU, texto consolidado, art. 25 https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/legislacion-consolidada/id/BOE-A-1994-26003/texto/bloque/a25
entries.locator: LAU art. 25, apartados 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8 (redacción vigente; ap. 7 por art. 1.13 RDL 7/2019)
entries.final_wording: What rights, if any, does a sitting tenant have when a Costa Blanca landlord sells, what notice must the landlord give and in what form, what follows if it is not given, and can those rights be given up in advance?
entries.note: A research question, not a claim; all four limbs are answerable from art. 25 LAU and the presuppositions hold. Rights: tanteo (ap. 2) and retracto (ap. 3). Form: notice 'en forma fehaciente' of the decision to sell, the price and the other essential conditions. Failure: the tenant may exercise retracto where no notice was given or a requirement was omitted, or where the actual price was lower or the other essential terms less onerous (ap. 3) — and under ap. 5 the sale of a let dwelling cannot be registered without proving the notices were given. Advance waiver: yes, under the current ap. 8 the parties may agree it, but the landlord must then tell the tenant of the intention to sell at least thirty days before the sale contract is formalised. Two limits worth carrying: ap. 7 removes tanteo and retracto where the whole building is sold together (unless it holds only one dwelling), and this is state law, not a Costa Blanca or Valencian rule.

entries.assertion: Establish from the LAU which article confers a tenant's right of first refusal and which confers a right to step into a completed sale, the exact time limits for each, the moment from which each runs, and for how long a notification retains its effect.
