BOE-A-2025-76)
entries.final_wording: Planning to rent it out to cover the costs? Since 3 April 2025 your neighbours get a vote — and in some places new licences are frozen.
entries.note: Both limbs hold. The 3 April 2025 date is the BOE's own effect date for LO 1/2025's amendment of LPH art. 17.12, and the amendment added 'apruebe' to the existing 3/5 rule, which is what turns a neighbours' veto into a neighbours' vote. The licence freeze is real and first-party: Alicante city suspended licences, declaraciones responsables and any other enabling title for new VUT (isolated and whole blocks) and changes of use, extended for a second year, and El Campello, Calpe, Dénia, Altea and Xàbia have their own moratoria. Two nuances the body must carry: the community agreement is expressly non-retroactive, so lettings already running are not caught; and whether silence alone blocks a new letting is contested — what art. 17.12 settles is the majority needed once the community votes.

entries.assertion: The definition being used: registrars count purchases by buyer nationality, which includes foreigners resident in Spain — so 'foreign buyer' is not the same as 'overseas buyer', and the piece must not silently swap the two

entries.locator: ERI 2T 2026, p. 117, methodological note 'Nacionalidad en las compras de vivienda registradas': 'Las compras de vivienda son clasificadas según la nacionalidad del comprador. Los resultados no se adentran en el concepto de residencia, ya que no es un dato que quede recogido en la escritura de compraventa, por lo que no se puede desagregar entre residentes y no residentes.'
entries.final_wording: The definition being used: registrars count purchases by buyer nationality, which includes foreigners resident in Spain — so 'foreign buyer' is not the same as 'overseas buyer', and the piece must not silently swap the two
entries.note: The Registradores say this themselves, in the ERI's own methodology: purchases are classified by the buyer's nationality, residence is not recorded in the deed, and residents cannot be separated from non-residents. So the ERI's 'compras por extranjeros' includes a Romanian or Moroccan national living and working in Alicante, and cannot be read as overseas demand. Publication reference period Q2 2026, published August 2026.

entries.assertion: Do not hard-code a 24%-on-gross rule for every UK or third-country owner as evergreen knowledge. Re-check AEAT and the current binding case-law position at generation time.
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: BOE consolidated RDLeg 5/2004 (TRLIRNR), arts. 24.6 and 25.1, https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-4527
entries.locator: TRLIRNR art. 24.6 limits the deduction of expenses to 'contribuyentes residentes en otro Estado miembro de la Unión Europea'; art. 25.1.a) sets 24% generally and 19% for EU/EEA residents with effective exchange of information. Audiencia Nacional judgment of 28 July 2025, ECLI:ES:AN:2025:3630, held the exclusion of third-country residents contrary to the free movement of capital (art. 63 TFEU); appealable in cassation.
entries.final_wording: Do not hard-code a 24%-on-gross rule for every UK or third-country owner as evergreen knowledge. Re-check AEAT and the current binding case-law position at generation time.
entries.note: A method rule, not a claim — but a well-aimed one, and it is currently earning its keep. The statute is unchanged (24% on gross for a UK-resident owner, expenses deductible only for EU residents), yet the Audiencia Nacional ruled on 28 July 2025 that denying expenses to third-country residents breaches art. 63 TFEU, annulling a TEAC resolution. That judgment is appealable in cassation and is not settled doctrine, so the honest position today is: the statutory rule still applies, but 'on gross' is under live challenge and must not be written as permanent.

entries.assertion: Do not imply that two clients face the same rate without checking the right variable: art. 25.1.a TRLIRNR turns on the owner's COUNTRY OF TAX RESIDENCE, not nationality. An owner tax-resident in the Netherlands, Belgium or Germany gets 19% on net; an owner tax-resident in the UK gets 24% on gross — but a British national tax-resident in Germany gets 19%, and a Dutch national tax-resident in the UK gets 24%.

entries.locator: Art. 25.1.a): 'Con carácter general el 24 por 100. No obstante, el tipo de gravamen será el 19 por ciento cuando se trate de contribuyentes residentes en otro Estado miembro de la Unión Europea o del Espacio Económico Europeo con el que exista un efectivo intercambio de información tributaria'. entries.final_wording: Do not imply that two clients face the same rate without checking the right variable: art. 25.1.a TRLIRNR turns on the owner's COUNTRY OF TAX RESIDENCE, not nationality. An owner tax-resident in the Netherlands, Belgium or Germany gets 19% on net; an owner tax-resident in the UK gets 24% on gross — but a British national tax-resident in Germany gets 19%, and a Dutch national tax-resident in the UK gets 24%.
entries.note: The load-bearing point — the rate turns on the state of tax residence, never on nationality — is exactly what art. 25.1.a) says, and the four worked examples follow correctly from it. Two riders for whoever writes from this: the 19% is EU or EEA-with-effective-exchange-of-information, so a Norwegian-resident owner is in the 19% group too (see the EEA point that is settled elsewhere in this project); and the 'on gross' half of the UK example is the statutory position now under challenge after the Audiencia Nacional's 28 July 2025 judgment (gid 167), so it should be written as the rule as it stands, not as a permanent fact.

entries.final_wording: Current Alicante-province price series, with the series type named each time: Registradores ERI 2T 2026 (registration-based average price of registered dwellings) publishes TWO Alicante figures that must never be mixed — 2.267 €/m² on the quarterly table, which carries +2,4% quarter on quarter, and 2.194 €/m² on the annual table, which carries +11,7% year on year; MIVAU publishes an appraisal-based €/m² (valor tasado) down to municipalities over 25,000 inhabitants, and separately a notarial (ANCERT) transaction statistic covering number and value of transfers at national, CCAA, province and municipality level; Tinsa is a PRIVATE appraisal-value index, not official statistics. Do NOT cite INE's Índice de Precios de Vivienda for Alicante — the IPV is published only for Spain and the comunidades autónomas, with no provincial breakdown. 'Costa Blanca' is not a statistical unit in any of them, but the province is NOT the finest official geography: the ERI also publishes provincial capitals, MIVAU's valor tasado reaches municipalities over 25,000 inhabitants, and the Consejo General del Notariado's portal reaches postcode level.
entries.note: Two errors, both material. First, the number is mis-paired: 2.267 €/m² is the ERI's quarterly figure and its own rate is +2,4% quarter on quarter; the +11,7% year-on-year rate belongs to the annual figure of 2.194 €/m². As written the instruction would have a writer publish a price and a growth rate that come from different tables — the single most damaging kind of statistics error, because both halves are individually true. Second, 'the finest official geography here is the province' is wrong and would suppress real, better-targeted data: the ERI gives provincial capitals, MIVAU's appraisal series covers municipalities over 25,000 inhabitants (which is most of the Costa Blanca's towns), and the Notariado's portal reaches postcode. The claim that INE's IPV has no provincial breakdown is correct and I have left it standing. Reference period Q2 2026, published August 2026; these figures are superseded quarterly.

entries.final_wording: Decreto 98/2022 (DOGV nº 9405, 16 August 2022; in force 16 October 2022) puts the disclosure duty in ARTICLE 3, not in a separate disclosure article: the agent must state the guarantee/insurance policy details in the contrato de mandato or nota de encargo signed with the client, AND must supply them to anyone who asks. Art. 4.1 makes the register itself public, free of charge and obligatory. Critically, the FIXED MINIMUM amounts of aval and professional liability insurance set in art. 3 were annulled by the TSJCV on 13 December 2024 (CNMC appeal), so the duty to disclose the cover survives but no statutory minimum figure may be quoted as current. Art. 3 c 2.2 obliges the agent to give the policy number and insurer name (or aval number and financial entity) to anyone who asks, buyers included.
entries.note: Every structural claim checks out against the DOGV text itself: publication 16 August 2022 (DOGV nº 9405), entry into force two months later on 16 October 2022, the disclosure duty sitting inside art. 3 rather than in a dedicated article, art. 4.1's 'público, gratuito y obligatorio' register, and art. 3.c).2.2's duty to hand the policy or aval number and the insurer or bank name to anyone who asks and to record it in the mandate. The TSJCV annulment of the fixed minimums on 13 December 2024 on the CNMC's appeal is confirmed by the CGPJ's own press note (the sentence number 706/2024 comes from legal databases, not from the CGPJ note). I closed the unclosed parenthesis and removed the stray internal cross-reference 'see id 434'; nothing substantive changed. The practical point survives intact and is the useful one: the duty to disclose the cover is alive, the minimum figures are not.

entries.final_wording: What must not be published: anything identifying a real client or counterparty, and anything that reads as an admission of professional negligence rather than a service failure
entries.note: A prohibition, not a claim about the world, and correct on both limbs. Identifying a client or counterparty in a published post is a personal-data disclosure with no lawful basis. The second limb is sharper than it looks in this specific regulatory setting: Decreto 98/2022 art. 3.c) requires Valencian agents to carry professional liability cover for 'negligencia profesional', so a published admission phrased as negligence is an admission against the very risk the policy insures, and could bear on cover and on liability. Distinguishing a service failure from professional negligence is the correct line to hold.

entries.final_wording: Before publishing any guarantee, insurance or qualification requirement, confirm the current post-TSJCV 706/2024 position from CENDOJ and DOGV, and whether an appeal or replacement regulation has changed it. Do not reuse the annulled fixed minimum figures unless current law has reintroduced them.
entries.note: A method rule, so not a sourced fact — but I applied it rather than just endorsing it. As of today: the 13 December 2024 judgment stands, I found no replacement decree or DOGV amendment reintroducing the minimum aval or professional liability figures, and no reported Tribunal Supremo cassation outcome. The rule's scope is also slightly wider than it says — the same judgment annulled two non-financial requirements (the reporting duty on non-habitual unpaid intermediaries, and the equivalent-register proof for agents established elsewhere), so the check should cover those too. The sentence number 706/2024 comes from legal databases; the CGPJ note gives the date, chamber and content but not the number.

freshness.source_locator: CGPJ: TSJCV Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo, Sección Cuarta, judgment of 13 December 2024 (notified 17 January 2025), partially upholding the CNMC's challenge; annulled the aval/seguro de caución minimums and the professional liability insurance minimums, plus the duty on non-habitual unpaid intermediaries to report after two services in 12 months and the requirement on agents established outside the Comunitat Valenciana to prove registration in an equivalent register; appealable in cassation to the Tribunal Supremo.

entries.assertion: Realistic renovation and reform costs on the Costa Blanca, plus the purchase costs a buyer must hold back (ITP or IVA plus AJD, notary, registry, legal fees) — because these are what actually shrink the buying budget
entries.source_required: see source_class
entries.source_opened: Instituto Valenciano de la Edificación (IVE), Base de Datos de Construcción / Costes de construcción, https://www.five.es/costes-de-construccion/ and https://productos.five.es/producto/base-de-datos-de-construccion
entries.locator: IVE (foundation promoted by the Generalitat Valenciana) publishes the Base de Datos de Construcción, 2026 edition, giving unit construction prices and the Módulo Básico de Edificación (€/m² of material execution cost); free item-by-item viewer, full BC3 file by paid subscription. No publisher of official statistics issues a renovation-cost series for the Costa Blanca or for any Alicante geography.
entries.final_wording: Purchase costs a buyer must hold back are law-verifiable and must be given by named component: on a resale, ITP at the Comunitat Valenciana rate in force (10% to 31 May 2026, 9% from 1 June 2026); on a new build, 10% IVA plus AJD (1.5% to 31 May 2026, 1.4% from 1 June 2026); plus notary and land-registry fees and legal fees. Renovation and reform costs are a different kind of claim and must not be handled the same way: no official statistic publishes 'realistic reform costs on the Costa Blanca'. The nearest Generalitat-backed reference is the IVE's Base de Datos de Construcción (unit construction prices and a €/m² execution-cost module, full base by subscription), which is a construction-price reference, not a record of what buyers actually pay. Any reform figure must come from real quotes supplied by the agency or a named contractor, must be labelled as such, and must never be presented as an official statistic.
entries.note: The instruction bundles two claims of different evidential status and would have a writer treat them alike. The purchase-cost half is fine and fully verifiable from primary tax law. The renovation half has no source of the required authority: I looked, and no official statistics publisher issues a reform-cost series for the Costa Blanca or for Alicante province. The closest thing is the IVE's construction price base, which is a costing tool for professionals, is largely behind a subscription, and measures execution cost rather than what a buyer is quoted — so citing it as 'realistic Costa Blanca reform costs' would be a category error. The correction keeps the useful instruction and blocks the invented €/m² figure that the original wording invites.
